Noticeably cautious and evasive on the timing of the large pending awards (GPRA 5, MAHAPREIT, Supertech, J&K), attributing delays to government approvals, Cabinet processes and state government working speed, and giving no firm dates beyond quarter-level estimates.

534392|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% to INR486 crore and EBITDA reached INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton), with PAT at INR41 crore.
534392|2026-06.overview: Sales volume was 59,000 tons, up 6.5% YoY, with revenue up 12% on higher volumes and OEM price revisions tied to input cost increases. EBITDA was INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton, management says excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds, the figure is near INR10,700/ton), and PAT was INR41 crore versus INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore a year ago. Management said demand exceeds what it can supply, the 3 lakh ton licensed capacity is the binding constraint, and it has applied for an increase to 3.6 lakh tons. Forging project with Aichi Steel is tracking on schedule with capex now below the INR475 crore estimate, and the greenfield 5 lakh ton plant scope and cost are being revised upward.

financial_highlights.value: INR10,760/ton (INR10,700 excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Automotive steel (core)
segments.commentary: Volumes were good and prices were revised upward on cost pass-through; Q1 settlement is complete with some OEMs and pending with others, where the price is expected to rise further. Maruti is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Direct exports are about 6-7% of sales and indirect exports via the Aichi trading arm about 5%; management guides total exports to 7-8% (max about 10%), with Aichi roughly 40-50% of exports.

segments.name: Non-automotive / die steel (planned)
segments.commentary: Ingot casting is due in Q3 FY27 and to stabilise in Q4; die steel production is expected to be regular in FY28. Die steel imports into India are about INR1,000 crore a year, and die steel sells at about INR2.5 lakh/ton (non-ESR) versus average realisation of about INR85,000/ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 255,000 tons; FY28 target above 270,000 tons, rising to about 290,000 tons if the environmental approval for 3.6 lakh tons comes through, and 330,000-340,000 tons in FY28-29 with new capex.
EBITDA/ton range is INR8,000-11,000 currently; management intends to move to INR8,000-12,000 for next year and to INR9,000-12,000 after the new solar plant and value-added products ramp up (FY28-29).
Q2 FY27 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase request; Q3 is expected broadly flat to slightly up or down depending on raw material prices.
Rolling mill has reached 3 lakh tons input capacity and is expected to reach 330,000 tons of input, about 10% higher, within the current licence constraint.
Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.
New reheating furnace has stabilised; new NDT (testing) line and new peeling line to be commissioned September-October 2026 to remove bottlenecks and reduce job work.
Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.
Price revisions follow raw material cost changes; OEMs can reverse or move prices, and the company operates within a band.
Non-auto product mix is a planned margin lever; die steel is high-price, low-volume and carries higher heat-treatment cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from exports, and how is business concentrated by customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exports are about 6-7% and indirect exports via Aichi's trading arm about 5%; Maruti is about 10% of sales, and management says there is no concentration risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

risks_watch: Licence cap at 3 lakh tons constrains volume; the 3.6 lakh ton EC approval is pending and not assured.
Pending OEM price settlements for Q1 and Q2 realisations depend on OEM acceptance and raw material costs.
Greenfield project cost is rising (metals inflation, rupee depreciation, added testing lines), and the refined project and cost are due in the next Board meeting and next quarter.
Solar savings in the next phase will be lower because of local cell rules, which affects the planned EBITDA/ton uplift.
The reported EBITDA of INR68 crore includes treasury income from surplus Aichi funds; management excluded it to get INR10,700/ton, so the operating figure should be tracked separately.
Direct export share was over-estimated earlier; the company will start estimating indirect component exports from next quarter.
534392|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the Aichi forging project, with clear timelines and cost savings; more cautious and hedged on the EC approval, greenfield plant cost, and pricing, which management repeatedly says will happen "when it happens".
key_quotes: We closed a good quarter.
Demand scenario is good. We are, in fact, finding it difficult to meet the requirements of the customers.
But -- and cost per ton is going to be lower than what we had estimated in the new plant.
So, the new plant is 5 lakh tons, not 5 million.

534425|2026-03.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q4 FY26 revenue up 13.65% YoY and PAT up 44.20%, with SSG of 2.25% for the quarter and 11.57% in April.
534425|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 13.65% YoY and PAT growth of 44.20%, helped by 2.25% same-store sales growth and gross margin expansion from 69.1% to 70.4%. Full-year SSG was 1.49%, and April SSG reached 11.57%, which management attributed to higher dine-in covers and refurbishments of older restaurants. Management guided to about 15% top-line growth in FY27 and about 15-16% EBITDA growth on revenue, with 32 new outlets planned. On the cost side, the company took a 4% price increase and moved 78% of its kitchens off LPG/PNG to induction, targeting 100% within 20 days.

financial_highlights.metric: Profit after tax growth (Q4 FY26, YoY)

segments.name: Mainland China / Asia Kitchen / Gong (Asian brands)
segments.commentary: Mainland China AOV is INR 1,200-1,300 per cover; Asia Kitchen INR 1,000-1,100; Gong INR 2,500-3,000, with a Bandra launch and Pune and Delhi (Vasant Kunj) openings planned. Management sees Asia Kitchen and Mainland China reaching about 50 restaurants within 5 years.

segments.name: Haka (digital QSR, delivery-first)
segments.commentary: Haka operates from hybrid sites, with about 40-50% of new Mainland China stores co-locating a Haka and Oh! Calcutta cloud kitchen. Management expects Haka to reach a 'decent number' within two quarters; no figure was given.

segments.name: Walters and Sweet Bengal
segments.commentary: Walters AOV is about INR 700 and Sweet Bengal about INR 400 per cover. Plans include 15 new Walters (to 20 total) and 10 new Sweet Bengal outlets in FY27, with Sweet Bengal rebranding and FMCG packaging planned.

segments.name: Siciliana (Italian)
segments.commentary: Newer chain; management cited an average spend of about INR 1,200-1,300 per cover, equal to Mainland China, per the answer on Siciliana's pricing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 15%, implying revenue near INR 600 crores; management said 'maybe more' and suggested about INR 700 crores by FY28 at a slower pace.
EBITDA to grow about 15-16% for each percentage of revenue growth, as front-end costs of new restaurants weigh over the next 2 years.
Restaurant-level EBITDA of about 15% post-rent (22% pre-rent) for a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store generating INR 8-9 crores revenue; breakeven in 4-6 months.
FY27 capex of INR 40 crores for renovations and new stores; 8 new restaurants (INR 32 crores) and QSR/confectionery (about INR 5 crores) for a total of INR 37 crores.
Planned 32 new outlets in FY26-27 (8 restaurants, 15 Walters, 10 Sweet Bengal), taking touch points from 121 at 31 March to about 150 by year-end.
Management expects double-digit SSG going forward after renovations of older restaurants.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of INR 40 crores for renovations and new store openings; INR 37 crores is earmarked for 8 new restaurants and QSR/confectionery.
Restaurant capex of INR 12,000-13,000 per sq ft for Mainland China and Asia Kitchen; lower for small Walters and Sweet Bengal stores.
Renovations started at Andheri West, then Pune and Bangalore; about 4 restaurants refreshed by April.
Walters commissary set up in Maharashtra, geared for 20-25 stores.
Induction conversion: about INR 1.12 crores spent on induction woks since 4 March; 78% of the restaurant chain off LPG/PNG, with 100% targeted within 20 days.
Average occupancy is about 2 times installed cover capacity on an average basis, according to management.
demand_pricing: April 2026 SSG of 11.57%; management said there was no sign of consumer slowdown as of late May, citing a planned redemption-coupon scheme (for example INR 200 or INR 150 off a INR 1,000 meal) launching at the end of May.
Price increase of 4% taken in FY26, with management stating it would not take more than 4% and is not seeking extra margin from price.
Management said there is no significant reduction in spend historically during high inflation or domestic shocks other than COVID, and none currently.
Franchisees: 11 earlier, 7 remaining, each paying 6% of revenue as royalty with no capex by the company; management said Indian partners need 'skin in the game'.
Competition: management sees Panda Express as a fast QSR format different from Mainland China, so no threat to the business.

qa_highlights.question: What were same-store sales growth for Q4 and FY26, and why is the company lagging peers like Barbeque Nation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 SSG was 2.25% and full-year FY26 was 1.49%. Management said April SSG was 11.57%, driven by more dine-in covers, and blamed slow growth on unrenovated restaurants, with refurbishments now under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the restaurant-level economics for top brands?
qa_highlights.answer: For a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store, revenue is INR 8-9 crores a year with 22% restaurant EBITDA before rent. Rent is about 20-21% of revenue (revenue-share triggers at 17-18%), leaving about 15% post-rent EBITDA. Breakeven takes 4-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing LPG and fuel supply, and what does induction cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company started the transition on 4 March and imported wok-based induction sets (around 300). It has 78% of the chain off fuel, targeting 100% in 20 days. Management said induction cost is the same or lower, with a 6% saving in a pilot restaurant from avoiding pilot-flame wastage.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on fewer brands, given that the bottom 8 brands contribute under 10% each?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed seven focus brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters, Sweet Bengal). Other brands are profitable and will not be shut, but no further expansion is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration, given the cash pile and the share price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the question would be taken up by the Board and it was too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY26 cash flow (about INR 80 crores CFO less about INR 50 crores rent) reconcile with a 15% EBITDA margin claim?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 15-16% figure is at restaurant level after rent. Cash-flow EBITDA is after corporate costs, which fell to about 4% of revenue from 6-7% as the company resumed expansion.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (fuel, energy, freight) with only a 4% price increase taken so far; management said it is not seeking extra margin from pricing.
Consumer wallet pressure on discretionary dining if inflation or geopolitical uncertainty deepens; management reports no current impact.
Same-store sales growth of 1.49% in FY26 is weak; the 11.57% April figure needs to be sustained through FY27.
Execution risk on 32 new outlets, Gong expansion in Pune and Delhi, and Haka scaling.
Corporate cost and new-store front-end costs may slow EBITDA growth to about 15-16% against revenue growth of about 15%.
Management's FY27 revenue of about INR 600 crores and FY28 of about INR 700 crores are forward-looking and dependent on macro conditions.
Gross margin and EBITDA reconciliation: an analyst said cash-flow-implied EBITDA margin was about 7-8%, against management's 15-16% restaurant-level figure; this gap was not fully resolved.

The leader holds the price line. So we continue to believe in that right from the beginning, and we've not taken more than 4% at this point.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cross INR600 crore in revenue with about 15 new stores?

qa_highlights.question: How was margin expanded despite cost pressure, including gas shortages?

qa_highlights.question: Is the delivery mix growth deliberate, and does it hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is driven by consumer demand and new formats, not a deliberate push. Dine-in grew from INR 71 crore to INR 81 crore; AOV is claimed to be among the highest in dine-in brands.

qa_highlights.question: How many stores are planned, and what are the constraints?

535754|2026-03.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

financial_highlights.metric: Premium cement share of trade sales

financial_highlights.change: up ~INR1 vs Dec quarter; down vs ~INR255 last year

segments.name: Sanghi Industries (acquired)
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% in FY27. Rail link at Naliya is an add-on, not in base case; seven marine vessels ordered for delivery from next year.

segments.name: Penna Cement (acquired)
segments.commentary: Utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% in FY27. Breakdowns and deferred maintenance cited; Sanghi and Penna together hold 19 Mt capacity, with a 5-10% utilization uplift targeted.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management says Orient is running at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Ambuja and ACC existing assets
segments.commentary: Management expects 75-80% utilization in FY27; consolidated utilization estimated at 70-75%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume guided at ~80 Mt, about 8% growth, versus industry growth of 5-5.5%.
FY27 cost reduction of INR250/t on a full-year average; cost peak of ~INR4,500/t in Q4, Q1 FY27 seen flattish, with savings accelerating over the remaining three quarters.
Minimum cost reduction of INR250/t in FY27 and another INR250/t in FY28 (INR500 cumulative); management says the earlier INR3,650/t target is not abandoned.

Capacity to reach ~119 Mt by end FY27 after ~10 Mt of additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window); FY28 target capacity slips toward FY30; Maratha adds 4 Mt clinker; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) follow in about 24-28 months.
FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crore; project IRR hurdle of 18% stated.
Management did not give EBITDA/t guidance; said it is too early to estimate given volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end after 10.7 Mt grinding and 7 Mt clinker added (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, Jodhpur, Bhatapara).
Clinker capacity 69 Mt now, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).
About INR4,000 crore of capex already under execution (capacity, WHRS, fly ash transport); balance is debottlenecking and maintenance.

Recalibrating growth capex: shutting some grinding units in North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat and Maharashtra to move them closer to markets; a Bihar grinding unit planned; Dahej Line 2 as clinker-plus-cement example.
Management paused new projects until current ones are completed; engineering to be finalized over next 6 months.
demand_pricing: Industry price rise in March quarter was about INR10/bag, INR15-20 only in selected pockets; management says industry cannot pass on costs under relentless pricing pressure.
April-May demand described as subdued and soft; management would be happy if industry recovers half of a price hike.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was muted (Orient-adjusted flat YoY per an analyst); packing bag shortages linked to West Asia conflict cost volume in March.
Premium cement gap versus base product INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium; price gap with the number-one player is INR5-10 in some districts.
Management expects FY27 demand to be soft due to inflation and weak monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 cost about INR4,500/t when management earlier pointed to an INR4,000 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for the March exit; March averaged ~INR4,100 normalized, with INR250 escalation from West Asia. Causes cited: branding, repairs at acquired plants, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, and lower government incentives.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost reduction is assumed for FY27 after Q4 inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,500 is the peak; a INR250/t reduction gives ~INR4,250/t for FY27 on a full-year average, with Q1 FY27 flat at ~INR4,500.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,650/t cost target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned; INR500/t cumulative over two years is the committed minimum, with further runway to the earlier target.

qa_highlights.question: Why the reset in capacity and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said performance fell short of commitments, citing cost, wrong contractor choice, projects started without full engineering, and breakdowns at Penna and Sanghi; ~80% of the five KPIs relate to cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a target IRR for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani stated a project IRR of 18%, all equity-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of high working capital and negative ACC operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinod Bahety said ACC has MSA receivables from Ambuja that will be settled via an ICD after shareholder approval; Ambuja's core working capital fell to 20 days from 30 days.

risks_watch: Cost trajectory: whether Q1 FY27 holds near INR4,500/t and the INR250/t FY27 reduction is delivered.
Acquired-asset utilization at Sanghi (57%) and Penna (46%) and reliability of Penna and Sanghi plants.
Pricing power in a soft demand environment; April-May trend described as subdued.
Capex execution delays (Maratha, Chhattisgarh) and capex recalibration; 10 Mt commissioning between now and September.
Non-core working capital, MSA receivables from ACC, and negative ACC operating cash flow, to be resolved via ICD.
Reduced government incentives after GST rate cuts and changed accrual policy.
535754|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on execution, with management admitting missed targets and a partial reset in timelines. Confident on controllable cost levers, but evasive on EBITDA/t guidance and on pricing outlook, which they called soft.
key_quotes: Therefore, I strongly believe INR150 to INR200 savings will come from these components.
So we are not shying away from our target.
So we'll be honest with you. Yes, partially, there is a reset.
Yes, we are moving away from the time line.
But I think any guidance on EBITDA will be difficult at this stage.

535754|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 331 bps to 16.7% and net cost down INR206/t to INR4,241/t, while total volumes fell (trade -2%, non-trade -21% YoY).
535754|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a value-over-volume quarter: trade share rose to 78% from 74%, and operating EBITDA reached INR1,589 crore on revenue of about INR9,500 crore. Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management said absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost inflation. Volumes declined, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21% YoY, and management attributed the quarter's weakness to diesel shortages, packing material issues and deliberate exits from low-margin South volumes. Management guided to 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY, and reiterated INR4,250/t full-year cost guidance.

financial_highlights.change: down INR206/t QoQ; from INR4,447/t in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated cost base cited by analyst

segments.name: Trade / non-trade
segments.commentary: Trade share rose to 78% from 74% QoQ; premium products are 34% of trade sales. Trade volumes -2% YoY, non-trade -21% YoY.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Trade volumes grew 2% YoY; management calls it the highest-EBITDA cluster. Roughly 25% of volume mix.

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Trade and non-trade both grew positively per management; about 30% of volume mix.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Trade volumes sustained with healthy margins; about 25% of volume mix.

segments.name: Central
segments.commentary: Volumes deliberately reduced; blended cement push lifted margins. About 10% of volume mix.

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Highest YoY degrowth as about 1 million tonnes of low or negative EBITDA volume were cut; about 10% of volume mix. Channel build-out expected to take one to two quarters.

segments.commentary: About 45 crore units of RE power sold in Q1 for roughly INR140 crore revenue (vs 24 crore units / ~INR70 crore in Q4); fly ash sales about INR15 crore in Q1 vs ~INR50 crore in Q4. Both are netted in operating cost per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 8%; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY. Trade share guided to remain above 75%.
Full-year FY27 net cost target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below (about INR250/t further reduction).

Identified cost levers worth INR130-150/t: about INR35/t lead distance cut (15 km), INR30/t from raw material logistics and fly ash sourcing, INR50/t from energy (heat rate, power units, 75 MW new RE), and INR10-15/t other headroom.
Q2 FY27 net cost guided to be slightly better than June-quarter levels, after absorbing potential geopolitical cost rise of about INR100/t.
Capex FY27 about INR6,500 crore; Q1 spend about INR1,500-1,600 crore. FY28 capex similar at INR6,000-7,000 crore on a run-rate basis.
Installed capacity to reach 119 Mtpa by end-FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt); 8-10 Mtpa of organic additions planned each year thereafter.
Long-term capacity utilisation target 70-75% on a value-focused basis; green power share to reach 60% by FY28 (48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis).
capex_capacity: Trial runs started at Dahej (1.2 Mt expansion); Salai Banwa (UP, 2.4 Mt) started; Bhatinda (Punjab, 1.2 Mt) and Jodhpur (Penna, 2 Mt cement / 3 Mt clinker) commissioned or stabilising, with Jodhpur clinker supplying grinding units from Q2.
Kalamboli (Mumbai, 1 Mt) and Warisaliganj (Bihar, 2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 FY27 (Warisaliganj most likely September).
Maratha clinker line (4 Mt) now expected Q1 FY28; Mundra expected 18-24 months out (around 2029).
RE capacity 973-975 MW (of 1,122 MW target; about 150 MW remaining); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW.
Three coal blocks in focus; first expected to be operational in about 30 months. AFR (alternative fuel) substitution at about 7%, targeted at 10-15% in FY27.
Sanghi: about INR600 crore jetty expansion for clinker. Penna: INR100-150 crore for AFR and WHRS. About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily closed for around six months.
demand_pricing: Management says cement demand was stable across infrastructure, housing and construction; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY.
Q1 headwinds: diesel availability, packing material shortages and logistics disruption in West and East. Logistics lead distance fell from 269 km to 249 km YoY, yet freight per tonne was flat.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed the gap to Incoterm and channel-cost netting. Analyst comparison put Q1 NSP about INR100/t below UltraTech's reported NSP.
Blended cement share 85%; clinker factor down about 3% to 64%.
Q2 FY27 cost pressure expected from geopolitical escalation (West Asia, fuel).

qa_highlights.question: Is it fair to expect muted FY27 volume growth if the value-over-volume strategy holds, given Q1 volume loss and earlier ~80 Mt chase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY; non-trade is a 'well calculated' reduction, with market share said to have held or improved only on trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will green power be consumed in-house, and what is the incremental benefit as captive use rises versus selling power?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; roughly 50% (about 20 crore units) expected to be consumed in Q2. Green power share is 34% on consumption basis, 48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis, targeted at 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus the cost of captive green power, and sales are capped at around 10% of output.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 FY27 net cost rise given inventory buffers, and what is the full-year cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 net cost expected to be broadly in line with or slightly better than the June quarter, after absorbing a potential geopolitical rise of about INR100/t. FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below. Clinker inventory about one month, coal about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade volumes still decline YoY, and how did the regions perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by diesel shortages, packing material issues and logistics disruption. North trade +2% YoY, West grew in trade and non-trade, East sustained, South cut about 1 Mt of low or negative EBITDA volume, Central degrew on blended-cement shift. Capacity utilisation 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the INR206/t sequential cost reduction come from, and what was the gross saving after West Asia cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to fly ash sourcing, RE power price per unit, clinker factor down about 2-3%, marginal logistics gains (INR10/t), and fixed cost optimisation. Management said the INR206/t saving absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia cost, implying gross savings of about INR316/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NSP down about INR100/t versus UltraTech's reported NSP, and what are the Incoterm and netting effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSP is netted for certain channel and Incoterm costs (ex-works terms), and that channel investment is being expensed against NSP. It did not quantify the gap and said NSP is market-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company keeping plants temporarily closed and treating non-trade differently at acquired assets?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 Mt of old ACC and one acquired-company facility temporarily closed for around six months; management said these are not permanent closures. Karan Adani said non-trade volumes at acquired assets were largely at negative or marginal EBITDA, so the company is prioritising value over volume.

risks_watch: Whether July's 8% trade volume growth holds and whether non-trade volume decline (-21% YoY in Q1) stabilises, given guidance needs roughly 12-13% growth in the remaining nine months.
Geopolitical and fuel cost pressure in Q2 (about INR100/t potential rise) versus the INR130-150/t cost-lever pipeline and the INR4,250/t full-year target.
Execution risk on capacity: Kalamboli and Warisaliganj (Q2 FY27), Maratha clinker slipped to Q1 FY28, Mundra around 2029, and 8-10 Mtpa annual additions thereafter.

Reconciliation gap: management did not provide a breakdown of cement vs RMC vs power vs fly ash cost, and deferred several analyst requests (fly ash/power cumulative P&L, RMC margin drop to about 7%, fixed cost bridge) to offline follow-up.

Accounting items to monitor: O&M cost equalisation across quarters still under discussion with auditors; INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item (VRS in South); depreciation true-up after Sanghi and Penna merger.
Green power transition: grid connectivity for some cement plants expected in two to three quarters, and green power share target of 60% by FY28 depends on consumption rising from about 50% of sales.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR 206 PMT from the previous quarter.
So the operating company, Ambuja has no debt.
535754|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and assertive on cost and volume recovery, repeatedly citing July trade volumes and the INR4,250/t target, but was evasive or deferred on several specifics: NSP gap versus UltraTech, RMC margin decline, cost breakdown across cement, RMC, power and fly ash, and parent-level debt and ICDs.

535755|2026-03.headline: ABFRL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore; Pantaloons grew 19% and reported loss narrowed to INR164 crore.
535755|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% YoY to INR1,990 crore, with Pantaloons up 19% (17% core format) and TMRW up 45%. Excluding a INR97 crore one-time demerger gain in the base quarter and an INR83 crore non-cash derivative gain at WROGN (TMRW associate), management said EBITDA grew 29% YoY at an 11.5% margin. Reported loss was INR164 crore versus INR171 crore a year earlier, and PAT loss narrowed to INR235 crore on an adjusted basis from INR289 crore. Management flagged a weaker wedding calendar, a marginal March slowdown from geopolitical disruption, and 3-4% raw material inflation with 5-8% price increases under evaluation for H2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 17% Pantaloons core format growth, and how much was EOSS timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the EOSS shift to January, merchandise resets in three categories (over 20% growth each in Q4), record sell-through, and new large-format stores. It said Nov-Mar like-to-like growth was about 7%, with total growth about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the store addition guidance not accelerating despite strong LTL?

qa_highlights.question: What is the OWND profitability and why are its store additions slower than Pantaloons?

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and pricing outlook?

535755|2026-06.headline: ABFRL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR2,026 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% and reported loss widened to INR249 crores.

538567|2026-03.headline: Gulf Oil Q4 FY26 posted record quarter: 45,000 KL lubricant volume (+14%), EBITDA INR 135 crore, FY26 revenue above INR 4,000 crore.
538567|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly volume, revenue and EBITDA for Q4 FY26, with lubricant volume up about 14% and revenue up about 14%. The Board recommended a record FY26 dividend of INR 51 per share, including a INR 30 final.

Yard extensions planned at Garhi and Piyala at about 70% to 80% utilisation; land bank can support up to 4x current ICD volume.
demand_pricing: West Asia conflict continues to subdue volumes; April trend similar to March (within range, not materially worse). Recovery timing unclear and tied to Iran-US resolution.
Warehousing pricing is positive: price increases passed through (including Haryana wage law changes) and management will seek price hikes at each contract renewal.

Snowman market position: about 160,000 pallets capacity versus about 80,000 for the second organised player; Snowman about 3% to 4% of total market including unorganised capacity. Management stopped giving region-wise market share.
Potential LCL and time-sensitive cargo opportunity post DFC: 6,000 to 10,000 TEUs per month within NCR, but nothing happening now and JNPT double-stack operations still pending by a couple of months.
Domestic business is lower-margin on revenue and EBITDA per TEU; management expects overall EBITDA to grow even as per-TEU metrics fall.

qa_highlights.question: Current trend in volumes after West Asia impact, and which commodities are affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes remain subdued with no clarity on recovery. Imports from US, Europe and Middle East and food, rice and frozen exports were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 12% to 13% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix of headcount additions ahead of Ankleshwar and domestic scale-up, plus retention bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Snowman gross and EBITDA margins fall and COGS rise about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Start-up warehouse costs (Kolkata, Krishnapatnam), DG power costs, stabling and empty haulage costs, upfront domestic costs, and one-time 5PL import procurement. Management said COGS relates to trading, which grew 23%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex in FY26 and FY27 guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt trajectory and use of cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt to keep declining; capex plans (rakes, EVs, solar, reach stackers, warehouses, Indore and Jaipur) absorb cash; dividends to continue; no near-term stake increase in Snowman.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15% rail growth achievable given historical 4% to 5% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rail grew about 10% last year, exceeding market growth, and cited new ICDs (Ankleshwar, Indore, Jaipur) and domestic volumes as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transport segment worth keeping versus outsourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Owns about 250 to 260 vehicles and leases about 200; plans to add vehicles; a transport management system going live within about a month for trip-level profitability tracking.

risks_watch: Prolonged West Asia disruption affecting import and export volumes; April trend similar to March.

Snowman INR1,000 crore revenue target could slip to FY29; per-TEU realisations and EBITDA trending lower as domestic mix rises.
Jaipur ICD legal outcome at the July hearing; Indore ICD timeline to 2028.
JNPT DFC last-stretch completion and double-stack readiness; timing of any volume shift still open.
Cash flow visibility: management agreed to consider a cash flow reporting format (lease rentals below EBITDA) from next quarter.
Transport segment remains under stress; TMS rollout to drive lane-level decisions.
Tax: MAT credit to shield cash tax for about 3 to 4 years, but ATI tax benefit lost.

key_quotes: So, volumes remain a bit subdued, and there's no clarity also on when things will pick up exactly. So, it's a wait-and-watch kind of situation.
INR1,000 crores is still our plan. Maybe it gets deferred by a year or so.

538635|2026-06.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.
538635|2026-06.overview: Joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics call covering Q1 FY27. Management attributed the volume softness to the West Asia conflict (since April), which cut imports sharply in April-May, and to July weather disruptions at ports; market share is described as intact while the underlying market has de-grown. Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. Management reported no specific Q1 financial figures in the call.

financial_highlights.change: reached after special dividend paid earlier this year
about 95% are customs bonds to government authorities

segments.name: Gateway ICD / rail
segments.commentary: Market share intact but market de-grew in operating regions; JNPT exposure about 5% of rail volume. Rail EBITDA per TEU fell on lower double-stacking, higher empty running and underframe usage, and wage and fuel costs.

segments.name: Snowman warehousing
segments.commentary: Pricing up 5-7% on average; about 24,000 additional pallets expected by end of FY27 (Pune first, then Patna).

segments.name: Snowman 5PL
segments.commentary: Service margin typically 5-6%; no new 5PL customer added in Q1, with new names possibly by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway)
segments.commentary: Volumes improved and a pricing increase taken to offset fuel and wage hikes; margin uplift possible in Q2. Management is not actively pursuing a sale.

segments.name: Domestic transport (Snowman)
segments.commentary: Around 500 containers a month currently, with scope to scale as network expands.

guidance_outlook: Gateway expects to close FY27 with double-digit volume growth, conditional on the West Asia situation easing.
Snowman guided 10-15% top-line growth for the year, across all segments.
Ankleshwar ICD to start EXIM operations by end of September 2026 (Q2); current volume zero.

Snowman adding about 24,000 pallets by end of FY27, with Pune commissioning in a couple of months and Patna to follow; similar additions planned in subsequent years.

demand_pricing: West Asia conflict since April cut imports sharply in April-May; imports improved from June-July, but July volumes were hit by weather-related port and double-stacking restrictions at Mundra and JNPT.

Warehousing market shifting from unorganised to organised; competitive intensity described as ongoing, with CONCOR the largest rail competitor.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gateway's ICD market share holding given the stagnant volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share is intact and the market itself has de-graded due to the war; double-digit growth for the year is still expected once the situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: How much MAT credit supports the low cash tax rate, and when does full tax apply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kartik Aiyer said the company will pay at 18.88% for at least 7-8 years, using accumulated MAT credit; management noted cash tax rose only INR 1-2 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why has rail EBITDA per TEU weakened, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower import share, lower double-stacking, higher underframe and empty running, port imbalance at Mundra and Pipavav, and steep wage hikes (Haryana up 35%); recovery expected as volumes return, with fuel impact visible in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JNPT exposure and the economics of shifting to it?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is about 5% of rail volume; on current pricing it is more expensive for North-bound customers but yields higher revenue and slightly higher EBITDA per TEU for Gateway due to distance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CFS business and its land?
qa_highlights.answer: A sale was explored about 1.5 years ago without a satisfactory valuation; no active process now, though management is open to a good offer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value of the land bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a formal valuation; cited Garhi (85-90 acres) at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase, with total land of about 475 acres.

risks_watch: Duration of the West Asia conflict and its effect on import volumes and market size.
Port congestion and weather-driven restrictions at Mundra, Pipavav and JNPT affecting double-stacking.
Whether shipping lines actually shift volume to JNPT and whether railways grant JNPT haulage relief.
Rail EBITDA per TEU recovery in Q2 as fuel and wage pass-throughs take effect.
Jaipur ICD litigation outcome (final arguments in September 2026) and Indore/Ankleshwar commissioning timelines.
538635|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth but cautious near term: management repeatedly tied the double-digit recovery to the West Asia situation easing and avoided quantifying monthly trends or JNPT shift timing.

538666|2026-03.headline: Sharda Cropchem FY26 PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores on record revenue of INR 5,268 crores; FY27 revenue guided at 10-15%.
538666|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR 2,065 crores, with EBITDA up 75% to INR 513 crores and PAT up 57% to INR 319 crores. Gross margin expanded 750 bps to 37.3%, aided by a sharp rise in FX contribution (+11.7% in Q4). For FY26, revenue rose 22% to INR 5,268 crores, EBITDA rose 69% to INR 1,040 crores (19.7% margin), and PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores. The company remains debt-free with INR 702 crores of cash and liquid investments. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15%, gross margin around 35% plus or minus a few points, and EBITDA margin of 18-20%.

FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 18-20%.

Geopolitical risk (Middle East war, shipping routes, freight costs) and weather affecting NAFTA demand; NAFTA revenue declined about 6%.

Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. Management maintained FY27 guidance of 10-15% revenue growth and about 35% gross margin.

539083|2026-03.headline: Inox Wind Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue flat YoY at INR1,306 crore; FY27 guidance of ~75% revenue growth and 20%+ EBITDA margin.
539083|2026-03.overview: Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA of INR333 crore, PBT of INR216 crore, PAT of INR106 crore and cash profit of INR268 crore, with FY26 revenue of about INR4,500 crore against an earlier INR5,000 crore target. Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall QoQ from about INR78 crore to INR69 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarterly variation to value-added services timing (about INR8-9 crore) and said the annualised run-rate is the right measure.

539118|2026-03.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.

Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. Installed FMCG and FMCG-intermediate capacity rose to 20,840 tons per month after a 1,700 MT soap line was commissioned at Roorkee. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR900-1,000 crores and a ~6% profitability level, with a further 0.75-1% improvement in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores from operating cash flow plus debt headroom; BD cash deployment guided at INR600-1,000 crores in the year (land outflow INR600-900 crores per earlier answer).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Not today; management is considering it after a few years, starting with for-sale assets to test development before holding assets.

risks_watch: Revenue and margin are lumpy and dependent on OC timing, with some OCs lined up in Q4; the Q1 margin of about 48-49% is well above the 25% portfolio average.
Net debt to equity rising from prior level to 0.29x as BD accelerates; management's comfort threshold is 1:1.
Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.
Labour and construction cost inflation is gradual per management but may pressure margins.
Guidance inconsistency: BD cash deployment quoted as INR600-900 crores in one answer and INR600-1,000 crores in another.
539301|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and bookings, with explicit reiteration of FY27 guidance; more cautious and deliberately non-committal on revenue recognition timing and annual collections guidance.

financial_highlights.value: about 48-49% (as cited by analyst in Q&A)

financial_highlights.change: up from prior level, company comfort 1:1

key_quotes: We have started the year with a very strong Q1 with presales of INR432 crores, which is a 147% growth year-on-year.
The significant growth in the financial numbers is majorly driven by the BU received for Phase 1 of Orchards project in Bengaluru.
But at the same time, probably factor in a 25% EBITDA at this particular stage as a company average.

539302|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 2,121 crore, while FY26 order inflow of ~INR 7,210 crore missed the INR 10,000 crore target by about 28%.
539302|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 2,121 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 237 crore (+2% YoY, margin 11.17%) and PAT of INR 153 crore (+18%). FY26 revenue was INR 6,107 crore (+16%), EBITDA INR 750 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT INR 412 crore (+18%). Order inflow missed guidance after cancellation of a INR 1,563 crore BESS order by the West Bengal electricity department, and the water division faced certification delays. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, order inflow of about INR 12,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12.5%.

segments.name: Power vs non-power mix
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 57% power and 43% non-power; FY26 was 64% power and 36% non-power. Backlog is about 70% power and 30% non-power.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 94% domestic and 6% international; FY26 was 95% domestic and 5% international. International work is mainly O&M and manpower supply (Middle East, Nigeria), with international revenue of INR 327 crore in FY26 versus INR 292 crore in FY25.

segments.name: MDO (mining, KBP and SAIL/Tasra)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 MDO revenue was INR 226 crore, including INR 117 crore in March. Management targets INR 500 crore in FY27 and INR 1,250 crore in FY28, with EBITDA margin of about 15% now rising toward 20% at peak rated capacity (FY29-30).

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M is the highest-margin business at about 15-16% EBITDA. Management cites O&M order growth of about 8% and about 4,100 MW of O&M orders in FY26, including a INR 279 crore Mumbai Monorail/metro O&M contract.

segments.name: EPC / civil
segments.commentary: Construction margins are below 8-10%. The BOP EPC order for the 800 MW Singareni project from BHEL is about INR 2,550 crore. Electrical transmission work has ended and was moved into civil.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.
539302|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term power and O&M demand, but cautious on near-term order inflow and the water division. Management was explicit about the BESS cancellation and the MDO timing shortfall, and gave specific numbers on most questions. Some answers on segment figures and MDO revenue were revised during the call, which weakens the precision of the guidance.
key_quotes: Otherwise, our numbers would have been much better in order backlog.
Of course, on the BOP side, we are going to bid for two- three projects, that's worth INR 15000 crores.
We are confident of achieving that, and even the MDO business ramp -up of production is happening, and we are more focused on the high -margin O&M business.

539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a normal rate of 22-25% should be used, with deferred tax rising next year as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar are capitalised; the Q4 deferred tax charge of about Rs 4-4.5 crore related to land recognised as right-of-use assets for the Madhya Bharat project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall short of the 8% margin management had earlier signalled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would have been Rs 75-80 crore without the deferred tax charge and leasehold-land provisions, which brought it to Rs 70 crore for FY26 (about 7%).

risks_watch: Raw-material cost and supply: ammonia and sulphur prices have roughly tripled and remain volatile; management could not predict when they will ease.
Unit 5 and 6 start-up timing is unresolved; the Kharif season is lost and Rabi FY27 is the next opportunity.
Demand and fertiliser affordability at current prices; management said subsidy support is not yet adequate and noted a 10% government cap.
Q1 FY27 inventory-liquidation benefit is unquantified, and management declined to give numbers; also the Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap is unexplained on the call.
Deferred tax and effective tax rate will rise in FY27 as projects capitalise; a term loan may be used for the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat capex.
Governance and disclosure: management relied on the CFO for most figures and its tone on the call was unusually unstructured.
539334|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid but cautious, emphasising conservatism and a wait-and-see stance on Units 5 and 6 and on FY27 pricing. Its visibility was often hedged ("I can't read too far"), and it repeatedly deferred detailed numbers to the CFO or to later IR follow-up.
key_quotes: So, sir, let the market be matured. Let the market be accepting these new prices, which are almost three times of the raw material prices of our earlier.
Old numbers will never be seen again.
So we will definitely do Rs. 250 crores in that. Rs. 1000 crores and Rs. 250 crores.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 280.1 crore (CEO remarks) / Rs 281.1 crore (CFO remarks)
Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

key_quotes: I believe this year will be much better than the last two or three financial years for the company.
So, I believe Q2 will be even better than Q1.
No, sir, you don't expect 10%. I did not say 10%. I said that we will come to the level of 8.5 %- 9%. I hope so.
Honestly speaking, after these sulfur rates came, we put our acid plants on low load.
First, you need value, then volume.
539334|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on FY27 outlook and pricing, repeatedly calling the year much better than the last two or three. It was evasive on volume recovery and on the Q4-to-Q1 order-slippage question, answering by pointing to revenue and profit growth instead. It was cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up, saying it is taking a measured approach, and it declined to confirm the 10% PAT figure, reiterating 8.5-9%.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR790 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR8.90 per share (445% of face value); outgo about INR835 crore

financial_highlights.metric: CGD EBITDA per SCM (FY26, excluding amalgamation impact)

financial_highlights.value: Gas trading about INR400 crore; CGD about INR450 crore; E&P about INR14 crore; renewables about INR5 crore

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Total trading volume was 10.2 mmscmd in FY26, of which about 5.3 mmscmd was intersegment sales to CGD; net external volume was about 4.9 mmscmd, down about 19% from FY25. Management guided trading margins of 4-6% and said FY26 included a one-off of about INR200 crore linked to a Petronet LNG regasification liability, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

segments.name: City Gas Distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

segments.name: Exploration and production (E&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA was about INR29 crore, but the segment is loss-making after depreciation. Reserves are stated at 6.71 mmboe. FY27 E&P capex is about INR100 crore for planned drilling.

segments.name: Power (renewables / GSEG and GPPC gas-based plants)
segments.commentary: Plant load factors were about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. FY26 segment EBITDA was about INR46 crore (renewables, as stated), and the segment reported losses due to forex and impairment items of about INR15 crore and INR23 crore. The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

guidance_outlook: CGD margin guidance of about INR5-6 per SCM was given, with a target of about INR5.5-6.5 per SCM; management said trading margins will be maintained.
Morbi price is about INR75 per SCM (non-Morbi about INR68) per management; June was raised by about INR1.5. Management said Morbi demand can reach 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, about 10% above the current level.
FY27 capex guidance: about INR1,000 crore for CGD and about INR100 crore for E&P; no capex for trading.
Gas trading volume is expected to grow 25-30% by FY30-31 from the current 10-12 mmscmd, with prices seen as reasonable from FY28-29.
Tax: about INR1,900 crore of tax losses remain to be used, so no tax is expected on profits up to that amount; the balance is to be used within about 8 years.
GTL demerger share listing is expected to complete by end-July 2026; the listing approval for new Gujarat Energy shares (about 93 crore shares total) is expected within 7-10 days.
capex_capacity: CGD capex guidance is about INR1,000 crore; E&P capex about INR100 crore for drilling a few wells.
Gujarat Energy holds about 36.8-38% of GSPC LNG (investment about INR1,700 crore), following conversion of outstanding amounts into equity; it became a subsidiary.
GSPC Mundra LNG regasification terminal utilisation was about 17% in FY26; it is now at about 35-38% from May 2026.
Management is exploring a dedicated propane import jetty, JT and storage tanks near Morbi, with port authorities in Gujarat under discussion.
Long-term regasification capacity at Dahej is 2.25 MMTPA; long-term LNG totals about 2.96 MTPA (about 10.66 mmscmd).
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic units on gas rose from 83 (1.66 mmscmd) in March 2026 to 710 units (about 8 mmscmd) by late May 2026; contracts are signed monthly.

Non-Morbi industrial pricing is about INR68 per SCM and Morbi about INR75 per SCM; an analyst's spot-LNG math suggested Morbi margins may be negative at current spot LNG prices, which management did not accept.
Sourcing mix (per management): APM about 2 mmscmd, New Well Gas 0.4-0.5 mmscmd, long-term LNG about 3.5 mmscmd (majority Brent-linked), short-term about 3.5 mmscmd.
FY26 gas trading sales by user: CGD companies about 52-53%, fertilisers about 27%, others (refinery, power, industry) the rest.
Two new long-term LNG SPAs signed in FY26 (Qatar Energy and Uniper, up to 1.36 MTPA combined); Qatar 1 MTPA ramps up to 2030; 2 cargoes already lost in May-June 2026 due to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current sales are about 8 mmscmd, with customers indicating up to 8.8-8.9 mmscmd. Pricing is about INR75 per SCM in Morbi and about INR68 elsewhere, indexed to exchange rate and calorific value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PLF was about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. Management is evaluating reviving the plants through alignment with other businesses. GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

risks_watch: Propane supply tightness supports Morbi demand, but a normalisation could cut spot prices and volumes; management said it would still compete.
Spot LNG price and INR/USD moves could compress Morbi and CGD margins; an analyst's calculation showed a possible negative spread at spot LNG of about $17-18/MMBtu.

The power segment (about 1,000 MW) is loss-making with very low PLF; its revival plan and the 700 MW PPA economics are unresolved.
