539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.
capex_capacity: CGD capex of about INR1,000 crores guided for FY27; INR127 crores invested in CGD infrastructure in Q1.
CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.
Gas sourcing for CGD: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term, and about 69% short-term or inter-segment.
demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Morbi run-rate is about 3 mmscmd of gas versus about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources. Gas is priced about INR78/scm against propane at about INR65/scm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD sourcing: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term and about 69% short-term or inter-segment. Gas trading: about 20% long-term (about 20% of which is Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic and about 67% spot. Long-term share is about 28%, or about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent, targeted at 4 million tonnes or more by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gas trading margin high in Q1, and can it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to timely sourcing and Brent-linked long-term contracts. It ruled out negative trading quarters and maintained FY27 gas trading profit guidance of about INR1,100 crores on total volume, with a 4-5% margin target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is about INR7,200 crores, with a concrete deployment plan by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification. It cited dividends of about INR835 crores under Government of Gujarat guidelines.

risks_watch: Morbi volume sustainability: run-rate about 3 mmscmd versus 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the 1.8-2 mmscmd floor on one-month contracts and propane supply recovering.

Gas trading margin durability: Q1 gas trading EBT of INR726 crores against FY27 guidance of about INR1,100 crores, with management stating it is conservative; Q2 visibility limited by Middle East volatility.
CGD EBITDA below guidance at INR5.18/scm against the INR5.5-6.5/scm range; management kept guidance but gave no segment-level explanation.
Third-party gas trading volumes down to about 3.3 mmscmd from about 5 mmscmd, with recovery expected only in FY28-29.
Power segment utilisation very low (about 6% PLF at GSEG and 1% at Pipavav); revival strategy to be shared in a few months.

Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Contributes about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book; management targets 30% in three years. Margin is about 1-2% higher than conventional castings.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet material; product development and qualification ongoing with three to four products developed. Initial contributions expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is installed capacity and maximum utilisation, and why have EBITDA margins fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT; utilisation about 73-74%, with 80-85% achievable this year. Margin fell to 12% because raw material prices rose sharply in March, aggravated by gas issues; recovery expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-6%, and gas, outsourced labour, manpower and freight costs also rose in March. Management expects a reversion to 15-16% margins if war-related disruption does not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and leverage comfort?

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage GNPA rose to 1.54% from 1.27% over the year; management attributed it to normal book ageing as the book is not being pushed (yield is low).

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Outstanding book INR9,875 crore with 5 million cards in force; credit card GNPA fell to 1.49% from 1.99%, while SMA rose to 1.49% from 1.35%.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to range-bound in Q3 from current levels and recover to about 5.8% by Q4 FY27, driven by excess liquidity deployment (7 bps drag reverses), day count (about 8 bps per management) and repo hikes.

Management assumes repo rate hikes of 25 bps already done, plus 25 bps in the remainder of FY27 (likely December) and 25 bps in April 2027. Blended FY28 cost of funds expected to rise about 5-10 bps over FY27.
Management expects FY27 cost-to-income ratio of about 55% on an incremental basis, with operating jaws of at least 500 bps (H1 jaws 553 bps; Q2 592 bps).
Credit cost guidance referred to as 1.5% to 1.6%; management said it is comfortable for the next couple of quarters, with El Nino risk to be watched in Q3-Q4.
FCNR scheme estimated to add about 100 bps benefit on INR35,000 crore cost of funds versus domestic alternatives; ROA impact of FCNR margin dilution estimated at only about 2 bps.
Management stated loan growth of at least 20% and deposit growth of about 20-22% are visible; LDR expected to stay flat or improve, with deposit flows slightly above loan growth.

IRDAI commission consultation paper could reduce fee income; management expects it to be broadly offset by repo hikes, FCNR benefit and product mix changes. Expected to come into effect from next year.
Operational risk RWA guidelines effective April 1, 2027 expected to offset ECL transition capital impact, leaving CET1 broadly neutral; further clarity expected in about a quarter.
capex_capacity: No new capex plan or branch-expansion figure was given. Management referred to the network of about 1,200 branches and 1,243 ATMs as a cost drag on the liability side.

FCNR(B) raise of USD3.6 billion (INR34,390 crore) was about 2.7% of national mobilisation under the RBI scheme; debut USD950 million bond raised from the offshore IBU; S&P and CareEdge gave investment-grade ratings.
Management said no pipeline for further foreign borrowings (ECB) as the borrowings have largely been mobilised.
Capital raise is under consideration depending on market conditions; not included in the 5.8% NIM outlook.
demand_pricing: Loan growth 30.1% YoY including FCNR-backed loans, 22.2% excluding them. Growth drivers were mortgage, vehicle, consumer loans, and business banking and wholesale (each above 30% YoY).
Deposit growth 25.9% YoY; bank deliberately slowed core deposit growth (ex FCNR 14.1% YoY) and repaid about INR5,000 crore of bulk deposits and about INR5,000 crore of maturing CDs in September.

FCNR(B) deposits cost about 6.85% annualised; management pegs the all-in cost of funds on these at about 6.8-6.85%, versus about 7.8% for domestic equivalent (including CRR/SLR costs), about 100 bps benefit.
Savings account rate cut: management said the bank moved from 7% to 6.5% to 6.25% and now pays 6% above INR25 lakh balances.
About 60% of the book is fixed-rate (including FCNR), about 31-32% repo-linked, and the balance MCLR-linked.

Corporate book: A-and-above rated are 76% of the book, with BBB at 20% and BB and below at 4%; net book about INR70,000 crore against about INR1 lakh crore total exposure including non-funded. Management cited nil delinquency in 7 years apart from one ATM company loss of about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain (Autonomous): Why no visible funding-cost benefit from strong FCNR inflows, and how is the INR34,000-odd crore being deployed; what spread sits behind the 7 bps liquidity drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhanshu said about INR5,000 crore of bulk deposits and about INR5,000 crore of maturing CDs were repaid in September, with excess liquidity parked in low-yielding treasury and nostro balances (LCR 139% in September, normalising to about 115-116% within a month). The 7 bps drag is expected to vanish by Q4. Management cited the savings rate cut (7% to 6%, above INR25 lakh) and guided blended FY28 cost of funds up about 5-10 bps over FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain: Is the 150-160 bps credit cost guidance right, and what is being seen on El Nino, oil and macro?

qa_highlights.question: Akshay Jain: Why did mortgage GNPA rise and credit card SMA inch up?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage GNPA went from 1.27% to 1.54%, attributed to normal book ageing with the book not being pushed given low yield and near-nil YoY growth. Credit card GNPA fell from 1.99% to 1.49%, while card SMA rose from 1.35% to 1.49%, described as normal quarter-to-quarter variation.

qa_highlights.question: Param Subramanian (Investec): Is 55% incremental cost-to-income a multi-year commitment, and what is the steady-state liability drag?

qa_highlights.question: Param Subramanian: Confirm the NIM waterfall, Q3 and Q4 path, and asset-mix effect.

Q3 NIM should be range-bound, with recovery to about 5.8% in Q4 from the 7 bps liquidity drag reversing, 8 bps day-count benefit, and repo hikes. Vaidyanathan said the 2-quarter view already factors in asset mix.

qa_highlights.question: Piran Engineer (CITIC): Does September NIM lag the Q2 average, and is the 5.8% guidance excluding a capital raise? Also, why has CASA growth slowed?

qa_highlights.question: Piran Engineer: What is the corporate book's composition, rating profile and ROA case versus retail?

qa_highlights.question: Abhishek Murarka (HSBC): Are the insurance commission impacts fully offset by FCNR savings and rate hikes, and what is the quantum?

qa_highlights.question: Jai Prakash Mundhra (ICICI Securities): Any further ECB pipeline, LDR outlook, fixed/repo split, and ECL transition impact?

539448|2026-03.headline: IndiGo posted a Q4 FY26 net loss of 25.4 billion rupees, driven by 48.2 billion rupees of FX losses; FY26 underlying profit ex-FX and exceptionals was 75 billion rupees.
539448|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by the December operational disruption tail, a March demand break from Middle East escalation, and a sharp rupee depreciation of about 5% in the quarter. Q4 capacity growth slowed to 3% (about 10% in Jan-Feb) and PRASK fell 4% to 4.46 rupees. qa_highlights.question: What is the CASK ex-fuel ex-FX outlook and rupee sensitivity?

qa_highlights.answer: Hedge ceiling raised from $1 billion to $3 billion: $1 billion for 12-month cash flows and $2 billion over 2 to 5 years; hedged position currently $1.3 billion. Fuel hedging is at an early internal-deliberation stage.

539448|2026-06.headline: IndiGo swung to a net loss of INR 2.4 billion in Q1 FY27 as fuel CASK rose ~80% YoY, despite yield growth of 21.3%.
539448|2026-06.overview: IndiGo reported total income of INR 256 billion (up ~19% YoY), with EBITDAR of INR 38.3 billion at a 15.6% margin versus 28% a year earlier. Net loss was INR 2.4 billion against a profit of INR 21.8 billion in Q1 FY26; ex-currency the loss was about INR 56 million. Yield rose 21.3% and load factor fell 1.3 points to about 83%, but fuel cost rose sharply on Middle East-linked jet fuel prices and the rupee's depreciation of more than 11%. For Q2 FY27 management guided flattish capacity and PRASK growth above 25%, while holding the single-digit FY27 ASK guidance.

539871|2026-06.headline: Thyrocare Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.3% YoY to INR240 crores, with EBITDA margin at 32.2% and PAT of INR51.3 crores (+34%).
539871|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR240 crores (+24.3% YoY) and standalone revenue INR225.6 crores (+26.1% YoY), led by pathology growth of about 26%. Gross margin expanded more than 290 bps to 74.1% on better negotiations, 28% task volume growth and operating efficiency. EBITDA grew 34% to a 32.2% margin and PAT rose 34% to INR51.3 crores. Management formally launched specialty diagnostics commercially (allergy and genomics), announced plans to divest the nuclear imaging business, and restated test volumes to exclude calculated parameters.

financial_highlights.change: Management to use last four-quarter average

segments.name: Pathology - franchisee
segments.commentary: Franchisee business grew 27% YoY; active franchisees reached about 11,700, with 900 added in Q1. Value per franchisee has been around INR500 per month, and revenue per vial rose above INR250 from about INR240 per management's comparison.

segments.name: Pathology - partnership (B2B/B2C)
segments.commentary: Partnership business grew 26% YoY, led by insurance and health-tech partners and API integrations. Management said vial-level volume exceeds value growth due to discounting of incremental tests per patient.

segments.name: Aarogyam and Jaanch
segments.commentary: Flagship Aarogyam grew 21% YoY; Jaanch (curative, about 2% of pathology revenue) grew 36% YoY. Aarogyam is growing slower than non-Aarogyam tests, and Q1 is seasonally weak for preventive tests.

segments.name: Radiology
segments.commentary: Core revenue fell 4% YoY on centre consolidation but profitability improved. Management is pursuing divestment of the nuclear business; Q1 PAT for the radiology business was about INR1.72 crores, guided at about INR6 crores for FY27, against an investment of about INR140 crores.

segments.name: Tanzania (international)
segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Specialty diagnostics
segments.commentary: Commercial go-live in Q1 FY27 with allergy (Phadia platform) and genomics (NIPT, exome, NGS, gut microbiome, and others); over 20 specialised tests added. Specialty is under 1% of the test volume of about 5.5 crore tests.

guidance_outlook: Franchisee additions: management revised the expectation to about 500-700 per quarter. Q1 added about 900, with Q2 about 500, Q3 nil (seasonal), and Q4 about 500; some churn is possible, so not all 900 may remain by year-end.
Franchisee growth guidance held at mid-to-high teens for FY27; management said it would firm up guidance after H1.
Specialty diagnostics: ambition to reach 15-20% of portfolio (peer benchmark) in 3-5 years; no formal doctor coverage target set yet.
Specialty margins are expected to be broadly in line with current EBITDA margin unless volumes fail to materialise.
Radiology divestment: about 6 months process, no definitive buyer yet.
Consumables: announcement on Thyrocare-branded consumables expected by September.
No dividend guidance is given by management.
capex_capacity: Lab network at 43 labs in India plus 1 in Tanzania; three new labs opened in Q1 at Muzaffarpur (Bihar), Kurnool (Andhra Pradesh) and Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh).

Central processing labs in Mumbai and Delhi carry most specialty capex, which is already done; significant specialty capex is not expected in the next year beyond expansion capex if volumes exceed plan.
Phlebotomy network of about 2,000-2,100 phlebotomists; on-time arrival at 99%.
Over INR250 crores of capex invested over the period, per management.
demand_pricing: Franchisee revenue per vial rose about 7% YoY to above INR250, attributed to a mix shift away from thyroid (now low single-digit % of mix versus about 20% four years ago) toward lipid, biochemistry, multi-marker and PCR tests.
Partnership vial-level pricing shows erosion because incremental tests are discounted to encourage fuller panels; management said test-level pricing is broadly in line.
Franchisee network grew to about 11,700 active franchisees, a fourfold increase since the FY21 takeover. Field team roughly doubled over the year, from about 35-40 to about 70.
Channel strategy: pay-for-performance structure for franchisees, branded stores, and Madhuri Dixit as brand ambassador.
Specialty pricing: NIPT priced at less than half of competitors' prices; management aims for affordability and volume.

qa_highlights.question: How significant could genomics and allergy be in 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early for specific guidance; peers have specialty at 15-20% of portfolio, and management's ambition is the same level in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed for specialty in the next couple of years?
qa_highlights.answer: Most investment is done in the central Mumbai and Delhi labs; significant capex is not expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for imaging divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Nuclear business has not grown or been invested in; process expected to take about 6 months, with no definitive buyer yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the test-volume definition changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Calculated parameters that are not billed were removed from test counts and past quarters restated; management said the variation is small.

qa_highlights.question: Will franchisee guidance be revised after 900 additions in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 500-700 per quarter is a reasonable run-rate, with Q3 nil; overall mid-to-high teens growth guidance held until H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 900 franchisee addition sustainable and what is the Q1 PAT for radiology?
qa_highlights.answer: Adds reflect the enlarged sales team and branded stores; radiology Q1 PAT was about INR1.72 crores, with about INR6 crores expected for FY27.

risks_watch: Franchisee churn: management said not all 900 Q1 additions may remain by year-end, and the Q2 base is high (Q2 FY26 revenue about INR200 crores).

Parent-level debt: API Group debt reduced to about INR1,050 crores from INR1,700 crores; promoter holding is pledged. IPO or reverse merger is not planned and is at least 12 months away, per management.
Specialty execution risk: the segment is at a nascent stage, prescription-driven, and not yet scaled. Management has not set doctor coverage targets.
Aarogyam growth (21%) trails non-Aarogyam tests, so mix shift could dilute per-test realisation.
Consumables announcement expected by September 2026; details unknown.
Radiology divestment: no buyer identified; contribution is small (about INR6 crores PAT expected for FY27).

Cautious and evasive on forward guidance: management declined to revise franchisee or growth guidance until H1, and gave no specialty targets or dividend guidance.
key_quotes: I'm proud to say that after a strong growth of 20% in FY26, in Q1 FY27, our pathology business has grown even faster at 26%.
So, it's too early for me to revise guidance. I will still hold to the mid to high teens guidance at this point in time.
I think API will consider an IPO when it is profitable ex-Thyrocare, as well as debt free.

539872|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.3% YoY to INR165.6 crore with gross margin up 210 bps to 48.3%; management guides 10-15% revenue growth for FY27.
539872|2026-06.overview: Bajaj Healthcare reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR165.6 crore, up 11.3% YoY and 8.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of about INR29.6 crore (17.8% margin) and PAT from continuing operations of INR13.9 crore (8.4% margin). Domestic API was the main growth driver at INR92.3 crore (up 27% YoY), while exports (INR50.1 crore) and formulations (INR23.3 crore) contributed the rest. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% and EBITDA margins of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28, and reiterated pipeline timelines for peptide, oncology API, and CDMO/novel-drug launches. Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end, and the call was the company's first earnings call.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR92.3 crore, up 27% YoY; management said API prices were broadly stable QoQ and the growth was not price-led. Ascorbic acid and salts contribute about 8-10% of revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Revenue INR50.1 crore in Q1. Magnesium L-Threonate (nutraceutical ingredient supplied to a US innovator) is the largest export product at about 10% of FY26 revenue, with FY27 growth guided at 15-20%. Management expects export share to rise to 30-35% over time.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.3 crore in Q1. Cenobamate CDMO launch expected to add INR10-12 crore in FY27; Oncocare brand business covers 15+ brands across 23 states and 3 UTs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% YoY; profit growth guided at a similar rate. FY28 top-line growth also guided at a similar rate.
EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28.
Capex of INR40-50 crore every year over the next few years.
Medium term: management said INR900-1,000 crore revenue achievable in the next two to three years.
Revenue mix expected to normalise as exports improve and geopolitical conditions ease over the year.
Receivable days expected to settle at 110-120 days going forward.
capex_capacity: Peptide plant: installed capacity about 250 kg per annum, commissioning targeted for Q4 2027. Management said peak revenue at full utilisation could be INR200-300 crore at 18-20% EBITDA margin, ramping over two to three years.
Oncology API dedicated facility: commercial target Q4 2028.
Gen Rx Pharmaceutical facility in Nashik (solid dosage forms): acquisition pending NCLT approval; commercial production expected in H2 2027.
Savli DSIR-approved R&D centre expansion of over 10,000 sq ft, expected to be operational by August 2026, housing 100+ researchers. R&D spend rose from 0.4% of sales in 2024 to 2.2% in 2026.
Three loss-making Tarapur plants: one sold, two remain with no buyer yet; sale proceeds not quantified.
demand_pricing: API prices stable QoQ in Q1; management said future pricing depends on geopolitical developments and oil prices.
Semaglutide (first peptide planned) market price cited at USD120-150 per gram. Plant is designed for global markets, with initial work for India.
CDMO: DMFs filed in UK and EU and six CEP approvals received in the last 6-8 months. Management said first customer revenue could come at end-FY28, with quantum not yet estimated.
Cenobamate: SEC recommendation received; DCGI NOC and state licence still pending; tie-ups with eight Indian marketing companies, with the company acting as CDMO partner.
Suvorexant: BE studies completed; commercialisation expected Q4 FY28 because the patent is still in force.

Vitamin C is about 8-9% of revenue; backward integration via ICT MoU expected to complete in 2029. Eight to ten API molecules being backward-integrated, expected to be 20-25% of revenue, with a 1-2% margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: Was domestic API growth driven by volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said API prices were stable QoQ, implying the growth was volume-led; it added that the outlook depends on geopolitics and oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and profit growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 10-15% for FY27, with profit growth expected at a similar rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial timeline for the peptide plant and the expected revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant commissioning Q4 2027 with Semaglutide as the first product. Peak revenue of INR200-300 crore at full utilisation, with 18-20% EBITDA margin. Management said commercial revenue would begin in 2028.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable days trend and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end; management expects 110-120 days going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and acquisition outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR40-50 crore each year. No further acquisitions planned until Gen Rx is commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: What working capital and inventory drivers apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory rose in Q4 FY26 on war-related precautionary buying; the longer-term increase reflects a shift from a few high-volume products pre-COVID to a larger product basket.

risks_watch: Commercial launch timelines for peptide (Q4 2027), oncology API (Q4 2028), Gen Rx (H2 2027) and CDMO (end-FY28) all depend on approvals or commissioning and have not been demonstrated yet.
Cenobamate revenue of INR10-12 crore in FY27 depends on pending DCGI NOC and state licence.
Receivables are high at 131 days; the 110-120 day target depends on customer behaviour, including government and institutional clients.
Inventory has risen sharply versus FY21 on a broader product mix.
Two Tarapur loss-making plants remain unsold.
Opioid-derivative intermediates are still in R&D, and the Government of India discussion on capacity is unresolved.
Management declined to name most peptide molecules, citing confidentiality.

539872|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores and PAT 26.9% to INR14.1 crores, with formulations up 82%.
539872|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 18.9% YoY to INR175.9 crores in Q2 FY27 and 6.2% QoQ, with H1 revenue up 15.1% to INR341.5 crores. EBITDA rose 12.2% YoY to INR32.1 crores at an 18.2% margin, while gross margin fell to 48.3% amid West Asia disruption. Formulations (INR41.7 crores, up 82% YoY) and export API (INR62.6 crores, up 28.5%) offset a weaker domestic API line (INR71.6 crores, down from INR76.3 crores). Management reiterated FY29 targets of INR900-1,000 crores revenue and 18-21% EBITDA margin, and flagged higher inventory held as a precaution against Gulf disruption.

segments.name: Domestic API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR71.6 crores vs INR92 crores in Q1 and INR76.3 crores a year ago; H1 up 10.1% YoY to INR163.9 crores. Management expects little pricing improvement over time.

segments.name: Export API
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR62.6 crores, up 28.5% YoY; Magnesium L-Threonate supplied to a US patent holder contributes about 11-12% of total turnover.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR41.7 crores, up about 82% YoY, driven by the Cenobamate API tablet launch in September through eight marketing partners; formulations are about 24% of revenue in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY29 target: revenue of INR900-1,000 crores with EBITDA margin of 18-21%.
Management said it is on track for the earlier guidance of 10-15% revenue and profit growth with 18-20% margin; Q2 growth was almost 20%.
Operating cash flow expected to be more than INR30 crores for FY27.
Total FY27 capex expected at INR65-80 crores; about INR50-60 crores per year thereafter to reach INR1,000 crores revenue.
Management expects gross margin and EBITDA margin to be maintained in coming quarters, supported by product mix.

Genrx (acquired, NCLT approved): INR200-250 crores revenue potential in two to three years. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after commissioning in Q2 FY28. Peptide facility: first-year revenue INR70-100 crores in FY28-29.
capex_capacity: Peptide manufacturing plant (250 kg per annum, solid-phase synthesis and fermentation) scheduled for completion by 31 March 2027.
Oncology API plant to commence in Q2 FY28.
Dedicated formulation plant at Nashik (solid oral dosage, nasal, oral oncology, nutraceutical, ointment) expected operational in Q1 FY28.
New R&D centre started in August with over 80 staff, planned capacity of 120 chemists; R&D spend raised to about 2.5-3% of revenue.
Genrx acquisition to handle non-Baroda formulation volumes; new molecules to be made at Baroda, which is an approved facility.
demand_pricing: Cenobamate API tablets approved by DCGI (first in India, six strengths), launched commercially in September 2026; repeat orders received from partners, but secondary sales not yet known.

Regulatory filings: 110 DMFs filed, with approvals taking two to three years; 8 CEPs approved and 4 under review in Europe; 17 products registered with KDMF in South Korea; 3 products registered in Egypt with 10 more planned; 17 products identified for Brazil CBPF submission.
API pricing described as under pressure with little prospect of improvement; management said prices are more or less stabilised but volatile given Gulf disputes, freight and interest rates.
Management expects 60-70% of the portfolio to be backward integrated in two to three years.
Mix target over three to four years: formulations 45-50% and API 50-55% (vs about 20-24% formulations today).

qa_highlights.question: Will Manjusar formulation production shift to Genrx, and what is the role of the Nashik facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Nashik is a strategic capacity addition for the next two to three years; new molecules will be made at the approved Baroda facility, and Genrx will handle other formulations for different markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital inventory rise and will it normalise by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the higher inventory is a deliberate policy decision to avoid stoppages from the Gulf dispute; management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue potentials from Genrx and the oncology API plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Genrx: INR200-250 crores in two to three years after start-up. Oncology API plant: about INR200 crores in two to three years after it is in operation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and is guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR65-80 crores; CFO said the company is on track for the earlier 10-15% growth and 18-20% margin guidance, with Q2 growth near 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given weak H1 conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash flow expected above INR30 crores for FY27; Q2 operating cash flow about INR15 crores; receivable days improved from 145 to 135.

qa_highlights.question: How is EBITDA margin holding up despite a roughly 225-250 bp YoY gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed stable EBITDA margin to product mix: export and formulation (Cenobamate launch) offset the domestic API dip, and said margins are expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio can be backward integrated, and what are the margin effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-70% of products could be backward integrated in two to three years, with revenue from these products rising about 10-15% and margins improving; no specific margin figure was given.

risks_watch: Gross margin fell YoY (about 225-250 bp per analyst) amid West Asia/Gulf disruption, freight and interest-rate pressure; management expects improvement but gave no figure.
Working capital and inventory build: operating cash flow in H1 weak relative to EBITDA; FY27 cash flow target of more than INR30 crores depends on inventory normalisation.
Domestic API revenue fell QoQ and YoY in Q2; API prices described as under pressure.
Commercial timelines: DMF/CEP approvals take 1-3 years; peptide and oncology plants depend on approvals with customers (6-10 months post-commissioning).
Cenobamate secondary sales not disclosed; management could not quantify FY27/FY28 revenue from it.
Execution risk from several new plants (peptide by March 2027, Nashik Q1 FY28, oncology Q2 FY28) and rapid senior hiring; management cited facilities as the main bottleneck over three years.

539876|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, with EBIT margin exiting near 10% versus 6.8% in H1.
539876|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, led by 10% growth in ECD and 14% growth in lighting. Management said EBIT margin improved from 6.8% in H1 to about 10% in Q4, driven by operating leverage, premiumisation, pricing and cost optimisation. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 271 Cr (11.9% margin). Butterfly returned to double-digit revenue and profit growth, and management took an impairment on its Butterfly carrying value, which is non-cash but hits ROCE and asset turnover. Management also announced a new super-premium product line, Crompton Rhion, and an identical dividend to last year.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, Q4; management called it industry-leading
YoY, Q4, with steady EBIT margins
Management says Butterfly is now cash flow positive

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 10%, broad-based across pumps, small domestic appliances and fans. Fans saw record March volumes; BLDC portfolio growing 30%-plus. Management says it gained share in every ECD product in FY26 but did not give category numbers.

segments.name: Small domestic appliances (SDA)
segments.commentary: Management said FY26 growth was in the early 20s percent and Q4 growth close to 30%, with a step-up in profitability. New launches included infrared cooktops, air fryers and premium juicers.

segments.name: Lighting (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 14%. Government share of B2B mix fell about 500 bps in FY26. Y-o-Y margin said to be roughly flat despite materially higher ad spend in the quarter.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 17% with steady EBIT margins and higher advertising spend. Management says it is back to strong double-digit growth in both revenue and profit, and an impairment was taken on its carrying value.

segments.name: Solar pumps and rooftop (new PLs)
segments.commentary: Solar pumps revenue was about Rs 200 Cr last year and grew significantly this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr (about 38,000 units in Andhra plus Telangana), with about 5,000 homes installed so far. segments.name: Wires (Crompton Armor)
segments.commentary: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and now selling in South India; national rollout is planned over the year rather than all at once.

Solar rooftop execution stepped up in the last 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases were taken against the cost inflation, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Two ECD price increases since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative in fans in FY26, mostly in Q4, which offset material inflation. Further inflation came in April, and management is waiting to see before deciding pricing for the rest of Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 contribution and FY27 ramp-up from solar pumps and rooftops?

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins dip, and is growth troughing?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Butterfly impairment's tax impact and is the merger still planned?

qa_highlights.question: What is the national rollout plan for wires?

540005|2026-03.headline: LTM to acquire Randstad's Europe and Australia tech and consulting arm: €469M revenue, €160M EV, plus a five-year Randstad GCC deal worth ~$55–60M initial scope.
540005|2026-03.overview: LTM announced on May 22, 2026 a proposed acquisition of Randstad's Technology and Consulting Services business in Europe and Australia, with annualized revenue of €469M (about $500M+) and a proposed enterprise value of €160M on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The package has three parts: the acquisition, a five-year IT services partnership to scale Randstad's GCC in Hyderabad with an AI-centric approach, and an agreement for LTM to manage subcontractor spend through Randstad's MSP capabilities. Management said the asset is a white-space play in continental Europe, Australia, and the aerospace & defence, automotive, utilities and BFS verticals, and will be run as a separate subsidiary. The call was Q&A-heavy on revenue decline, margin dilution, and the durability of client relationships; the transcript contains no reported Q4 FY26 financials.

qa_highlights.question: How does coal margin trend, given FY25 blended margin around 26% vs 23% in FY26?

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of borrowing and what drives the interest cost trend?

InvIT valuations depend on final BPC values, land handover and scope changes; InvIT unit values on balance sheet are about INR1,600 crores.
Delivery of the net debt-free goal by FY28 relies on InvIT transfers and mining cash flows.
Competitive intensity and high bidding in certain segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11-12% remain unchanged, and will revenue growth be back-ended?

qa_highlights.question: How much bid value is pending opening, and what is the working capital outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Can MDO revenue reach the Rs 2,500 crore FY27 level given Rs 362 crore in Q1 and 4.79 MT output?

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated net debt trajectory, and is there a consol-level target?

Rs 7,801 crore consol net debt is referenced; the company cites Rs 45,000 crore of road HAM projects done.

qa_highlights.question: Other income breakup and standalone capex?

540048|2026-03.headline: S.P. Apparels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR 364 crore (from INR 399 crore) and EBITDA margin to 12.2%; management guides INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue.
540048|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was soft on volumes: consolidated revenue declined year-on-year to INR 364 crore and EBITDA to INR 44 crore, with PAT down to INR 18.59 crore, as US tariff after-effects and shipping disruption delayed orders. Full-year consolidated revenue grew 13.2% to INR 1,578 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 217 crore. Management says US orders are returning, guides to INR 2,000 crore consolidated revenue in FY27, and points to Sri Lanka ramp-up and EU/UK FTA benefits. Current utilisation is cited at 64%, and the timing of recovery in H2 FY27 is the key uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation driving incremental volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty-paid status versus duty-free Bangladesh and Sri Lanka helps competitiveness and is bringing more business. The CFO added that 80% of orders are covered when booked, so there is no direct benefit from depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 2,000 crore FY27 target be reached, given Sri Lanka and Sivakasi ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sri Lanka FOB is about INR 45 crore in FY26, targeting INR 200-250 crore in FY27. Sivakasi adds about INR 40-50 crore, and H2 FY27 is expected to see the recovery as utilisation rises from 64%. Analyst arithmetic came to about INR 1,850 crore, and the gap was not fully bridged.

qa_highlights.question: Will Retail become PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said Retail is at EBITDA breakeven, and that finance cost on Retail Ventures is the drag. He said equity raising is needed and the company is ready to raise it now.

qa_highlights.question: Has labour returned after the capacity cut?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said workers left after the US capacity reduction, and that 30-40% have returned. Recruitment and training are ongoing, and management said this is not a labour disruption.

segments.commentary: Served through 8,400 dealers across over 5,000 towns in 24 states. FY26 volume grew 65% and value 111%, helped by a higher-priced second model and price increases.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales grew 136% YoY and platform sales 39% YoY in FY26; management cited a 52% value growth figure in Q&A.

segments.name: Australia (Joyce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR422 crore with EBITDA margin of 10%, up almost 400 bps from FY25, driven by yield programmes, price renegotiation and supply-chain restructuring.

segments.name: Spain
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR391 crore with EBITDA margin of 10.4%, against 8.4% in FY25. Management sees a stable 30-32% gross margin range.

segments.name: Furlenco
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR370 crore (over 60% growth) and PAT of close to INR60 crore versus INR3 crore in FY25. Company holds about 43% fully diluted; FY27 revenue target is about INR500 crore.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR70 crore.

guidance_outlook: Targeted growth of 15%+ over the medium term, expected to be higher given raw material-led price increases; management is aiming for a 3-5 year horizon to become a full product player.
Management believes core EBITDA margin is in an 11-12% range and can move higher with growth; Q1-Q2 FY27 margin impact from raw materials expected at no more than 50-100 bps.
FY27 standalone depreciation guided at INR140-145 crore on a consolidated basis, roughly INR35 crore per quarter.
FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking, marketing capex for new stores, across India, Australia and Spain.
Consolidated finance cost guided at about INR50 crore for FY27 (about INR35 crore interest plus INR15 crore other charges).
India debt of about INR300 crore expected to be repaid in 1-1.5 years; Australia and Spain debt of about INR350 crore is self-liquidating.
Remaining Kurlon synergies of about INR40 crore (out of INR250 crore total) depend on new machines that are delayed about 1.5 quarters; installation expected by mid or end of Q1 FY27.
Furlenco IPO decision to be taken in the next 3-4 months; listing expected in about one year or later.
Dividend of 20% for FY26 recommended, subject to shareholder approval; first dividend in company history.
Pillows (about INR100 crore market) to be treated as a separate category going forward; brand.com and U2O remain focus areas.
Hope to cross 100 integrated Furlenco-Sheela stores in FY27 (currently over 40).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking to support volume growth of about 15% in FY26, and new store marketing capex.

TDI supply: GNFC plant shut for technical and gas reasons, so the company added a new hedging supplier (Korea, Japan and China sources) and avoided stock-outs at higher prices.

Marketing spend for FY26 is around 4.5% of sales, similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins under pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 given higher-cost raw material inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said price changes flow through in 10-15 days and inventory costs match, so the gross margin impact is limited to about 50-100 bps. Volume growth, given a 30%+ contribution margin, should support EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is U2O value growth (111%) far above volume growth (65%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Rakesh Chahar said a higher-priced second model was introduced and both models saw price increases. U2O margins are between offline and e-commerce margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the change in depreciation policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the written-down method front-loaded depreciation (70-75% in the first 3-4 years) for assets with 40-50 year lives, so the policy was realigned to useful life.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Australia and Spain margins, and is a sale still under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees Spain gross margins at 30-32% and Australian margins up about 4-5 points on a normal basis. The target is 10-12% EBITDA. Rahul Gautam said the company is open to a sale but is not actively pursuing one.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Furlenco plans and how is ROCE?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the remaining synergy is pending?

Sustainability of the Q4 volume spike, which was partly from competitors exiting; whether customers stay after supply normalises.
Delayed INR40 crore synergy from new machines; watch whether it is installed by end of Q1 FY27.
Depreciation policy change flatters reported profit; compare with peers on a like-for-like basis.
Furlenco IPO timing and valuation, and integration of its stores into the network.
Management did not disclose the U2O volume share of total mattress volumes; a follow-up was promised.
540203|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the dividend, with explicit targets. Cautious and somewhat evasive on raw material pricing trajectory and on the timing of any sale of the international business.

540203|2026-06.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
540203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Standalone India revenue grew 20% to INR761 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR68 crore, with gross margin compressed by sharp raw-material (TDI/polyol) swings that management attributes to the Middle East conflict. Management chose to keep growing foam volumes, which was cash-accretive, and international subsidiaries (Australia, Spain) posted sharply higher margins on inventory gains. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

segments.name: India mattresses
segments.commentary: Value up 15% and volume up 6% YoY. U2O channel revenue up 81% with volume up 19%, now about 10,000 dealers, helped by 5- and 6-inch mattresses.

segments.name: India foam
segments.commentary: Value up 26% and volume up 4% YoY; faster foam growth diluted gross margin but was cash-accretive as competitors lacked raw material.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales up 69% YoY, platforms up 19%; overall category up 30% with volumes up 23%.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 67% YoY with EBITDA margin around 28-30%; Presence 360 crossed 3.2 lakh users.

segments.name: Furlenco (associate)
segments.commentary: Operating profit roughly INR9 crore per quarter; Q1 PAT share reflects 35% stake and no deferred tax asset recognition (DTA only booked at year end, likely Q4).

guidance_outlook: Reiterated 15% EBITDA margin target for next year; management said there is no change to this stance, though Rachna Kukreja's question suggested earlier 11-12% FY27 guidance.
Expects more than 15% revenue growth for the full year and double-digit volume growth in both foam and mattresses for FY27.

International operations to grow about 5% in local currency with 10-12% EBITDA margins; for FY27, management is confident of crossing INR1,000 crore revenue and about INR120 crore EBITDA for overseas operations.
Synergy benefit of about INR40 crore still pending; machine under installation, with full impact expected in Q3.
Integration of Kurlon about 96-97% complete; roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the balance expected.
Expects volume recovery with Q3 (festive) and Q4 the strongest quarters; FY27 volume expected to exceed last year.
Expects ROCE to reach roughly 20-25% in three years from about 10% currently.
Debt: India debt above INR300 crore to be cleared in about one year; overseas debt of about INR350 crore to be repaid over five years. Balance sheet will not be debt free by year-end.
capex_capacity: Company-operated stores (COCO): about INR27 lakh capex per store plus INR20-22 lakh working capital; about INR50 lakh per store, so about INR25 crore for 50 stores. Stores are about 2,000 sq ft (range 1,800-3,000).
COCO store rollout: 22 existing stores upgraded; target 50 stores with about 42 operational.
Furlenco shop-in-shop: about 40-50 stores currently; first target 100 stores. Company has about 3,500 exclusive brand outlets.
Standalone synergy-related machine under installation, expected to deliver full impact in Q3.
Operating units reduced from 21 to 12 as part of Kurlon integration.
demand_pricing: Standalone India volume growth about 6%; management views sub-10% as satisfactory and says industry grew close to 5%.
U2O price increase taken last year to fix channel margins; value growth well ahead of volume as a result; management says the pricing level is now sustainable.
Raw material (TDI/polyol) prices swung roughly +40% to -20% in the period; prices spiked in March after the Feb 28 Iran conflict, eased in April, then rose again about a month before the call.
Management says price increases pass through commensurately, but in-pipe inventory on the high seas can lag on sharp falls and hit margin.
Foam share of COGS: TDI and polyol are 65-70% of COGS.
Premiumisation: ASP marginally up across segments; new products introduced to lift ASP; consumer-led promotions launched.
Organised mattress market combined share of Sleepwell and Kurlon close to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Australia/Spain margin gain sustainable, and how much of it is inventory benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains came from longer-held low-cost inventory and yield and supply chain programmes. Overseas momentum should moderate as India recovers, with normal inventory levels by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-volume trade-off after the steep price hikes, and expects double-digit volume growth for the year once volatility eases. Gross margins were hit mainly by foam, while incremental foam sales generated cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not guided for 13% for FY27 (only 11-12%) but stands by its margin commitment; the current volatility makes it hard to comment, and gross margin has fallen more than the guided range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and rollout of company-owned stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR27 lakh capex plus INR20-22 lakh working capital per store, with 42 operational of a 50-store target; about INR25 crore for another 50 COCO stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kurlon integration status and synergy realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration about 96-97% complete, operating units cut to 12 from 21, and roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the remainder on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Furlenco store rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Furlenco is present in 40-50 shop-in-shop stores with a first target of 100, and will go only where it fits its micro-market strategy.

Volume recovery: standalone India volume grew about 6% against double-digit growth last year; management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27 and strongest volumes in Q3 and Q4, contingent on volatility subsiding.

Synergy and capex execution: about INR40 crore synergy pending the machine installation (full impact expected Q3); COCO rollout of 50 stores at about INR50 lakh each (~INR25 crore) and Furlenco shop-in-shop target of 100 stores from about 40-50.

So, we guided for 11% to 12%. We never guided for 13% for the current year. Yes, we do stand for it.
There is no change in stand on the margins. We have a target of 15% EBITDA margin for the next year.
So, there would definitely be volume recovery. I would say we would go back higher than what the volumes we clocked last year.

It declined to give a view on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 margin figures put to it and repeatedly said it would revisit once volatility eases.

540205|2026-03.headline: Aditya Vision Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR625 crore and PAT 36% to INR22 crore, despite a weak summer and FY26 PAT up only 11%.
540205|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR2,672 crore and PAT grew 11% to INR117 crore, with EBITDA at INR228 crore (8.5% margin) and gross margin at 15.6%. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 28% and same-store sales growth of 18%, though gross margin (16%) and EBITDA margin (8.1%) were lower than the prior year. Management said H2 is now as important as H1, reflecting a shift away from a seasonal model. Store count reached 207 across four states, with Chhattisgarh entered and Madhya Pradesh planned this year. Inventory was built up to about INR840 crore ahead of anticipated OEM supply constraints and BEE-driven price increases.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Largest market at 74% of Q4 FY26 revenue and 75% of FY26 revenue; 118 stores across 38 districts.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: 14% of Q4 and 13% of FY26 revenue; 53 stores covering 30 of 75 districts, with most new stores opened in Feb-Mar 2026 and contributing less than a full year.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: 12% of both Q4 and FY26 revenue; 33 stores covering 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Entered early with 3 stores covering 2 of 33 districts; no revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Mobiles and laptops together exceed 25% of sales; ASP of mobiles rose about 20% in Q4, diluting gross margin. Small appliances grew about 50%, per analyst; cooling products (ACs, coolers, refrigerators) underperformed due to weak summer.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal store guidance; it cites about 25 stores when asked, and has added over 30 stores a year for the last 3-5 years.
Madhya Pradesh entry is on track for this financial year; Chhattisgarh and UP to be scaled up.
Management expects opex to grow in line with overall expenses rather than rise faster, as the store base becomes more mature.
Management cites an 8% to 10% EBITDA margin range as its endeavour, with 9% as a central target, but declined to give a timeline.
April 2026 described as very robust; May started colder but is expected to normalise into a normal summer.
No equity raise planned this financial year; internal accruals and working capital borrowings are expected to suffice.
capex_capacity: Store base reached 207 at March 31, 2026, after 102 stores were added in the last three years versus 105 in the prior 23-24 years.
Stores take 9 to 12 months to break even, per management.
Inventory of about INR840 crore held at end Q4 FY26, built ahead of OEM supply uncertainty (gas shortages linked to a Gulf conflict) and BEE-driven price increases of about 8% to 10%.
Plans to scale UP and Chhattisgarh while deepening Bihar and Jharkhand; a neighbouring state, previously held back by political uncertainty, is now being considered.
demand_pricing: Weak summer and extended rains hit H1; Q1 FY26 revenue grew 6% and H1 grew 11%. Q3 grew 28%, driven by festive demand.
Historically Q1 and Q2 contributed 55% to 60% of annual sales; management says this is now shifting towards a more balanced full-year model.
Price increases on mobiles and laptops lowered the margin mix; management said price hikes are not the main driver of profitability.
Management said OEMs bear the burden of unsold inventory and do not take returns; they help liquidate stock before new billing.
Real estate slowdown seen in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad has not yet affected Bihar, UP or Jharkhand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will high inventory give a competitive and margin advantage over peers in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on peers' inventory and said it holds inventory as per its own strategy and historical levels, not to profit from price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 100 bps YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to weak cooling-product sales in H1 and a Q4 surge in low-margin mobiles (ASP up about 20%) and laptops (ASP up 8-10%), which together exceed 25% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 50% rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to brand ambassador onboarding, UP expansion, and variable costs such as freight, card commissions and dealer discounts that rise with the 18% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised margins for mature Bihar, and when will UP match them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose state-wise margins, saying it aims to bring other states up to Bihar's level over time without sacrificing sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance given; management cited 25 stores when pressed and said it expects to keep beating its informal targets.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline and pointed to an 8% to 10% margin range, with 9% as the central target, while not compromising sales growth.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from mix shift toward mobiles and laptops, whose ASPs are rising.
Q4 inventory build (about INR840 crore) exposes the company to price-cut and demand risk if the summer underperforms; May started colder than normal.
Cash conversion: management declined to guide on OCF/EBITDA, saying it depends on inventory and working capital.
Finance cost implies about 12.8-13% on average debt per analyst, but this includes lease liability interest; the bank borrowing rate was not disclosed.
Most UP stores opened in the last months of FY26, so UP contribution and unit economics are not yet visible on a full-year basis.
Opex rising faster than revenue in new geographies (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) could weigh on EBITDA margins.
540205|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, demand momentum and the all-season model, but evasive on specifics: management declined to disclose state-wise margins, peer inventory, store targets, cash flow guidance and margin timelines.
key_quotes: I'm truly delighted to give the comfort to our investors and stakeholders that your company is now an all-weather, all-season company.

540212|2026-03.headline: TCI Express Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 327 crore, EBITDA margin 11.3%, PAT flat at INR 21 crore amid fuel and labour cost pressure.
540212|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 6% YoY to INR 327 crore and 4% QoQ, with total income of INR 331 crore. EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 37 crore (11.3% margin) while PAT was flat at INR 21 crore (6.3% margin). Full-year revenue grew about 2% to INR 1,236 crore, with PAT of INR 90 crore (7.2% margin). Management said the Gulf conflict pushed ATF prices up sharply and labour costs rose, and volume growth slowed to 4% YoY in Q4 after March.

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; management said surface margin should improve with diesel-linked price pass-through, citing about 30% arbitrage. Surface grew in single digits in the last two quarters, with mid-single-digit to ~10% growth expected going forward.

segments.name: Multimodal (Air, Rail, C2C, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About 18.5% of FY26 revenue, with management citing about 20% growth; target of 22% to 25% share over 2 to 3 years. Domestic and international air margins were hit this quarter, while rail and C2C margins were described as stable.

segments.name: Rail Express
segments.commentary: Management said rail gross profit is above 30% and realisation is about 2.5x surface. Rail volumes are not disclosed.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of business, with a target of 5%. Focus is on D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse movement with SME clients, not quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 10% to 11%, with revenue growth of about 15% including price hikes.
FY27 margin improvement of 100 to 150 basis points at EBITDA and PAT levels, conditional on fuel prices stabilising.
Q1 FY27 volume expected at high single-digit growth, improving QoQ through the year.
Multimodal growth guided at about 20% in FY27.
Depreciation run-rate of INR 30 to 32 crore per year after ROU additions; about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter.
Capex plan revised from INR 500 crore to INR 400 crore for FY23 to FY27; about INR 130 crore planned for FY27. A new five-year plan will follow.
Branch expansion of about 100 branches in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail, air and C2C).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 83.25% in Q4, improved QoQ.
Nagpur sorting centre upgraded and now owned; semi-automated, about 70,000 to 75,000 sq ft, with only 5% to 7% change in cut-off time.
Ahmedabad and Kolkata sorting centres under construction, to finish in FY27, with automation ramping up in the first half of FY28. Lucknow also in progress.
Mumbai and Kolkata sorting centres moved to 5-year leases, which added ROU assets and raised depreciation.
Next sorting centres planned for Chennai and Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Management said diesel rose about INR 8 and the company is passing it on to customers, with 85% pass-through expected and 10% to 15% of customers still negotiating.
Air fuel (ATF) rose about 50% and international air rates went up 2x to 3x after the Gulf conflict began at end-February, leading customers to hold shipments in March.
Labour costs rose 15% to 20%, adding about 100 basis points to overall cost, per management.
SME share of revenue was 48% to 52% against a historical 50:50 split; management expects a return to 50%+ with the last two months' results described as good.
Revenue per kg is about INR 12.3 to 12.4 with EBITDA of about INR 1.25 to 1.27 per kg, against a historical INR 1.8 to 2.0 per kg, per an analyst's calculation.
The company expects to benefit from air-to-surface and rail shifts as higher air prices push customers to other modes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been restricted and margins fallen from 15% to 16% to 10% to 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Gulf war and ATF spike, airline consolidation, airport privatisation, lower truck utilisation and a 100 bps hit from labour costs. It guided FY27 PAT margin recovery of 100 to 150 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of about 10% to 11% and revenue growth of about 15% for FY27, with Q1 at high single digits and QoQ improvement after that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the multimodal segment margin dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said air margins were temporarily hit by costs. Rail and C2C margins are stable and surface margin should improve with diesel pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the depreciation and interest increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Two sorting centres were moved to 5-year leases under Ind AS 116, which lifted ROU assets. Management said depreciation runs at about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA would have been about INR 29 crore, versus INR 32 crore reported, per the analyst's calculation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is about 2.5% of business, targeted to 5%, through D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse flows with SMEs and some aggregator platforms. Quick commerce is not in the strategy.

Prolonged Gulf conflict may raise ATF prices, reduce air volumes and push costs up.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and social security norms, plus state-level pressure.
Rupee weakness raising input costs.
SME stress and the share of SME revenue, which fell to 48% to 52%.

540716|2026-06.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.
540716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 GDPI grew 7.5% to ₹83.18 bn, below industry growth of 10.9%, with retail lines driving growth while commercial lines de-grew 13.8%. Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Grew 24.9% vs industry 20.1%. Retail Health grew 69.5% with share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; Group Health grew 16.3% with 10.3% share. Management attributed the higher health loss ratio to industry-wide claim incidence, not company-specific.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a quantified forward impact of the Motor TP judgement; said it is too early and will update each quarter.
Expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision; judgement-driven industry loss ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.
Expects Fire price aggression to moderate after Q1, though full recovery of de-growth in the rest of the year is uncertain.
Health claim incidence watch-point for Q2 (monsoon-linked); next detailed update to come with October results.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning plans were discussed on the call; the call covered underwriting, pricing, reserving and claims only.

Capacity was referenced only qualitatively: management said reinsurance renewals were relatively soft and capacity had been made available across the industry, which drove Fire price competition. No company-specific capacity figures were given.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.
Digital servicing capacity: digital interactions rose to 624K in Q1 FY27 from 214K in Q1 FY26; digital share of servicing was 69.0% in Q1 FY27 and 71.0% in June 2026.
Management did not discuss any new product launches, branch or distribution expansion, or timelines for system or platform commissioning.
demand_pricing: Industry Fire rates were cut sharply in the April renewal cycle; the reinsurance renewal was relatively soft, enabling capacity and competition.
Motor TP has seen no third-party price change for several years; the judgement adds a Motor TP loss ratio impact of 12-15% for the industry.

Digital interactions rose to 624K from 214K; digital share of servicing 69% in Q1 FY27 and 71% in June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹165 crore (₹1.65 bn) Motor TP provision only for Q1 business, and will it recur each quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the provision is a holistic assessment of exposures as at June 30, covering past book as well as Q1 business; it declined to say whether it will recur, citing variability in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the judgement affect closed cases, and what is the Fire loss ratio excluding the two large losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Closed cases typically do not reopen after court finality, so impact is largely on open exposures. Excluding the two large losses, Fire loss ratios should be within the historical 65-70% average range; the company has never exceeded 100% in Fire.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Health loss ratio rise despite GST benefit, and will it rise further in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects industry-wide higher claim incidence, similar to last year's Q1; it is watching monsoon-linked claims into Q2 and will update in October.

qa_highlights.question: Arbitration award of about ₹78 crore: provision and impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The award relates to a policy about seven to eight years old and is on a gross basis; the company will pursue legal remedies and believes the net P&L impact is not material given reinsurance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the reserve prudence buffer still generate releases given the ₹165 crore charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its reserving philosophy is unchanged, prudence will continue, and reserving triangles should continue to show favourable development over cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Why did commission and other opex ratios rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a higher retail mix, which carries higher acquisition cost but better loss outcomes, and said opex changes are business as usual.

540719|2026-06.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.

Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.
