540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Prop contributed ~70% of revenue but ~49% of consolidated FY26 profit (~52% standalone). Client turnover reportedly exceeded prop turnover (53% vs 47%) for the first time; target 60% client share of turnover by year-end.

segments.name: MTF (margin trading finance)
segments.commentary: MTF book grew from INR 239 crore (FY25) to INR 424 crore (FY26); Dec-25 level was INR 457 crore. FY27 target INR 650 crore; FY28 vision also cited as INR 650 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Reported NIM of 17.64% for FY26, roughly flat with FY25; management said NIM will decline as the book shifts to secured lending.

segments.name: uTrade (algo platform)
segments.commentary: Active clients crossed 5,000 in FY26 (5,231 currently); still small in revenue, with focus on adoption. Multi-broker plan slowed by a SEBI circular requiring vendors to set up separately for each broker.

segments.name: Wealth management and PMS
segments.commentary: PMS launched in Q4 FY26 with AUM above INR 100 crore; FY27 target INR 200 crore. Third-party distribution team under Charu Sehgal to start operations in Q3. AIF CAT-3 application filed with SEBI, approval expected by end-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 with six issues closed; FY27 target at least INR 500 crore of issues.

segments.name: Institutional business
segments.commentary: Institutional empanelments rose 35% from 137 to 186.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: NBFC, merchant banking, insurance and technology together contributed about 7% of FY26 bottom line. MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) cash segment doing INR 300-400 crore daily volume; Sizable stake held.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA ~38% (+/-2%) and PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) reaffirmed; management says no structural Q4 pressure.
MTF book target INR 650 crore by FY27, with mgmt saying INR 200 crore incremental is achievable if markets stay normal; deviation possible in low single digits on sentiment.
Target 30 new Tier-3 company-owned branches in next 2-3 years; 6 more targeted by FY27 year-end on top of 7 existing.
Prop share of profit targeted to fall to ~30% in three years; client share of turnover to reach 60% by FY27 year-end.
Share India Cred target INR 500 crore of issues in FY27; PMS AUM target INR 200 crore by FY27-end.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; expected to conclude within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Seven company-owned Tier-3 branches operating (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur), with six more targeted by end FY27.
Target of at least INR 10-15 crore MTF per Tier-3 branch per year; 30 branches implied INR 300-500 crore.
AIF CAT-3 approval awaited from SEBI; wealth-management operations to start Q3 FY27.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; post-merger plans include HFT trading.
MSCI exchange planning IPO segment, SME segment, and derivatives launch in FY27 (subject to approvals).
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 was volatile, with commodities (gold, silver, crude, natgas) driving turnover; cash ADTO rose to ~INR 2,000 crore in Q4 FY26 from ~INR 1,500 crore, and total ADTO rose to ~INR 4,500-5,000 crore from ~INR 1,400 crore in Q4 FY25 (figures as stated in call). Options were ~18% of Q4 ADTO.
MTF demand said to have risen in the last 1.5 months; Tier-3 pricing reportedly better because of less competition from sub-brokers.

RBI curbs: intraday bank limits for prop trading withdrawn; bank guarantees allowed for client business. Management estimates ~20% impact on overall deposits/limits used but minimal bottom-line effect; bank guarantees valid to 30 June can continue to expiry (up to March 2027).
SEBI market-making framework expected in 3-4 months; company is lobbying RBI for liquidity-provider relief.
Mgmt estimates INR 40,000-50,000 crore of capital to exit the market due to RBI curbs, which it expects to widen per-trade margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why do margins dip every March quarter and is that sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Q4 was weak in FY25 and FY26 due to volatile markets; management prefers annual view with EBITDA ~38% and PAT ~22% (+/-2%). Sachin Gupta said Q4 pressure is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: Status of uTrade multi-broker plans and monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said talks with Motilal Oswal and Dhan stalled after a SEBI circular requiring third-party vendors to set up infrastructure separately per broker, which is costly. No monetisation details were given.

qa_highlights.question: At what MTF AUM does the interest spread become meaningful, given borrowing costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said full-year borrowing costs will flow into FY27 and new NCD and third-party borrowing lines could cut costs by a few hundred basis points. Tier-3 direct branches are meant to remove mediators and lift NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Break up of brokerage vs prop income?
qa_highlights.answer: Prop contributes ~70% of revenue but ~49% of FY26 consolidated profit (52% standalone). Client turnover exceeded prop turnover for the first time (53% vs 47%).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI regulation on prop business and Market Maker regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated ~20% impact on limits used and minimal impact on bottom line. Company sought liquidity-provider status; the company is hybrid-classified and can continue bank guarantees until expiry (up to March 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Ballpark revenue diversification in the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 70% client and 30% prop share of profit over three years. Non-broking segments were ~7% of FY26 bottom line; detailed split not disclosed.

risks_watch: RBI curbs on prop intraday limits effective around 1 July 2026; watch for actual impact on prop turnover and margins versus the ~20% management estimate.
Consolidated PAT flat YoY due to fair value losses on group investments; recurrence risk.
NIM compression expected in NBFC as lending shifts to secured products; MTF book is cyclical with market sentiment.
Regulatory changes: SEBI vendor-per-broker circular hurts uTrade multi-broker plans; market-making framework still pending.
Silverleaf NCLT approval and AIF CAT-3 approval timing are uncertain.
540725|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and diversification, but defensive and hedged on the RBI prop curbs and market-dependent targets. Management repeatedly stressed that targets depend on normal markets and geopolitical stability.
key_quotes: So, the Company should be able to continue with the current margins. There is nothing like Q4 type of pressure on us.

540725|2026-06.headline: Share India Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 48% YoY to Rs 124.41 crore on revenue of Rs 448 crore; management targets ~20% growth this year.

Standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 349 crore and PAT rose 32% to Rs 90.85 crore; consolidated revenue rose 31% to Rs 448 crore and PAT rose 48% to Rs 124.41 crore, with consolidated PAT up 114% QoQ. Growth was attributed to MTF lending income, new subsidiaries (Share India Cred, GIFT City), PMS launch and merchant banking. Management plans CP and NCD issuance to offset funding constraints.

financial_highlights.value: Rs ~74 crore across six issues; EBITDA Rs 1.08 crore; PAT Rs 40 lakh

segments.commentary: MTF book ~Rs 470 crore at end Q1, targeted at Rs 1,000 crore in two years; management called MTF the main source of sustainable interest income.

segments.name: PMS / wealth

guidance_outlook: Management expects ~20% growth in the current financial year, subject to market conditions.

AIF launch expected in Q3 FY27 pending regulatory approval; wealth distribution operations also targeted from Q3 FY27.
PMS AUM target ~Rs 250 crore by financial year end.
Plans to issue commercial paper (rated Crisil A1+) and NCDs to diversify funding; CP programme initiated.
capex_capacity: Seven new branches opened recently against a 30-branch target over two years; branches rolled out in tranches of about eight.

AI, automation and in-house platform Techyon cited as technology investments.

Mid and small-cap volatility affected MTF book; management said it held its numbers with mild growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback period for Tier-3 branches given lower ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said each branch should reach break-even in ~8 months by building a Rs 15 crore MTF book; branches not profitable after 12 months will be closed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock underperforming despite low PE and high growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, attributing it to industry regulatory consolidation and cited diversification, institutional clients and subsidiaries as positives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of acquiring Silverleaf, the tech company?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Silverleaf (founded by IIT Bombay graduates, 12+ years in business) brings a technology stack and HFT protocols, supporting third-country expansion and back-end technology.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking and trading performance and what is the prop vs broking split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business has shifted toward lending via MTF (~Rs 465-470 crore) and fee streams from PMS, MF distribution and third-party products; prop contributes ~52% of profit and broking ~48%.

qa_highlights.question: Why pay up to Rs 45 crore for Enshrine, a company with Rs 2-3 crore turnover?

qa_highlights.question: Is prop still a very high share of total revenue and PAT?

Stock underperformance despite strong earnings; management attributed this to sector consolidation and external factors.

540735|2026-03.headline: IRIS RegTech targets INR500 crore revenue, needing ~30%+ growth over 4-5 years; FY26 revenue grew ~23% with EBITDA margin ~14%.
540735|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as steady: total revenue grew about 23% and EBITDA margin was about 14%, with management asking analysts to judge the business on annual rather than quarterly numbers. IRIS CARBON ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins and iDEAL ARR grew 17%, while SupTech added 3 new logos including the Government of Qatar. Post the TaxTech divestment, cash was about INR155 crore and net worth rose to INR200 crore from INR76 crore. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue aspiration and said the Middle East crisis is a watch item rather than a current drag.

financial_highlights.change: From INR76 crore as at March 31, 2025
Delayed Indian customer decisions in H1 FY26

Sales and marketing spend is planned to be stepped up in a measured way, at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, and kept EBITDA positive.

segments.name: RegTech - IRIS iDEAL (BFSI automated regulatory reporting)

segments.commentary: Spun off into a subsidiary for sharper focus. Loan facilitation piloted from February 2026 with 3 lenders onboarded so far; monetisation is at an early stage and management's internal target is earlier than the 2-year horizon an analyst suggested.

SaaS ARR growth target of about 35% (stated externally), with management saying internally it could be higher.
SupTech expected to grow at a lower rate than SaaS, with possible lumpy upside.

qa_highlights.answer: SaaS impact seen as minimal given Europe and US focus. SupTech pipeline linked to Middle East regulators could see delays if the crisis persists beyond roughly June; 3-4 SupTech wins still expected.

540743|2026-03.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore; FY27 guidance is early double-digit revenue and mid-teens PBT growth.
540743|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore and PBT before exceptional items rose 16.8% to INR87 crore, driven by volume growth and better mix. For FY26, revenue crossed INR10,000 crore at INR10,233 crore (+9%) and PBT before exceptionals rose 17.2% to INR569 crore. Animal Nutrition volumes grew 15% in Q4, Astec reached EBITDA break-even for the year, and Crop Care was hit by co-marketing channel inventory carry-forward. Management guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth for FY27, with the Iran war and a weak monsoon forecast flagged as variables.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, well ahead of industry; cattle feed +24%. Margins expanded, helped by new Type 1 products, East and Central share gains, raw material cost reconfiguration, and a ~INR9.5 crore pet food manufacturing income booked in other income.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: FY26 marked by record area expansion, strong volume growth and an all-time high oil extraction ratio. Q4 is seasonally weak (~60,000 t of FFB out of 6.37 lakh t annually) but margins held. Specialty fat refinery to start rolling out in May 2026.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Q4 hit by carry-forward of co-marketing channel inventory, lowering in-house volumes; partly offset by specialty products. FY27 is guided as a recovery year, with recovery from Q2 and very high double-digit growth in top and bottom line.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Achieved EBITDA break-even in FY26; Q4 revenue and EBITDA grew strongly on CDMO volumes, realisations and utilisation. FY26 mix was ~48% enterprise and ~52% CDMO; exports ~53% of revenue. Board reconstituted with Arijit Mukherjee as Executive Director.

segments.name: Creamline Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~5% YoY ex bulk sales in Q4; profitability pressured by elevated milk procurement costs. Management expects milk prices to ease gradually from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: EBITDA margins improved significantly in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded revenue salience above 80% in FY26. Live Bird trading is being phased out; momos and frozen chicken entries planned.

So this is a very small part which comes in this. So it's a very marginal quarter for OPB business per se, but the good part is we were at a 19.76% last year on OER in the same quarter.
540743|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 volume-led growth and Animal Nutrition, and on oil palm and Astec. Cautious and evasive on the monsoon, palm oil prices, and the Astec structure, where management said it is too early to decide.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

financial_highlights.change: Cattle feed volume +15%; total segment volume +7%
Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)
vs EBITDA loss of INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
Value-added share of sales 49% vs 42% a year ago

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

qa_highlights.question: What FFB volume growth and EBITDA trajectory can Oil Palm deliver over 3-5 years, and what capex and returns are involved in value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kataria guided FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over 4-5 years, targeting double digit; specialty fats refinery to start in September, with a 16-18% IRR hurdle and about 200 bps EBITDA uplift at scale. He did not give an explicit EBITDA number.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was hit by a 40% June deficit; July is better than last year's base, and it will decide on the recovery by end-September. Consolidated growth now targeted at double digit, with the exact level to be given by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Arijit Mukherjee said FY27 revenue growth is now expected at more than 20%, with the 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO margins intact and enterprise margin normalising as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex stays within the INR300-350 crore envelope already guided. Dairy volume grew 8% but packaging and milk costs hit margin; Foods B2C is in a 3-4 year investment phase, with live bird trading being wound down.

qa_highlights.question: How much maize inflation has Animal Nutrition passed through, and what is EBIT per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of commodity cost increases passed on; EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150, with Q1 EBITDA per tonne in that range or slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Oil Palm segment margin fall from 19% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to a one-off pricing-formula change in the quarter and flat FFB, offset by better OER; expects margins to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Crop Care lagging peers, and what are margins on the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is segment-mix and macro driven (cotton herbicide concentration), not share loss; new products carry lower margin than Hitweed but healthy, with total Crop Care EBIT margin seen at about 26-27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated PBT growth: management still targets double-digit growth, narrowed from the earlier mid-teens guidance; exact position in the range to be given by end-September (end Q2).

Astec LifeSciences: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20% (up from the ~20% earlier guidance); Q1 revenue dip of 8-9% to be recovered in later quarters; CDMO dissilience around 50-52% for the year, with some CDMO shift from H1 to H2.
Astec enterprise margin: Q1 benefited from low-priced raw material and war-driven finished goods price increases; prices now easing, margin normalising. CDMO margins intact.

Oil Palm: FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over the next 4-5 years (LRP); management says it targets double digit; full-year FFB growth guided at high single digit to double digit; margin drop expected to even out over the year.
Animal Nutrition: EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150 per tonne.
Crop Care: no firm FY27 numbers; recovery quantum to be assessed by end-September after cotton herbicide season. Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite tough year.

Dairy: milk procurement prices expected to stay at current elevated levels for 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation expected to ease by August; some impact may persist in Q2; cost initiatives to be doubled down on in H2.
Godrej Foods: live bird trading to decline 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years; branded B2C to be in investment phase for 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Overall business-level capex guidance of roughly INR300-350 crore, phased over 3-4 quarters; includes the integrated palm oil complex (phase 1 started, nursery and CPO mill; seed garden in 18-24 months; refinery later) and specialty fats refinery (rollout late August/early September 2026); management says no new investment beyond this envelope.

Oil Palm area expansion: added about 17,000 hectares last year and on track to repeat this year; LRP target to take area from about 80,000 ha to about 150,000 ha, with Telangana and Northeast expansion; about 50% of plantations are juvenile (0-4 years).
New capex hurdle: IRR of around 16-18% required for new assets; management says the specialty fats downstream business, when scaled, adds roughly 200 bps to overall EBITDA profile.

Godrej Foods: investments in automation of plants and advertising behind branded B2C; NPD pipeline including chicken momos (launched about 4 months ago) and wet momos (planned in 3-4 months), and frozen chicken category push.
demand_pricing: Animal Nutrition: revenue +12.6% on demand and realisations; cattle feed volume +15%, fish feed volume up ~20%+ (about 7% of segment), cattle feed about 55-56% of segment; total segment volume +7% as poultry was deliberately cut in unprofitable geographies. Management says it passed on about 60-70% of commodity (maize) inflation.

Oil Palm: revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations; oil extraction ratio 18.8% vs 18.4%; FFB volume broadly flat against a strong early-monsoon base last year. Segment margin dipped on a pricing-formula change that management calls one-off.

Crop Care: revenue -16.2% on a 40% June rainfall deficit delaying sowing; cotton herbicide volume hit. Ashitaka (maize) and Takai (paddy insecticide) together 18-20% of Q1 sales; July said to be better than last year's base. Management said no share loss to competitors; cited product-mix differences versus peers.

Dairy (CDPL): volume +8% and value +11.5%; value-added share 49% vs 42%. Packaging inflation (linked to crude/LPG after Middle East conflict) and milk procurement prices hurt margin; industry passed on about 70% of price increases.

Godrej Foods: B2C (Yummiez and Real Good) volumes +28% (Yummiez +22%), about 32% of Foods business; overall Foods revenue only about 1-2% growth due to planned live bird decline; B2C value growth about 20%.
Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet): strong double-digit growth in volume, value and PBT under new leadership.
risks_watch: Crop Care recovery depends on the cotton herbicide season and erratic rainfall; management will give a firm view only by end-September.
Dairy margin pressure from elevated milk procurement prices (expected to persist 2-3 quarters) and packaging costs, with some impact likely in Q2.
Oil Palm Q1 margin decline (19% to 17% EBIT) attributed to a pricing formula; watch whether H2 margin recovers as management expects.
Astec: CDMO revenue shifting from H1 into H2, and the 8-9% Q1 dip must be recovered to hit the more-than-20% FY27 target.
Animal Nutrition: poultry volume cuts and maize cost volatility; the segment reported volume growth (+7%) lags cattle feed (+15%).
Godrej Foods reported top line stays near flat (1-2%) while B2C invests; profitability is pressured by input costs and the investment phase.
key_quotes: So I would say, yes, there has been a hit in the quarter 1, which has very clearly come because of this weather pattern.
Nothing crosses our bridge broadly beyond -- until we are doing an IRR of around 16% to 18%, and this meets that bridge for us.
But I think one thing we're still pretty confident of is that we'll be able to target a double -digit growth still.
We have a tight filter on this very clearly. This is a high ROCE business for us.
540743|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Oil Palm, Animal Nutrition and Astec, but cautious on Crop Care and the consolidated guidance, which management says will be narrowed only at end-September. Several answers stressed one-off factors (packaging, pricing formula, weather) while deferring specifics on Crop Care and dairy margins.

540749|2026-03.headline: MAS Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 25% YoY to INR104 crore, with AUM at INR15,304 crore, up 19%.
540749|2026-03.overview: Consolidated PAT for Q4 FY26 was INR104 crore versus INR83 crore a year earlier, and full-year PAT was INR379 crore, up 21%. Standalone AUM grew 18.71% and standalone PAT grew 23.39% YoY in the quarter to around INR100 crore. Standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, slightly better than 1.72% in December 2025, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%. Cost of borrowing fell 42 bps YoY to 9.39%, and management guided to 9.20-9.25% over the next two to three quarters. Credit cost was elevated because of deliberate aggressive write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, which management said were funded from profit.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Micro-enterprise loans (MEL)
segments.commentary: AUM rose about 20% to INR5,737 crore from INR4,793 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - SME loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 15.78% to INR5,213 crore from INR4,502 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: AUM grew 35.43% to INR1,063 crore from INR785 crore; yields cited at 19-23%.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: AUM grew 11% to INR1,085 crore from INR979 crore; growth being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Salaried personal loan
segments.commentary: AUM grew around 22% to INR1,264 crore from INR1,040 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM rose 22.41% to INR940 crore from INR768 crore; Q4 PAT INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, net Stage 3 0.68%. Management aims for INR1,000 crore, now about a quarter later than planned.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% on a sustained basis; long-term target of INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036.
Credit cost guided at 1-1.25% of closing AUM statistically, with management indicating about 1.25-1.3% on closing AUM, and up to about 1.5% in quarters with aggressive write-offs.
Cost-to-NII guided at 35-37%; ROA after opex and credit cost targeted at 2.75-3%.
Yield range-bound at 16-17%, expected to be sustained into FY27.
Cost of borrowing guided to fall from 9.39% to around 9.20-9.25% over the next 2-3 quarters.
Branch additions of 30-35 planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches.
Dividend: final dividend INR0.75 per share, total INR2 per share for FY26, about 10% payout.
Capital adequacy to be maintained at around 20%; debt tie-up for about half of FY27 done, full-year tie-up expected soon.
capex_capacity: More than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres; branch network to grow by 30-35 in FY27.
Average cash and cash equivalent balance of about INR1,000 crore plus unutilised cash credit of over INR200 crore.
Cash credit facility of about INR1,500 crore across 14 banks, utilised at 70-75%.
Sanctioned facilities over INR2,000 crore as of 31 March (term loans, NCDs, direct assignment, co-lending).
Term loan sanctioned pipeline of about INR1,300 crore; INR750 crore term loan raised in Q4 at 3-5 year tenor; INR100 crore NCDs raised in Q4.
Direct assignment of INR940 crore executed in Q4; a further INR500 crore+ of direct assignment and co-lending sanctions to be used in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Direct sourcing is about 64% of the book; fintech partnerships are about 10% of business.
Yield rose about 40 bps sequentially, attributed to fintech mix and 2-wheeler growth; SME yields were also higher.
Management said assignment income is amortised, not upfront, and the NII rise was mainly from lower borrowing cost and the MCLR reset.
Standalone 90+ write-offs were aggressive in FY26 (more than 0.10% of assets), mostly unsecured per management.
Caution list added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters and some chemical industries in Feb-March 2026, alongside textile and agro, due to West Asia supply concerns.
Management reported no slowdown in disbursement growth as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is MAS using data and AI for risk-adjusted growth, and what early warning systems exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it back-tests risk models on its own repayment experience, not generic bureau scores; it moved from LOS to business rule engines and plans AI-based risk management after 6-9 months. Field checks included more than 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after the Middle East crisis, plus bounce data from 100% bank or e-NACH collections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis and inflation affect lending and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset quality should hold but is being watched closely; it is growing CV more slowly as an energy- and logistics-linked precaution. Disbursement growth has not slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of borrowing and the Q4 cost of borrowing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowing is 9.39% and is expected to fall to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters. Q4 interest expense was about INR222 crore vs INR219 crore in Q3, with the MCLR reset adding to NII.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the origination and fee cost high, and what is driving opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fees and commission depend on product structure. Fintech partners get the spread as commission, and yields rose about 0.5%. Opex is judged against ROA, not in isolation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise was from deliberate write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, not stress. Normal credit cost is 1-1.25% of closing AUM; 1.5% is possible in quarters with aggressive write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CV growth slow, and what is the write-off and recovery policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is slowing CV growth for 1-2 quarters due to logistics and transport risk. Write-offs occur after 360 days across all products; recoveries are credited to P&L net.

risks_watch: Rising inflation and energy costs from the West Asia crisis could hit logistics, transport and fuel-linked MSMEs.
Credit cost is a function of aggressive write-off policy; quarterly credit costs could run towards 1.5%.
Pricing may need to be passed on to borrowers if borrowing costs fall, which could compress the yield gain.
Housing finance subsidiary's INR1,000 crore AUM target now slips about a quarter.
Debt tie-up for FY27 is only about half complete; rate reduction depends on market conditions.
Gross Stage 3 is at 2.57%, up slightly QoQ.
540749|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with a clear 20-25% AUM growth target. Cautious on the macro, with CV growth slowed and sector caution lists expanded. Management was less direct on the split of NII growth and on the detail of the write-off strategy.
key_quotes: And on the asset side, we continue to have the confidence to grow anywhere between 20% to 25%, given the positive macro situation because we always prioritize risk management and profitability over just the growth.
So, we are at a striking distance away from INR1,000 crores.
We have cash credit facility of approximately INR1500 crore spread over 14 banks, of which we maintain utilization level of around 70 %-75%, keeping the remaining portion as liquidity buffer.
So, we do not upfront income in order to improve the profitability or the NII growth.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.name: MEL (Micro/MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Book grew 23% from INR5,009 crores to INR6,153 crores; MEL is about 77% of loan book combined with SME.

segments.name: SME loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR4,526 crores to INR5,485 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: Grew 19% from INR872 crores to INR1,039 crores; management said Q1 is seasonally muted, with festive Q3/Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (used CV)
segments.commentary: Grew 13% from INR967 crores to INR1,096 crores; eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening, with growth push deferred 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR1,131 crores to INR1,374 crores; about 9% of the loan book.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.
Borrowing cost: 9.25% average with incremental cost at 9.2%-9.3%; a sub-9% level is called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters, and the credit rating upgrade has no timing.

Off-book share fell below the 20%-25% target this quarter; management says it is opportunistic and the target is unchanged. Gujarat floods and monsoon effects on two-wheeler and collections are still unquantified.
key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.
So, that is the impact which translates to roughly around between INR5 crores to INR7 crores in provisioning.
Difficult to comment right now because the cost of borrowing is dependent on the macro situation.
So, currently, sub-9 immediately within next 1 or 2 quarters looks like a far -fetched assumption.
540749|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, profitability and asset quality, with the 20%-25% AUM guidance reaffirmed and the upper end targeted. More cautious and non-committal on credit cost trajectory, borrowing cost, used CV recovery timing and the flood impact, where management repeatedly said it cannot yet predict or quantify.

540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why has RTM grown to near DAM size in India, unlike in Europe where DAM dominates?

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for final market coupling regulations, and what is the expected DAM market-share loss?

qa_highlights.question: Does the market coupling challenge affect CERC approval of the new products?

qa_highlights.question: Why did REC volumes fall about 80% YoY and QoQ, and why is standalone realisation per unit down sharply?

540879|2026-06.headline: Apollo Micro Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% YoY to INR156 crores, while consolidated revenue jumped 88% to INR251 crores; standalone PAT up 43% to INR28 crores.

540900|2026-03.headline: Newgen FY26 revenue rose 6% to INR1,574 crore and Q4 rose 5.3% to INR457 crore, while management declined to guide FY27 growth.

Q4 revenue was INR457 crore against INR430 crore in Q4 FY25, with Q4 SaaS up 44%. Profit after tax was INR301 crore reported, or INR334 crore excluding a one-time Labour Code impact and a INR42 crore legal provision; management described the adjusted PAT as up 6% and the adjusted net margin as 21.3%. Large-deal closures slowed in India, Middle East and EMEA on geopolitical uncertainty and decision delays, and management withheld a FY27 growth number, asking for one more quarter of visibility.

demand_pricing: Industry view: RAC volumes were down about 30% in Q1 and Q2 FY26 and recovered in Q3-Q4, leaving FY26 roughly flat. Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for FY27.

Price increases of about 14% YoY on finished goods: one in January 2026 from the star-rating change and one in April 2026 for commodity costs. Copper clad laminate prices are up more than 60% in one year and still rising; gold is up about 60%.
PCB pricing: Tier 1 EMS pass-through works on a quarterly lag, but PCB (Tier 2) has about a two-quarter lag. Two price increases of about 15% and 18% have been received, with more under negotiation.
Compressor import relief: government allowed imports of about 30% of last year's volumes for compressors below 2 tonne, extended for a year. Management says there is no compressor shortage.
Electronics margin pressure: PCBA about 5% and PCB about 12-13% versus a normal 16-17%. Management expects the price increases to flow through over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RAC industry growth expectations for Q1 and FY27, and which segments face margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for the full year. Margin pressure comes from minimum wage hikes (35% in Haryana, about 22% in UP), CCL and gold costs, and currency depreciation. Indian Railway fixed-price contracts cannot pass costs through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-12% price increase reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases are about 14% YoY, from a January star-rating change and an April commodity-driven hike.

qa_highlights.question: Will compressor shortages hurt FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there is no shortage. Five new domestic manufacturers have come up, and imports of 30% of last year's volumes are allowed. Commercial AC compressors are still largely imported.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Consumer Durables finished-goods share rise, and is it realisation-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods rose because gas-charging customers moved to ODM solutions, not because of realisation. Finished goods fell from about 80% at listing in FY18 to about 40% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCB versus PCBA mix and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 Electronics: PCBA about INR2,281 crore at about 5% margin; PCB about INR600 crore at 12-13%; Power-One about 15% margin; Unitronics not disclosed as it is listed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and net cash outflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 gross capex INR1,800-2,000 crore with cash outflow of about INR1,100-1,200 crore. FY28 cash outflow of about INR1,400-1,500 crore.

risks_watch: FY27 margin squeeze of 50-100 bps from commodity inflation, currency depreciation and minimum wage revisions in UP, Haryana and other states.
PCB price pass-through lag of about two quarters and the Tier 2 position, which limit near-term recovery.
Net debt rising to INR700-800 crore by March 2027 while capex is heavy; working capital days up to 29 from 9 due to inventory build.
Ascent Hosur construction delay (about one quarter) and Ascent-K HDI timelines; subsidies arrive with a 5-6 year lag.
Non-controlling interest from CCPS: auditors assumed about 30% dilution as a maximum, with actual dilution expected to be lower; NCI remains a balance-sheet item.
Electronics customer shifts from purchase to job-work could cause organic top-line volatility; organic growth was subdued in Q4.
540902|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, with an explicit caution on near-term margins. Management was candid about the 50-100 bps FY27 squeeze and the PCB lag, and gave specific numbers for capex and cash flow. Management declined to give Unitronics-level detail because it is listed.
key_quotes: So our endeavor on going towards the value side of the businesses is because in B2B business, what we are trying to attempt is we are trying to balance the left and right.
To sum up, we expect a margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps at consolidated level, which is of temporary in nature and expected to normalize as macro environment improves.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Santhosh Seshadri (Avendus) asked about Oppo mobile export discussions, PLI eligibility, and PCB fixed-price contract exposure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export talks with Oppo are early and export would be considered after one year of domestic production; three ECMS approvals (INR3,200 crore Jewar, about INR1,000 crore Hosur, INR500 crore Shogini) are in place; PCB pass-through runs on a two-quarter lag as tier-2 supplier, with some customers already raising prices in July. Draft PLI guidelines are awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia (Investec) asked whether Q1 consumer durable margins reflected raw material inflation and inventory benefit, and about H1 margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement and a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne), which will not be annualised. He said margins are not expected to compress and the full-year outlook remains in line with projections.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia asked about the operational impact of the IL JIN incident.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said reconstruction permission was received the previous day and assessment is under way. Guided numbers for the quarter are still expected to be met, and exchanges will be informed.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruv Jain (Ambit) asked why Electronics growth looks lower excluding acquisitions, and about FY27 guidance and railway margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Arora said EMS growth slowed because customers destocked and some shifted to job work, and smart meter and smart watch segments declined; full-year EMS guidance is intact. For Railways, Jasbir Singh guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and margin of 15-16%, citing fixed-price railway contracts and first trains supplied through a principal.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Lahoti (HDFC Securities) asked why minority interest swung from INR28 crore positive to INR19 crore negative, and about the IL JIN incident impact.
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Goyal said the swing was checked later: the INR123 crore exceptional loss sits in Electronics entities with minority holders, pushing the minority share negative. Jasbir Singh said assets are insured, production has shifted to other IL JIN locations, and the impact will be quantified within a week.

qa_highlights.question: Sameet Sinha (Macquarie) asked about input cost pass-through timing and local CCL manufacturing.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said consumer durable is tier 1 with a one-quarter lag, while PCB is tier 2 with a two-quarter lag, so pass-through starts from Q4. A first Wipro CCL plant is nearly operational, two more are planned, and Amber is in JV talks targeting own CCL plants by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama) asked about PCB margin quantum, next-two-quarter margin path, and drivers of the 40% Electronics growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said normalised PCB margin is about 16% versus about 12% now, with Q2 still impacted and recovery from Q3 to a 15-16% range, subject to no further CCL price rises. All three Electronics divisions (PCBA, PCB, industrial power electronics) are expected to drive the 40% growth. Sudhir Goyal said a group-level minority percentage cannot be given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavik Mehta (JP Morgan) asked whether the consumer durable industry growth and the 50-100 bps FY27 margin decline guidance still hold, and the timing of Oppo revenue recognition clarity.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said consumer durable growth is in line with industry, cited at 13-15%. Jasbir Singh said the 50-100 bps decline is moderated, with margins normalising absent further currency or commodity disruption. Oppo revenue-recognition clarity is expected in 15-20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) asked about Oppo revenue booking entity, minority stake in IL JIN, and consolidated net debt.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said the booking entity (IL JIN or Amber) depends on ERP integration and will be formalised before mid-September. Sudhir Goyal said minority is computed on a diluted basis of about 60% with about 39-40% treated as minority interest, and net debt was about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about INR510 crore at March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Agarwal (IKIGAI) asked for an entity-wise Electronics revenue build-up over three years.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh declined a three-year number, citing asset turn of 0.8:1 and the capex plan (Jewar INR3,200 crore, Hosur INR1,000 crore). Power electronics is guided to grow 35-40%, and the Electronics TAM is $16-17 billion today, estimated at $35-40 billion by FY30. He did not accept the INR5,000 crore consolidated electronics sales framing.

risks_watch: IL JIN facility incident: final loss quantification and insurance recovery still pending; management promised an update within a week and a reassessment of the guided numbers.
PCB margin recovery depends on customer price pass-through and no further CCL price increases; Q2 FY27 is expected to remain impacted at about 12% margin versus about 16% normal.
Q1 consumer durable margin benefited from pre-stocking and a premium mix that management said will not be annualised; watch for normalisation as the BEE tonnage labelling mix clears by Diwali.

Net debt rose to about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 from about INR510 crore at March 2026, alongside a fundraise enabling resolution of up to INR5,000 crore at IL JIN with quantum and form undecided.
Oppo mobile: revenue-recognition model (IL JIN vs Amber level) to be decided by mid-September; PLI eligibility depends on draft guidelines not yet issued; trial production targeted for Q4 FY27.
Minority interest swung to negative INR19 crore from positive INR28 crore; the adjusted minority figure was not provided on the call and was to be calculated later.
key_quotes: But what we have seen in July is that there are some customers who have increased the cost. So our margins are coming back to where it was.
But let me tell everybody on the call that the guided number of what we did last quarter, we are hopeful that we should be in line to deliver despite of this disruption.
So we are not looking at any margin compression.
But only subject to no further CCL price increases are happening.
540902|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, the Oppo project, and the 40% Electronics and 30-35% Railways guidance, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, the IL JIN impact, and any quantified multi-year targets. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on consumer durable margins, three-year revenue build-up, and group minority allocation, citing volatility.

540935|2026-03.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR122 crore (from INR135 crore) and EBITDA/MT to INR20,114; Q1 FY27 guided to high end of 6-8% volume growth.
540935|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by West Asia war disruptions to logistics, feedstock availability and customer ordering, with Egypt operations stalled through March. EBITDA declined year-on-year to INR122 crore and EBITDA per metric ton to INR20,114 from INR21,715. India volumes grew 8% YoY in Q4 while AMET volumes fell 15% and RoW fell 7%, with the Americas a relative bright spot after US tariff reversals. Management guided only for Q1 FY27 (high end of 6-8% volume growth and high end of INR19,000-21,000/MT EBITDA), declining to give full-year guidance given the uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Why was specialty revenue flat QoQ (INR493 crore to INR498 crore) despite US tariff reversal, and how big is India's specialty mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat QoQ figure to product mix in US Q4 as products were shifted after tariff reversal. India specialty base is small, but D2C brands are growing their presence and use specialty ingredients.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term specialty mix outlook and the outlook for FY27-28 volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to grow both segments, expects a 60:40 to 70:30 range depending on performance, and still sees 60:40 to 65:35 by 2031. No FY27-28 volume guidance beyond Q1 given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and pass-through, and the risk of down-trading?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Egypt facility's status on raw materials, logistics and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand not a challenge; March was disrupted by stuck inbound materials. Operations restored from mid-April, and management expects May and June to run uninterrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Q1 volume guidance rely mainly on supply constraints at competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; the guidance is driven by India recovery to 8-10% growth, US business revival and AMET supply recovery, with a caveat that the outlook holds only if current conditions do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AMET fallen from ~90,000 MT to ~60,000 MT and what is the market outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Local backward-integrated players gained share; Egypt plant idle in March. Management said AMET has likely bottomed, with market growth of about 3-4%.

540935|2026-06.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
540935|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the specialty share decline from about 40% to 34% a concern?

qa_highlights.question: Will AMET return to positive volume growth in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of reformulation reversing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reformulation remains favourable while petrochemical and oleochemical balance holds; it does not see a big risk currently but will monitor coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 22–23/kg gross margin or INR 25/kg EBITDA a steady-state base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the structure has improved but said it wants at least one more quarter before changing long-term guidance, to avoid overpromising.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pricing gain is from finished-goods inventory spikes or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight costs, mix shift toward dry (100%/95% active) products, and the reformulation mix all lifted realisations; it declined to quantify the ASP increase excluding these.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and Indonesia's biodiesel mandate?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is around USD 1,100–1,200/MT and the mandate is largely priced in; fatty alcohol expected to hold at INR 2,600–2,800 on a sideways basis, with El Nino a possible supply-side risk for next year.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to about 32% depends on inflation easing; copper touches new highs about every two weeks and steel moved from about 65 to above 80.

Working capital at 34 days versus target of about 20 days; receivables rising with DTM expansion.
Wires expansion is limited to North, East and parts of South; pan-India launch not yet done.
Project Sanchay savings need to step up in H2 to beat FY26 full-year level of about INR70 crores.
Hyderabad plant utilisation at about 40% on single shift.

qa_highlights.question: Root cause of the July 2025 EU GMP failure and reinspection scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to data-integrity observations on EudraGMDP, over-reliance on manual documentation, and said CAPA added digitalisation, e-logbooks and tightened QA; the process was overseen by consultants over six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differential and revenue on the alternate CMO for Star Product 1?

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% EBITDA margin achievable in 24-36 months, and is 17-product scale-up feasible without more capex?

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q4 licensing fee income absent and when does it resume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said licensing milestones tied to EU GMP (dossier submission and MA) stopped; they should resume once EU GMP is restored.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 'draft report' and disclosure of inspection observations?

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will sales follow EU-GMP approval, and what growth is expected in FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Is the price hike a one-off, how large is it, and does it come with scheme rollbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide hike after about 2 years: 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June, total about 4-6% (CFO cited 6-7%). It is a pure price increase; schemes and discounts are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be substantially reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt can be reduced to zero by FY28; about INR50 crore of short- and long-term borrowings were repaid last year. Management expects further cash from a 5-7 day cycle reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin decline, cotton or competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mix (economy at 47%) and yarn costs were the main factors; prices were unchanged while realisation fell. Management denied meaningful discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the economy-segment shift structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is temporary, citing high demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, formalisation from unorganised players, and advertising of Dollar Lehar from the past three years. Force NXT grew 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin return to double digits and what is the FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins should be better than FY26 and it is eyeing double-digit growth, but gave no specific number and deferred guidance to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working-capital outlook?
