The call flagged the planned ramp-down of two large SDV programs (one with a European OEM, one a surprise stop by a Japanese OEM after Honda cancelled new platforms in April), which will weigh on Q1 FY27 revenue by an estimated 3-4% QoQ. Management guided FY27 EBITDA to 20.5-21.2% and a medium-term 22-24% margin, with solutions and products growing 30% a year.

financial_highlights.metric: Total contract value (TCV) won in Q4

financial_highlights.value: Up 18% YoY in FY26; up 11.6% in Q4

segments.name: Trucks and off-highway
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY in FY26 and led Q4 growth at 11.6%. Added 4 truck OEMs and 6 off-highway OEMs across four countries in the year.

segments.name: Connected vehicles and cloud-based connected services
segments.commentary: Cited as the second growth driver in Q4 and the highest-growth area in the industry, per management.

segments.name: Powertrain
segments.commentary: Continued to grow across electrification, hybrid, conventional and hydrogen pilots, though slower than the top segments.

segments.name: Vehicle engineering (Caresoft)
segments.commentary: Expanded beyond software into cost reduction and software benchmarking; positioned for off-highway and cost-reduction work.

segments.name: After-sales
segments.commentary: Called a fast-growing area with 9% YoY growth from OEM clients; Tier 1 revenue declined from a non-focus base.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 20.5-21.2%, after higher investment in AI solutions, products, and new markets; currency movements add uncertainty.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 22-24%, driven by solutions and products mix, fixed-price and outcome-based contracts, and per-person productivity.
Solutions and products revenue expected to grow about 30% YoY, rising from 15% of revenue to 40% in three years (management also cited a 50%-plus share as a longer-term goal).
Two large SDV programs ending; management expects the revenue gap to be covered by new accounts, with FY27 sequential growth of 4-5% lost versus the prior plan.
India revenue (about 4% of total) expected to roughly double in FY27; medium-term target of double-digit annualised growth.
Truck and off-highway spend expected to pick up in H2 CY2026 with pre-buying; management expects the T40 account base to become more balanced across segments.
capex_capacity: R&D investment held at above 5% of revenue, with partner and acquisition investments (about $400 million cited) on top of that.
Ecosystem partnerships with Qualcomm, Microsoft, Qorix (middleware), Helm.ai (autonomy), Pathpartner, Technica, Cymotive and Caresoft.
Beacon AI platform used internally across about 13,000 staff and licensable as a product.
Two new Chinese OEM engagements won; China presence refreshed, with revenue still small.
New partnership with Hero Motors for micromobility, launched from India.
demand_pricing: Management said it had about 10-11% market share and that wallet share among the top 25 clients (T25) was about 10% last year, targeted to rise to 15-20%.
More than 80% of new contracts are fixed-price; four of the largest clients to convert to outcome-based models in Q4 and the next four in Q1 FY27, taking that share above 75%.
Added 13 new clients in FY26 (4 truck, 6 off-highway, 3 passenger car OEMs), with a large North American off-highway OEM awarding a SDV program.
OEM spend outlook: McKinsey data (Jan 2026) shows automotive R&D spend growing about 2x by 2030, led by AD/ADAS (about 3x); management said its addressable share is smaller.
Management said no OEM has yet cut spending due to the Middle East conflict and oil prices, though a conflict beyond 3-6 months could hit trucks first.

qa_highlights.question: How will AD/ADAS progress for a legacy supplier when much of the new spend goes to new-age OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said legacy OEMs are sourcing autonomy from new partners (e.g. Momenta, Helm), and KPIT's opportunity is validation and simulation, plus off-highway autonomy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap to cover in FY27 from the 4-5% sequential growth lost to program ramp-down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is 3-4% of quarterly revenue, starting Q1 FY27, and it expects to cover it with pipeline in existing clients and new accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the move to a 22-24% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Products and solutions carry higher gross margins, reusable assets and AI-infused work improve margins, fixed-price conversion helps, and AI lowers SG&A.

qa_highlights.question: How does KPIT compete with Chinese automotive engineering firms that run lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said KPIT competes favourably outside China and already sells products to top China OEMs; Sachin said China's advantage is EV platforms and batteries, which are complementary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 TCV jump, and is that repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said the jump came from off-highway commercial wins and traditional clients; Sachin said quarterly variability is normal but half-yearly and yearly TCV is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Do European and North American OEMs plan to increase SDV spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin said European OEMs are focused on cutting cost and reconsidering partners, creating opportunities, while US OEMs are investing in next-generation SDVs.

risks_watch: Revenue loss from the two SDV program ramp-downs (one a planned European OEM program, one a Japanese OEM program stopped near production) hits Q1 FY27, with 3-4% quarterly impact.
Delivery of FY27 EBITDA guidance of 20.5-21.2% while investing in AI and new markets, with currency swings a stated risk.
Pace of solutions and products growth (30% target) and conversion of the four largest clients to outcome-based contracts in Q4 and Q1.
Middleware (Qorix) and autonomous driving revenue delayed by architecture program slippage, with a 1-2 year lag.
Macro risk: Middle East conflict and oil prices could affect truck and off-highway spend if they persist beyond 3-6 months.
542651|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term story and pipeline, but cautious on near-term revenue after the program ramp-downs. Management was more open than usual about the surprise OEM program stop and was reticent on the names and size of specific accounts.
key_quotes: So, it challenged near-term growth, but expanded foundation for substantial future expansion.
We expect 30% year-on-year revenue growth in solution and products, and we hope it will increase over the period.
More than 80% of our new contracts are fixed price in nature.

542651|2026-06.headline: KPIT Q1 FY27: constant-currency revenue grew only 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 17.2% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion.
542651|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was roughly flat YoY in constant currency (+0.1%) and down 0.6% YoY in USD, with QoQ constant-currency revenue down 3.6%, against management's earlier guide of about 1% YoY degrowth and about 5% QoQ decline. Profitability fell more than proportionally: EBITDA margin was 17.2%, EBIT margin 12.3%, and PAT INR 1.17 billion, hit by forex losses and a share of losses from Qorix tied to postponed European revenues. Deal wins were USD 257 million, led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous. Management guided H2 better than H1, with a return to growth by Q4, and said margin recovery will largely follow revenue recovery.

financial_highlights.change: QoQ decline of about 4.5% in USD terms (per analyst question, not disputed by management)
Hit by forex loss and share of loss from Qorix
Led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue impact about 4% for the quarter from postponed revenues; more than 50% of KPIT revenue comes from Europe. Management expects the impact to show up in Q2 at a regional level.

segments.name: Americas (US)
segments.commentary: Growth described as fairly well balanced across the portfolio, with good CV growth and long-standing passenger car relationships; management expects growth to continue.

segments.name: SIMA (Southeast Asia, India, Middle East, Africa)
segments.commentary: Management said SIMA showed a sharp drop this quarter off a small base, but described significant growth there.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue fell more than other segments because of a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter that did not recur; management expects CV growth in Q2 and Q3.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 3.5 million in the quarter; management said PV growth expected but did not materialise, and two accounts (one Japan SDV program cancelled, one Europe SDV program ending) are stabilising by Q3.

guidance_outlook: H2 expected to be better than H1; return to growth by Q4 led by Q4 performance.
Q2 revenue expected to be flattish QoQ, per management's June update as reconfirmed on the call; Europe impact to be visible in Q2.
Margins to improve incrementally, not significantly, until revenue returns to growth; Qorix losses expected to continue for at least one or two more quarters.

Management did not commit to a specific Q4 margin level; asked whether a return to 20%+ EBITDA by Q4 is the working assumption, the CEO said it depends on growth and European cost take-out takes longer.
Medium-term margin aspiration of 22% to 24% by FY29 (from Analyst Day) reiterated as achievable, driven by products and solutions growth and outcome-based models.
Q4 growth comparison basis was not firmly defined: management said Q-on-Q for growth turnaround, with Q4 margin level 'flattish' per the CEO.
risks_watch: Timing of European pipeline conversion into revenue; management said wins are not in question but start dates are uncertain.
Europe cost take-out is slower than other regions, delaying margin recovery.
Continued Qorix share of losses for at least one or two quarters.
Q2 revenue flattish and Europe impact visible in Q2; Q3 stabilisation of the SDV-linked accounts depends on delivery.
Wage increases deferred this year; management said increments will be given in stages, starting with younger grades.
542651|2026-06.management_tone: Candid but cautious: management acknowledged a weak quarter and that European and Japanese OEM disruption created uncertainty, repeating the H2-over-H1 and Q4 growth timeline. Answers on margin timing and Q4 growth basis were less specific, and management pointed to pipeline and wins rather than firm numbers.
key_quotes: What we are not sure in the case of the current part is when these deals will realize.
So revenue will be the major driver.
I think the learning from the recent challenges with Japan and Germany is, I think we just need to have a lot more intensity and we have to run faster.

qa_highlights.question: When will commercial vehicles return to growth, and is the Europe weakness temporary given strong Europe deal wins and OEM model launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the weakness is not permanent; CV was hit by a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter and growth is expected next quarter. He said the uncertainty is about when deals will realise, not whether KPIT gets its share.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 22% to 24% margin aspiration for FY29 from the Analyst Day still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the medium-term outlook remains good, with product and solutions revenue expected to grow and be margin accretive, and some solutions ready to deploy in the next quarter or two; outcome-based models are also part of the plan.

qa_highlights.question: Can you unpack US growth between OEMs and off-highway, and is the momentum sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Chinmay Pandit said US growth is fairly balanced across the portfolio, with good CV growth and long-standing passenger car relationships, and visibility for the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Europe impact show up in Q2, and what is the Europe revenue quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said Europe impact was about 4% of quarterly revenue, will show up in Q2 at a regional level, and will be offset by US and SIMA growth at company level. He said SIMA dropped sharply this quarter off a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply this quarter, and what is the margin trajectory for the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyamvada Hardikar said the increase reflects forex impact on consolidated accounts, provisions linked to acquisitions, and subcontracting costs in the European region, all operational. Kishor Patil said margins will improve incrementally, not significantly, until revenue returns to growth, and Qorix losses will continue for at least one or two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 flattish, Q3 growing and Q4 significant growth still the assumption, and is 20%+ EBITDA by Q4 the working assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the large part depends on growth. European cost take-out will take much longer than other regions, so margins return once revenue grows. He said Q4 growth would be measured Q-on-Q and Q4 level would be flattish.

capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were given on the call; the only investment reference was to batteries, where management said a sodium-ion pilot plant needs more than USD 100 million of investment and about two to three years before production, with royalties only after production milestones.
Management said wage increments are being deferred this year and will be given in stages, starting with younger grades, with senior staff to follow over time.
Management said the Caresoft acquisition is being used for cost-reduction programmes for existing OEMs, and provisions relating to acquisitions were cited as a driver of higher other expenses in Q1.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 constant-currency revenue grew 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ; USD revenue fell 0.6% YoY. Management had earlier guided about 1% YoY degrowth and about 5% QoQ decline.

Deal wins were USD 257 million in the quarter, led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous. Management said wins are not in question and the issue is the timing of revenue start dates, especially in Europe.

Europe impact was about 4% of quarterly revenue from postponed revenues; management said the impact will show at a regional level in Q2, offset by growth in the US and SIMA. More than 50% of revenue comes from Europe.

Commercial vehicles fell more than other segments because of a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter that did not recur; management expects CV growth in Q2 and Q3. Passenger vehicle revenue fell about 3.5 million, with one Japan SDV program cancelled and one Europe SDV program ending, both expected to stabilise in Q3.

Management said the Europe OEM conversation has shifted to helping clients cut product cost by 30% to 40% and production cost, with revenue from these initiatives expected after the next couple of quarters. Pipeline growth areas cited were off-highway (seven new OEMs), trucks and bus (four OEMs), and new passenger car OEMs in Korea, Europe, US and Japan.
Strategic clients were about 87% of Q1 revenue and the management clarified the 84% figure is the share of the prior quarter's revenue, with QoQ strategic-client decline of 1.3%.

542652|2026-03.headline: Polycab Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY with EBITDA margin at 13.1% and record quarterly PAT of INR 7.9 bn, while Cable & Wire volumes grew only low single digits.
542652|2026-03.overview: Management reported record annual and quarterly revenue, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 27% YoY and PAT of INR 7.9 bn (up 7%, 8.9% margin). Growth was price-led: cumulative price hikes of 18-19% were taken from January to March, while Cable & Wire volumes grew low single digits in the quarter. Middle East escalation, PVC price spikes and pollution-related construction halts hit March, which is the key month of Q4. FY26 was a record year: revenue above INR 285 bn (+29%), EBITDA margin 13.9%, PAT above INR 27 bn (+32%), and FY26 volume growth of 18%.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 30% YoY, with domestic cables up 30% and combined volume growth in low single digits. EBIT margin was 13.1%, and Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+. Cables outpaced wires, and institutional sales grew faster than channel.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 47% YoY, the ninth straight quarter of outperformance versus industry. EBIT margin was 4.1%, and FY26 EBITDA margin was mid-single digit. Solar was the largest FMEG category, growing 2x; premium fans were about 25% and premium lighting about 35% of segment revenue.

segments.name: International (exports)
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY and contributed 4.4% of consolidated revenue in Q4. Full-year export share was 5.4%, and Middle East was about 16% of FY26 exports, which was hit during the quarter.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue fell 15% YoY to INR 5,098 mn on project execution timing. Segment profit was INR 386 mn, a 7.6% margin. Sustainable margin is guided at mid to high single digits.

guidance_outlook: Project Spring: Cables & Wires to grow at 1.5x industry growth; FMEG at 1.5x-2x industry growth.
Near to mid-term EBITDA margin guided at 12-14%; long-term 11-13%.
Exports to reach more than 10% of revenue by FY30; management expects exports to grow beyond 5% in FY27 and hopes to get there sooner.
Working capital cycle expected to revert to 45-50 days from 25 days in Q4.
Dividend payout to exceed 30% by FY30 (27.2% in FY26).
Capex of INR 60-80 bn over 5 years; FY27 capex guided at INR 12-16 bn per year; FY30 capex of INR 60-80 bn cited as Project Spring target.
EHV capacity expected on stream by end of calendar 2026, with revenue contribution from FY28.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is mid-70s (75-76%); management says plants practically reach early 90s but a sustainable level is 80-85%.
FY26 capex was about INR 14.8 bn, including roughly INR 15 bn invested in capacity expansion; the company plans INR 1.2-1.6 bn of capacity addition every year.
Around 90% of capex goes to Cable & Wire capacity (largely fungible), about 5% to backward integration and 3-4% to FMEG.
EHV (extra high voltage) capacity is on track to be commissioned by end of calendar 2026; about 50% of domestic EHV consumption is imported.
Management says there will be no scenario where Polycab runs out of capacity over the next 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price hikes of about 18-19% were taken from January to March; pass-through of copper, aluminium and PVC is described as complete and in tandem with input costs.
Volume growth was low single digits in Q4 as West Asia tensions, pollution-related construction halts and PVC price spikes (60-80% in early March) hit primary and secondary sales.
FY26 Cable & Wire volume growth was 18%, versus industry growth of 11-12%, with domestic wires and cable organised market share at 30-31% (up 300-400 bps over FY25's 26-27%).
Channel is about 90% of business and institutional about 10%; channel margins are 3-4% higher than institutional. Institutional mix was 2-3 points higher in Q4.
Demand sectors: power 40-45% of cables, manufacturing and private industry 35-40%, mobility 10-12%, energy and exploration 5-6%.
Power capacity additions in FY26 were about 55-56 GW, nearly double FY25; management expects demand to defer by weeks, not be lost.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Cable & Wire volume growth and price hikes taken from January?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined volume growth was low single digits, with cables ahead of wires. Cumulative price hikes were about 18-19% from January to March.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the Middle East disruption in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary sales were hit as distributors lifted less, since secondary sales did not move at the expected pace. Private sector demand was hit by gas rationing, and PVC prices rose 60-80% in early March. The impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutional sales were about 2-3 points higher than channel in Q4 (about 13-14% of the Cable & Wire top line in Q4 per management's arithmetic). Channel margins are 3-4% higher.

qa_highlights.question: Peak utilisation and capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-76%. Management says early 90s has been reached at times, but 80-85% is the sustainable level, and there is room for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Use of surplus cash and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on capex funded from internal accruals and on the dividend payout. M&A is being evaluated in India and abroad, but nothing is in view for the near to mid term.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a firm number, but expects exports to exceed the current 5.4% share. US distribution was re-established and North America was about 40% of FY26 exports. Middle East was about 15-16% of FY26 exports and is not expected to contribute meaningfully in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains and raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there are no inventory gains or losses because raw materials are hedged for copper and aluminium, and copper is largely imported. XLPE and compound availability is comfortable for about one quarter, with a diversified vendor base.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable & Wire Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+, and above the 13.9% company level for FY26. FMEG was mid-single digit for both Q4 and FY26.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, Brent around USD 100/bbl and a record-low rupee (INR 94.83/USD) raise input and inflation risk; the company's stated pass-through has so far held.
Working capital at 25 days in Q4 is flattered by letter-of-credit payables; reversion to 45-50 days would absorb cash.
Institutional mix rising reduces margins (channel is 3-4% higher); watch the mix next quarter.
March volume shortfall: whether primary sales recover as secondary sales normalise, and whether stocking unwinds.
FMEG margins (EBIT 4.1%) remain well below the 8-10% EBITDA target for FY30; watch the trajectory.
Export share fell to 4.4% in Q4; Middle East recovery timing and the US distribution ramp are open questions.
EHV commissioning by end of calendar 2026 and first revenue in FY28.

Answers on volume split and inventory gains were brief, and the company declined to give a firm FY27 export or growth number.
key_quotes: Importantly, these gains are not cyclical but very much structural in nature, driven by a shift towards organized players, increasing preference for quality and compliance and our ability to serve customers reliably across geographies.
So we have a hedging mechanism in place. So we don't have any inventory gain unlike peers.
So whatever we've delivered is again the best side of the industry growth.
So in FY28, you'll be able to see revenues from EHV.

542652|2026-06.headline: Polycab Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 39% YoY, record PAT of INR 7,967 million (+33% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.8%.
542652|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 39% YoY with EBITDA up 32% and margin at 13.8%, about 70 bps sequentially higher. Record quarterly PAT of INR 7,967 million at a 9.7% margin. Wires & Cables grew 39% and FMEG grew 71%, while EPC revenue fell 11%. Volume growth in domestic cables and wires was low to mid-single digit against a high base of about 26% last year, and exports declined on the Middle East disruption. Management cut prices by 3-4% in early July and said channel destocking followed the sharp fall in copper and aluminium prices in June.

financial_highlights.change: improved significantly, aided by temporary rise in payable days from LC usage

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Segment revenue grew 39% YoY; domestic W&C grew 43% YoY with domestic volume growth of low to mid-single digits. Segment EBIT margin was 13.3%, supported by wires mix, channel mix and operations; exports were a drag.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 71% YoY, the tenth straight quarter of outperforming industry growth. EBIT margin was 8%; premium mix reached about 25% of the portfolio (fans about 33%, lighting about 38%). Solar more than doubled and is now the largest category, though still below 50% of FMEG.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR 3,077 million, down 11% YoY on project timing; profitability was INR 338 million at an 11% margin. Management attributed the dip to milestone-linked revenue recognition.

guidance_outlook: Wires & Cables medium- to long-term EBIT margin guidance maintained at 11% to 13% under Project Spring.
FMEG targets EBITDA margins of 8% to 10% by FY30 (full-year basis) and growth at 1.5x to 2x industry growth.
EPC: sustainable operating margins expected in the high single-digit range over the medium to long term.
Management reiterated 1.5x market growth on volume plus value; FY26 volume growth was 18%.
Working capital cycle expected to normalise to the 45 to 50 day range as LC-related payable effects unwind.
Exports guided to exceed 10% of consolidated top line by 2030. Management expects a sizable US export pickup in the coming quarters.
EPC: Bharat Net and RDSS together expected to contribute about INR 800-1,000 crores (Bharat Net) and about INR 800 crores (RDSS) this year; combined order book about INR 10,900 crores.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was INR 3.2 billion.
Bharat Net order is about INR 8,000 crores, of which INR 4,500 crores is an execution piece over about 3 years; fibre for the execution period is already secured.
Data-centre opportunity estimated at 8-16/18 GW versus about 1.6 GW installed base; management cites INR 20,000-25,000 crores of cable market over 5-8 years.
T&D: about 2,000 circuit km added in April-May FY27; CEA estimate of about 17,000 ckm for FY27 versus about 20,000-21,000 ckm average for FY26-FY30.
demand_pricing: Domestic W&C volume growth was low to mid-single digit on a base of about 26% last year (cables above 25%, wires above 20%); wires grew high single digit and cables low to mid single digit.
Price revision of about 3-4% taken in the first fortnight of July 2026; pricing is cost-plus and passes through copper movements.
Channel stocking was below expectation in June as aluminium fell about 18-20% and copper fell from about INR 14,000 to INR 13,100-13,200; healthy channel stocking is about 20-25 days.
Exports declined YoY (about 13% per analyst); Middle East was about 20-24% of Q1 exports, North America 45-50% (US about 50%), Europe 18-20%. Order book is healthy in US, Europe and Latin America.
Channel contributes about 90% of W&C sales; Polycab estimates it gained 3-4% market share over the last 10-12 months (per last update).
FMEG: fans, pipes and conduits, lighting and switchgear all grew faster than their industry categories; FMEG ex-solar volume and price split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What were the price hikes and volume growth YoY, and how will pricing look in Q2 given copper?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic cable and wire volume grew low to mid-single digit on a high base; no Q2 copper guidance given, as pricing is cost-plus. A 3-4% price revision was taken in early July.

qa_highlights.question: Acceptances rose; how much are LC/acceptances and is their interest booked in finance costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about 100-110 days, LC-based payables about 80-90 days, and receivables 20-30 days, producing a 15-day cycle this quarter. The accounting treatment was deferred to an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre and optical fibre opportunity, and export trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres could add about INR 3.5 crores of cable per MW, an INR 20,000-25,000 crore market over 6-8 years, and Polycab already supplies conventional cables to some existing sites. Exports are recovering with a healthy order book; Middle East was 20-24% of Q1 exports.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Net fibre price risk and why EPC revenue fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre for the execution period is already secured, so Bharat Net is not exposed to higher fibre prices. EPC revenue timing is milestone-linked and may shift between quarters, with no material full-year dip expected.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume growth outlook and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 10-12 month trends rather than quarters; FY26 volume growth was 18% and 1.5x market growth is reiterated. Share gains of 3-4% were reported in the last update, with the next analysis expected after peers report.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of channel stocking benefiting Q1, and is the margin improvement limited?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking was below expectation as raw-material prices fell in June. Margins were supported by wires mix and channel mix, offset by weaker exports and operating leverage; the company targets the 11-13% range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG margin trajectory, and is 8% EBIT sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were operating leverage on a low base, a premium mix of about 25% overall, and regional product strategies. Management expects seasonality and targets 8-10% EBITDA margin for FMEG for full year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the data-centre and T&D demand strong enough to move industry growth, given the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that 1 GW of data-centre additions alone would be limited, but said T&D demand is accelerating, with about 15% cable content in T&D spend and transformer makers' order books at about 2.5x revenue.

risks_watch: Copper and aluminium volatility: June price falls led to destocking, and a 3-4% price cut was taken in early July.
Export recovery depends on Middle East and US trade conditions; exports declined YoY in Q1 with the Middle East impacted from March.
Working capital cycle of 15 days is flattered by LC-based payables and is expected to revert to 45-50 days.
Volume growth was low to mid-single digit against a high base; management points to a 10-12 month trend rather than quarters.
Data-centre and T&D demand timing is uncertain; CEA's 17,000 ckm FY27 target versus a 14,000-15,000 ckm five-year average was questioned by an analyst.
EPC revenue is lumpy and milestone-linked; Bharat Net and RDSS execution depends on milestones.

542830|2026-03.headline: IRCTC FY26 revenue from operations rose 11.55% to Rs 5,215 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 27.33% on exceptional items.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
542830|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR732 crore (+33.8%); segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26. Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

guidance_outlook: Management expects catering margins to return to the traditional 10-12% range; proof-of-concept trains to finish by September (2 trains) and November (2 trains).
The one-time HR cost of about INR20 crore (catering INR10 crore) is not expected to recur in Q2.

Rail Neer augmentation: Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles/day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles/day, targeted for FY27; four new plants (Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, Bhagalpur) may spill into FY28.
About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.
Active-active disaster recovery planned at Secunderabad, with further investment expected in Q2-Q4.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer installed capacity about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after closure of one plant (from 18.4 lakh); supply about 15.5 lakh bottles/day against higher demand at some stations.
NGET infra refresh: about INR150 crore infused into PRS modernisation; ticketing throughput about 37,000 tickets per minute, targeted to exceed 1 lakh.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh a year earlier; e-pantry live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100.
Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.
demand_pricing: Average daily tickets 14.58 lakh; Q1 total 13.27 crore (AC 6.92 crore, non-AC 6.35 crore). IRCTC share of railway ticketing rose to 88.92% from 88.78%.
UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.
Tourism OTA-linked income about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%); internet ticketing about 18% of total revenue excluding convenience fee, 26% including it.
Rail Neer priced at INR14 per bottle; third-party brands visible on non-AC trains and kiosks. Management attributed this to unauthorised vendors filling gaps at non-mandatory stations.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the resignation of Sanjay Jain and assurance on no material discrepancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a completely personal decision, praised his leadership, and said he will continue supporting from outside. No discrepancies were addressed beyond that assurance.

qa_highlights.question: Why third-party bottled water brands are visible on non-AC trains and kiosks, and Rail Neer's incremental revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail Neer is priced at INR14 per bottle; installed capacity is about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after one plant closed (from 18.4 lakh) against supply of about 15.5 lakh. Gaps at mandatory stations are exploited by unauthorised vendors. Augmentation: Ambernath 2 to 3 lakh and Danapur 1 to 2 lakh bottles/day; four new plants at Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi and Bhagalpur, with timelines possibly spilling into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Catering attachment rates, opt-in/opt-out mix and passenger-experience steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Opt-out for prepaid-train catering is roughly 15-30% (later said 25-30%, unconfirmed). Complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals. E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day from 1.05 lakh; e-pantry is live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100. Branded players are at policy-formulation stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Tejas rebranding and tourism margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC runs two private Tejas trains; non-fare revenue from naming and wrap rights is a policy-backed lever, with the Tejas naming done for the first time. It was described as a previously dormant revenue stream now being promoted through regional and zonal offices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the catering revenue increase in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Catering revenue rose from INR547 crore to INR732 crore, a delta of about INR185 crore. Onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore, licence fees from prepaid and other trains to INR224 crore from INR192 crore, static units to INR33 crore from INR20 crore, e-catering to INR22 crore from INR9 crore, and election specials to INR41 crore from INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the payment aggregator licence (IRCTC Payments) and monetisation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: The final RBI application was submitted by the 4 August 2026 deadline, together with the SAR and MVP; RBI response is expected within this financial year, and a TSP is engaged. Current iPay volume is about 2.7 lakh transactions, and expansion would follow once the licence is granted.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of convenience and non-convenience fee, and why the internet ticketing EBIT margin fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Convenience fee rose to INR248 crore from about INR236 crore; non-convenience fee fell to INR113 crore from INR123 crore. Marketing and ad income dipped about INR3 crore (INR14.51 crore to INR11.03 crore), and agent business was restricted. About INR10 crore of maintenance was booked, and NGET infra refresh and active-active DR at Secunderabad are being invested in. EBIT margin was 80.33% vs 84.12%, and management said it normally sits at 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the catering margin decline to 9.29% and the one-time HR cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Proof-of-concept on six trains cost more than INR4 crore. Total HR/gratuity one-time charge was about INR20 crore, of which INR10 crore was booked in catering, covering gratuity (INR20 lakh to INR25 lakh) and post-retirement benefits. Management said this will not recur next quarter, and the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by September (two trains) and November (two trains).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Rail Neer margin decline and how big was the profit impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell from about 14-15% to about 10%, mainly due to resin and petroleum cost increases linked to the West Asia crisis; material cost rose from INR55 crore to INR61 crore. Management said overall profit fell by only about INR4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What share of tourism and internet ticketing revenue comes from OTA partners and other channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Tourism OTA-linked income was about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%), or 5-7% from online hotels and ticketing alone. Internet ticketing revenue excluding convenience fee is about 18% of total revenue, and about 26% including it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected run rate for non-convenience fee and the UPI share of tickets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a quarterly run-rate and said the figure will not revert to INR110-115 crore. It aims to return toward INR150 crore via iPay, the e-wallet loyalty programme (growing more than 200%) and changes to agent associations. UPI share of tickets was 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat catering model and steady-state margin given the GST treatment on prepaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC's model is largely licensing. Vande Bharat catering is outsourced via limited tenders to empanelled licensees, while IRCTC runs catering in 81 Vande Bharat trains. On a Vande Bharat basis, the licence fee plus GST earns about INR105 per unit against INR222 paid to licensees, with about INR11 of non-claimable GST. Management said the 10-12% traditional catering margin range is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on new train additions and their ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains are expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore). Passenger growth of about 8% year-on-year also supports catering charges. Train additions are a ministry decision.

qa_highlights.question: Why has internet ticketing revenue not grown, and is the convenience fee being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said convenience fee grew about 4.89% quarter-on-quarter and has historically risen 5-7% a year. The UPI fee of INR10-20 is cited as a drag, and credit card and credit line options carry a higher fee of INR15-30. Management said it will push for a higher convenience fee but cannot force a policy decision.

risks_watch: Catering margin recovery to the 10-12% range depends on the proof-of-concept trains ending by September and November and on the one-time HR charge not recurring in Q2.

Internet ticketing EBIT margin (80.33% vs 84.12%) and non-convenience fee (INR113 crore vs INR123 crore) depend on the outcome of the website transformation, reintroduction of ad revenue, and agent business changes; the target of INR150 crore has no timeline.

RBI response on the IRCTC Payments aggregator licence is expected within FY27; iPay monetisation depends on that approval.
Rising prepaid-train mix carries lower GST-adjusted margins, and the 25-30% opt-out rate has not been confirmed by management.
Management was evasive on the reason for Sanjay Jain's resignation, saying only that it was a personal decision.

Our convenience fee has always grown. In this quarter also it has grown.

Max Lucknow Gomti Nagar: 426 beds currently, rising to 570 beds over the next 2 quarters; further 200-300 beds planned on the 27-acre Gomti Nagar land bank over time. Lucknow Shaheed Path: 700-bed greenfield approved at INR 1,400 crore, phased over ~3 years, expandable to ~900 beds; 5+ acres.

Pipeline (commissioning in next 2-3 years): Max Nagpur 100 beds by FY28; Zirakpur, Mohali 400 beds in FY28; Max Dwarka 260 beds (building plan submission underway, 24 months); Max Vaishali 200 beds (awaiting building plan approvals, 24 months post approval); Max Patparganj 400 beds with D-wall construction started, commissioning by FY29. Dwarka brownfield of 200-plus beds being planned; Dwarka oncology centre to start next month.

Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, 10-acre site): controlling stake acquired in May 2026, consolidation from Q1 FY27; about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA; plans to revamp and expand. Acquisition consideration not discussed.

FY26 capital deployment: INR 1,627 crore into ongoing expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, INR 131 crore for land at Vaishali, INR 146 crore dividend paid; Q4 deployment INR 328 crore.
demand_pricing: Network Q4 occupancy above 75% despite higher operational beds; OBDs up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; ALOS up 9% YoY due to simultaneous multi-location brownfield rollout, expected to tighten over time.

ARPOB INR 77,900 in Q4, after absorbing higher ALOS and discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients (CGHS). Oncology OBDs down ~5-6% YoY; oncology share of in-patient revenue 21% vs 26% in Q4 FY25 and 24% in Q3 FY26. Management expects oncology share to hover at 21-22%, not return to 25-26%.

Chemo-drug discontinuation: discontinued since October 2025; annual chemotherapy billing down ~INR 200 crore (gross); net of GST ~INR 140 crore. Earlier drugs were billed at MRP with ~15-16% margins; CGHS now requires ~30% discount to MRP. Management says this is industry-wide but Max is most affected given oncology and institutional mix. Q4 carries the full impact.

CGHS rate revision: ~INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates, at two hospitals so far) to flow over the coming months. Management said CGHS is reconsidering the chemo discount but timing is not fixed. ECHS and PSU patients lack dispensary access to drugs such as Keytruda.

Noida ramp-up: occupancy above 64-65% in Q4 with doctors hired; management says it is in line with expectations. Dwarka at 80-85% occupancy. Management cited a hockey-stick occupancy curve: units break even around 50-55% occupancy, and the real value comes from 60-65% to about 80%.

Other metrics: Max@Home revenue INR 73 crore (+30% YoY, 16 service lines, 15 cities); Max Lab revenue INR 52 crore (+14% YoY, 60+ cities, ~6 lakh patients); international patient revenue INR 227 crore (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital revenue); digital revenue INR 838 crore (~31% of revenue). Q4 doctor costs about INR 435 crore; management expects operating leverage from here.
Management stated the company sees 10-12% PAT margin as the industry's steady state. It said doctor compensation increases in micro-markets are transferred to patients over time.

key_quotes: We started the financial year with healthy momentum across the Network, recording year-on-year growth of 16% in revenue and 15% in operating EBITDA.
A hospital does not admit a patient, a doctor admits a patient.

So, one is that oncology will start to normalize from Q3 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the India segment profit negative and what is the cash conversion outlook?

543230|2026-03.headline: Advait Energy Transitions Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR228 crore and PAT 55% to INR19.96 crore; order book hit a record INR1,304 crore.

segments.commentary: Accounts for 36% of the order book and about 25%-27% of FY26 revenue per management. BESS EPC revenue of INR43 crore (reported as Q4 revenue of INR46 crore) came via group company Advait Green Energy.

segments.commentary: Dholera multi-integrated facility is expected to be operational in Phase 1 by Q4 FY27, with 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser Phase 1 capacity. Management guided INR100-200 crore BESS manufacturing business in FY27 as the plant starts only around September-October 2026.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40%-plus in FY27, described as conservative by management; it said FY26 growth was about 80%.

Fuel cell: technology transfer with AVL and TECO for a plant in Ahmedabad; manual plant in about 1.5 years, automatic in 2-3 years; management sees about 500 MW of fuel cell demand within 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Solar EPC physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year, per management, with QRs now in place for large tenders.
Dholera facility: Phase 1 expected operational by Q4 FY27, covering 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser capacity; BESS plant to be 5 GWh over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 BESS revenue INR46 crore if BOO projects will sell electricity?
qa_highlights.answer: The BOO projects were awarded to the group company Advait Green Energy and booked as EPC revenue (INR43 crore). Electricity revenue will sit in SPVs and be consolidated after COD, likely from FY end.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and margin expectations?

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on commodity cost inflation to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund capex and what about dilution?

qa_highlights.question: When will the company move to pure-play solar EPC and what is the solar EPC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to bid on large tenders including module-supply projects and win some orders this year. Physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year.

Margin pressure from metal and fuel cost inflation and from the NRE mix shift; Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin of 12.61% compares with 11.73% for FY26 and 12.87% in FY25.
Electrolyser and fuel cell timelines depend on government policy and market opening; the Dholera facility is due Q4 FY27 and fuel cell deliveries from FY27-28.

543232|2026-03.headline: CAMS Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record with non-MF revenue up ~24.5% YoY and EBITDA margin back at ~46.5%, while MF revenue was flat (+0.5% QoQ).

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of ~10% in FY26 is the lowest in 5 years: how much is deliberate discretionary cost management versus sustainable savings?

Total cost growth was 9% including depreciation and 7.8% excluding it, with QoQ cost growth under 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Passive mix shift typically hurts RTA yields more than AMC yields. Is there scope to renegotiate RTA pricing on passives or to gain bargaining power on the active book?

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-5 bps AMC fee cut be passed to RTA fees? Is any RTA fee negotiation under way?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete RTA fee change has been agreed. Discussions may happen, but management said it is comfortable with the price-value equation and does not expect a material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Should yield decline be modelled at the historical 3-3.5% for FY27 and FY28, given that margins have previously dropped from 46-47% to 42-44%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5% is the 5-year average and should be used as a conservative model input, with the aim being a lower number, possibly under 3%. On margins, Anuj Kumar said 46% was reached about 5 quarters ago, dropped to 42%, and has now been regained over 4 quarters. He attributed the earlier fall to investments in non-revenue businesses made over 2022-2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for employee cost, overall expenses and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth is guided below 5% and total expense growth below 9%, with increments effective from Q2 FY27. No formal margin guidance was given; the aim is to retain the Q4 FY26 margin of ~46.5% after salary increases, investments and yield compression.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~20% non-MF growth be built in FY27 with KRA flat, and what is the breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a base of ~INR60-62 crore quarterly non-MF revenue, or ~INR250 crore annualised. It needs ~INR45-50 crore of increment: payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore (quoted as INR4-5 crore in one place and ~INR15 crore in another), with ConsenPro and GIFT City adding a few crore.

qa_highlights.question: KRA: what is the price cut, and how is FY27 revenue flat after it?
qa_highlights.answer: The industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 is expected to reduce KRA revenue by ~INR8 crore on a base of ~INR42-43 crore. NSE KRA integration adds ~INR3 crore, leaving a ~INR5 crore gap that management expects to close through new-logo growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: ConsenPro is a commercial DPDP-compliance product built inside Think360 from an internal captive offering. It covers consent management, data discovery, regulatory reporting and consulting. Management expects ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies to need it over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Could a single KYC regime through CKYC reduce KRA pricing or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CKYC is not yet eligible to substitute for KRA KYC. KRA runs a second verification layer (name match, face match, DOB and address against DigiLocker or UIDAI), so the risk is seen as a watch item rather than an immediate threat.

risks_watch: MF yield: the passive mix shift continues to pull yields down. Any AMC pass-through of 3-5 bps could lead to RTA fee discussions. Management guides yield decline below 3%, against a 3-3.5% historical average, and says no concrete RTA fee change has been agreed.

KRA: a ~INR8 crore fee cut from 1 April 2026 is only partly offset by ~INR3 crore from NSE KRA. FY27 flat guidance depends on new-logo growth to fill a ~INR5 crore gap. A possible single-KYC/CKYC shift is a watch item.

Margin sustainability: management is targeting retention of the ~46.5% Q4 margin through FY27 after salary increases, investments and yield compression. Past cycles show margins falling back to 42-44% after investment phases.

MF AUM and asset growth: AUM fell from INR58.5 lakh crore at a point in Q4 to INR55.1 lakh crore, reflecting Middle East-related market weakness. Management says asset growth is awaited after the last two months, and FY27 MF revenue is not guided.

ReArch execution: a 5-year programme with ~2 years done and ~3-4% behind the schedule curve. The data lake is due in 1H FY27, and the data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform are due within 3-4 months. Non-MF margin target is 20% by end FY27.

Non-MF growth dependence: ~20% FY27 growth needs ~INR45-50 crore of incremental revenue. The breakdown includes ~INR20 crore from payments, with a new-logo pipeline (SIFs, ConsenPro, GIFT City) still early.

qa_highlights.question: Headcount reduction and employee cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise headcount is targeted to fall about 5% in FY27, with 2-3% already down; net employee cost benefit is expected at about 3-3.5% because AI and automation hires offset some exits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5% employee cost growth target medium-term, and what about margin expansion beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5% employee cost growth is an end-of-FY27 year-on-year target (about INR500 crore base, adding INR25-30 crore). Total cost growth is targeted below 10% a year for the next two to three years; margin expansion of about 1% a year, with a possibility of 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-asset MF revenue decline YoY despite transaction growth?

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are AI and automation gains, and what is the payments and yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits from the new platform are incremental, with productivity gains over about 3-4 years; cloud and hardware cost inflation will offset some. Payments growth is mainly credit cards under the PA licence and will be scaled step by step; nothing one-time. Yield compression from 4Q FY26 and 1Q FY26 is in the base; residual compression over 3-4 quarters is expected to be small, with a historical 2.5-3% annual decline.

qa_highlights.question: Capex, capitalisation and depreciation outlook, and implied PAT growth?
qa_highlights.answer: On-prem capex about INR75 crore; re-architecture cost about INR500 crore, INR290 crore capex, with INR40 crore capitalised in Q1 and at least INR80 crore more in FY27. Depreciation to rise by INR4-5 crore for the rest of FY27. With EBITDA growth about 45%, PAT growth is about 31%; PAT margin expected at 30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: Non-MF EBITDA breakeven status by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Account aggregator, pension and CAMS Repository are not yet EBITDA positive; CAMSRep is expected to turn positive on a Q4 basis. Think Analytics is almost at breakeven. Account aggregator adoption faces a bottleneck, mainly on the fintech and lending side.

risks_watch: Recovery in KRA revenue from Q2 FY27 after the April 2026 pricing reset (rates down about 29-30%); Q1 non-MF margin fell to about 13%, and management needs it near 17-20% by year-end.

Employee cost growth target of about 5% and total cost growth below 10% a year for two to three years; cloud and hardware cost inflation could offset AI-driven savings.

Management said the company is now a near-record on revenue and PAT, helped by a forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements. The call focused on the "Fund in India" conduit model, high-speed rail and DFC pipeline, NIM targets, and questions on fertiliser exposure and the agreement-to-disbursement lag.

segments.name: Railways (core, sole financier)
segments.commentary: Management says IRFC remains the sole financing arm for Indian Railways; no railway business was booked in FY24 but FY26 saw a restart in diversification. Railway repayments drive quarterly AUM dips.

segments.name: Diversified / non-railway (fertiliser, metro, GenCo, ports)
segments.commentary: Three HURL urea plants (Gorakhpur, Barauni, Sindri) are financed on railway-linkage grounds, refinanced from SBI-led lenders at 50bps+ lower cost. Hyderabad Metro Phase 1 refinancing signed; Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) pending decision.

guidance_outlook: Year-end FY27 AUM targeted around INR5 lakh crore (management: possibly INR4.95 lakh crore); mid-year guidance of about INR5 lakh crore also referenced.
FY27 disbursement guided to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore; Q2-Q4 expected to pick up, with some refinancing assets in the pipeline.
NIM target: about 10bps average annual improvement, 2% by end-2030; FY27 NIM targeted above 1.6%, with Q4 NIM expected to be higher than the 1.65% full-year ambition referenced by the analyst.

Planning around INR50,000-plus crore disbursement per year for the next decade; high-speed rail and DFC pipeline cited as more than INR50,000-60,000 crore per year, with metro and rapid rail adding INR20,000-30,000 crore per year.
Targets new lending at about 8% with spread above 100bps; repayments on legacy assets at 35-40bps lower margin.
capex_capacity: Planned high-speed rail corridors (7 announced) with financing need about INR16 lakh crore; DFC about INR3 lakh crore; combined about INR20 lakh crore, per management.
Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore; Phase 1 refinancing already signed.
Greenfield projects take 3 to 5 years from agreement to first funding, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says recent open-tender rates for GenCo and transport projects are around 8%, and IRFC is comfortable lending at that level with 100bps+ margin.
Fund in India: IRFC intends to act as a conduit for bilateral and multilateral funding, offering bespoke tenor and currency solutions.
Competitors' NIMs are falling across the sector per management; IRFC's low overhead cost is cited as the advantage.
Q1 disbursement was small because the pipeline is thin; management says it is not reliant on FY26 agreements converting in-year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hold the INR5 lakh crore AUM guidance at half-year and end FY27, and what is the disbursement and AUM growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about INR5 lakh crore AUM by year-end, noting it may land at INR4.95 lakh crore. FY27 disbursement is expected to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore. The Q1 AUM dip reflects a September repayment from railways.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 2% YoY against AUM growth of about 4%, implying NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM rose from 1.40% in FY25 to 1.50% in FY26 and is expected to exceed 1.6% by year-end. Legacy 35-40bps assets are repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets, which is a gradual effect over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the material other income in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements, reflecting rupee appreciation against the yen. Management said the gain is accounted per Ind AS and a corresponding metro receipt is expected in Q2. Last year's Q4 saw a INR7 crore forex loss.

qa_highlights.question: How are the fertiliser borrowers linked to railways, and is there sponsor support or guarantee for these loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HURL urea plants depend on railway sidings for raw material and finished urea movement. Output is sold to government agencies on a cost-plus model with 10-12% margin. Management described the loans as refinancing of an existing SBI-led bank facility, with rate cuts of at least 50bps. No explicit sponsor guarantee was described.

qa_highlights.question: What does the agreements-executed versus disbursement table mean, and why is there a lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR92,799 crore of agreements were largely greenfield, of which about INR37,000 crore has been disbursed. Greenfield funding typically starts 3 to 5 years after agreement, with the remainder expected over 1 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on diversification into metro and infrastructure, and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hyderabad Metro is on track, with Phase 1 refinancing signed and Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) awaiting a decision. Pipeline spans high-speed rail, DFC, metro, rapid rail, ports, GenCo, transco and renewables linked to railways.

risks_watch: Q1 disbursement of about INR2,000 crore leaves the INR35,000 crore-plus FY27 target dependent on a steep ramp in Q2-Q4.
AUM guidance hinges on repayments from railways and new refinancing deals; a September repayment could again lower the AUM figure.
NIM guidance (1.6%+ this year, 2% by 2030) relies on legacy assets at 35-40bps repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets; the call did not provide a quarterly path.
Fertiliser exposure to sister-company-linked borrowers; management cited cost-plus economics but no formal guarantee was described.
Hyderabad Metro Phase 2 decision and the high-speed rail and DFC funding framework remain unconfirmed; the large INR20 lakh crore opportunity is not yet contracted.
Forex gains on yen funding may not recur; the Q1 other income is currency-driven.

543257|2026-09.headline: IRFC reports H1 FY27 revenue up over 20% and PAT up over 10%; management reiterates ~INR5 lakh crore AUM target for FY27.
543257|2026-09.overview: Management said H1 FY27 beat both company guidance and street expectations, with revenue up more than 20% and PAT up more than 10% year on year. The CEO said PAT grew in double digits in five of the last six quarters, the exception being Q4 FY26, which carried provisions for new business under RBI norms. Diversification beyond the Indian Railways single-client model is the core theme, with non-railway lending at margins 2-3.5 times the railway book. The call also covered a large pipeline of railway-linked financing (DFC, high-speed rail, freight JVs) that management expects to start in FY28. Most Q&A was on strategy and shareholder value; the transcript gives no reported Q2 figures beyond the H1 growth rates.

segments.name: Railways (IR) lending
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% plus of AUM is with Railways, at a NIM of about 1.3% (around 35 bps margin on cost-plus). Railway book is being replaced over time by higher-yield non-IR assets.

segments.name: Non-railway lending (diversification)
segments.commentary: Non-IR assets earn margins of 2-3.5 times the railway book, per management; INR35,000 crore of disbursement last year was non-IR. Pipeline covers metros, ports, renewables, thermal power, Gencos linked to Railways, and some road linkages, targeted for Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements to exceed last year's level; guidance reiterated.
AUM target of near INR5 lakh crore (possibly slightly short by INR1,000-2,000 crore) by end FY27; management expects to show progress by Q3.
PAT expected to grow near 10% annually even with flat AUM, as non-IR assets replace railway assets at higher yields.

Railway-related funding of minimum about INR50,000 crore a year from FY28 for next decade, subject to the funding model (multilateral/aggregator role) to be finalised by end FY27; clearer numbers promised in Q3.
Mix target of 60% pure railways and 40% diversification by 2030.
Margin floor of INR0.85-0.90 per the ALM policy on non-railway loans; WACC target of 6.55% to be maintained.
capex_capacity: Management cited a Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat (over 2,000 km, more than INR3 lakh crore), seven sanctioned high-speed rail corridors, and six freight lines planned under JV/PPP; total pie over INR20 lakh crore over about 10 years.
IRFC plans to act as sole financing arm and aggregator, with talks under way with the World Bank, other multilaterals and domestic players; model expected in place by end FY27.
Employee headcount roughly doubled in the last year, per the CEO.
demand_pricing: Floating-rate exposure: repo rate up 25 bps and back-to-back TONAR up 25 bps; management says it passes these through on non-railway loans and that resets are both ways.
Yen borrowing: about USD2 billion raised last year at around 1.8%, now about 2.25% after TONAR increases; hedging cost stated as not above 6.3%.
Term loans from banks are about 25% of the borrowing mix; management claims a 20-30 bps cushion against rate moves.
Prepayment: management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no floor on benchmark-linked pricing, and lowest-in-market cost of funds.
Overhead cost cited at about INR0.15 per unit of lending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities, and what are the main risks on railway capex, asset growth or funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 disbursements will exceed FY26, with non-IR pipeline (metros, ports, renewables, thermal, Gencos, roads) ready for Q3 or early Q4. Railway-linked funding is to start from FY28 at a minimum of INR50,000 crore a year, with the aggregator model to be set by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key financial risks (NIM, borrowing costs, asset quality) in a changing rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO cited a 6.55% WACC, lower than other NBFCs, and a push to raise more 54EC bonds and ECB. Management said the ALM team monitors margins weekly and keeps a minimum spread of INR0.85-0.90 on non-railway loans.

qa_highlights.question: How is non-railway lending priced, and how fast can rate increases be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans are priced on a cost-plus basis, and floating-rate loans reset monthly, quarterly or yearly. Management said a 25 bps repo hike and TONAR increase were passed through, and the company keeps a 20-30 bps cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there prepayment pressure, as seen at other government lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no benchmark floor, and the cheapest funding in the market. Some prepayments by borrowers into IRFC were said to be business wins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM and disbursement vision, and is the INR5 lakh crore AUM target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated near INR5 lakh crore AUM by end FY27 (possibly 1,000-2,000 crore short), up from INR4.85 lakh crore at end FY26. It targets a 60:40 railway-to-diversified mix by 2030 and near-10% PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share price move so much, and what are the dividend and value prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share price moves are outside its control and pointed to fundamentals. It cited an interim dividend of INR1.15 this year against INR1.05 last year, and a payout of about 40% of profit over the last two years.

risks_watch: Funding for the railway-linked pipeline (DFC, high-speed rail, freight lines) depends on a model yet to be finalised with the Ministry, multilaterals and bilaterals; no numbers given yet.
Rising floating rates (repo and TONAR each up 25 bps) and hardening yen hedge costs could squeeze spreads if pass-through lags.
AUM target near INR5 lakh crore may slip by INR1,000-2,000 crore; Q3 is the next checkpoint.
Non-IR loans are ticket-size lumpy (INR10,000-20,000 crore), so disbursement may be concentrated in H2.
Management did not disclose a specific Q2 standalone figure or asset-quality (GNPA/NPA) data in the call.

Management was firm on AUM and disbursement targets but vague on the railway funding model and gave few hard numbers beyond H1 growth rates. It answered the investor-relations question on share price with general market commentary.

numbers are not manufactured; they are earned.
We are not putting any prepayment penalty, whereas others.
PAT of this company will keep growing year-to-year on that line.

543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

segments.name: Paint categories (Q4 FY26 value growth / volume growth)
segments.commentary: Primers and distemper grew 14.9% value and 9.6% volume; putty and cement paint 12.6% value and 9.5% volume; emulsions 10.5% value and 11.2% volume; enamels and wood coatings 7.2% value and 5.4% volume. All four categories grew in value and volume.

segments.name: Apple Chemie (subsidiary, waterproofing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR27.5 crore (+34.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR75.1 crore (+17.8%). Gross margin around 40% plus/minus 1%. FY27 target is 30%-plus growth.

guidance_outlook: Management is prepared to accept a 2-2.5pp gross margin decline to drive faster top-line growth, while expecting EBITDA margin broadly unchanged.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.
April growth was driven largely by price hikes; some dealer overstocking has occurred, so May-June demand is uncertain.
Industry price increases of about 12% on the overall basket were implemented; management does not foresee another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation deteriorates.
Management expects gross margins across the industry to normalise by Q2 FY27 as raw material costs stabilise, though Q1 may see volatility.
Apple Chemie targets 30%-plus revenue growth in FY27.
No major capex is envisaged until FY29; FCF is expected to step up from FY27 onwards. FY26 dividend proposed at INR5 per share, up 43% from INR3.5.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant, 90,000 KL per annum capacity: final commissioning stage, trial production expected June 2026.
New solvent-based plant and expanded putty plant at Jodhpur have already commenced production in recent months.
Network at 31 March 2026: over 19,350 active dealers, over 12,200 tinting machines, 55 depots across all 28 states.
330 kW solar installation at Kochi factory is fully operational.
demand_pricing: Industry demand recovered from November 2025 after roughly 8 quarters of subdued growth; the Iran war from about March 2026 disrupted raw material supply and pushed some input prices up 50-100%.
The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.
Management said the competitive intensity has moderated over the last couple of quarters; it sees no change in behaviour since JSW's acquisition of Akzo.
Differentiated products make up about 30% of sales and are described as price-inelastic, so margin reduction is expected mainly in the other two-thirds of the portfolio.
Premium emulsions are a growing share; management said value growth has exceeded volume growth in almost all categories over the last 20 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Apple Chemie growth accelerate to 35% in Q4 and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was muted because government contractors' payments were delayed, but Q3 and Q4 grew about 30%-plus; gross margin is about 40% plus/minus 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company pursuing more aggressive market share gains, and will a 200bp gross margin sacrifice be enough to reach about 24% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board judged the company had been too conservative on margins; it will spend more on trade schemes and influencers, lowering gross margin 2-2.5pp while EBITDA margin should hold. Management said yes, 24% growth is achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the gross margin reduction come from, and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Extra spend will be netted from revenue through trade discounts and influencer costs, mainly in non-differentiated products. Management said competitive intensity has normalised and the move reflects a wish to grow faster, not a response to competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile double-digit gross growth with single-digit reported growth, and will net sales be sacrificed?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross sales grew double-digit in each of the last five months, but higher trade and influencer discounts cut Q4 net growth to 8.5%. Management does not expect net sales growth to fall back to single digits.

qa_highlights.question: Will more price increases be needed, and how is pricing held if costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation worsens. It said the company now acts independently on pricing and that margins should normalise by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company growing in metros and dealer productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 1 and Tier 2 coverage is now good, and growth will come from deeper dealer throughput, not city size; with about 19,500 dealers it sees room to double sales per dealer.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression of 2-2.5pp from trade and influencer spending; watch whether EBITDA margin holds near 23%.
Gap between gross and net sales growth caused by rising discounts; watch Q1 FY27 net revenue.
Possible overstocking by dealers after April price-led growth; May-June demand is unclear.
Raw material volatility from the Middle East conflict; solvent-based products carry an uncovered cost gap.
Commissioning and ramp-up risk at the Jodhpur water-based plant, targeted for June 2026.
Apple Chemie's dependence on government-linked infrastructure payments, which were delayed in H1 FY26.
Treasury income is exposed to bond yield mark-to-market movements (Q4 FY26 treasury income was INR0.19 crore against INR5.6 crore a year earlier).

key_quotes: We are in a phase where growing and gaining market share is the top priority.
we are prepared to accept some moderation in our gross margins if required.
We are not a company that has ever burned cash or come even remotely close to it.
we do not envisage any further major capex until FY '29.

543258|2026-06.headline: Indigo Paints Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18.7% to INR350 crore with EBITDA margin up to 17.7%, its best Q1 margin in four years.
543258|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 18.7% YoY to INR350 crore, with double-digit volume and value growth across all four product categories. EBITDA rose 42% to INR61.9 crore (margin 17.7% vs 14.8%), and PAT rose 60.7% to INR42.4 crore, helped partly by a mark-to-market treasury gain. Consolidated revenue was INR369.7 crore (+19.7%), but subsidiary Apple Chemie's margins were compressed by high-cost inventory and limited B2B pass-through. Management said it will spend more aggressively on trade and influencers in Q2 to widen the growth gap versus the industry, and that the Jodhpur capex cycle is complete.

Solvent-based Jodhpur plant already in production for several months and ramping up.
Legacy water-based plant to be scrapped and output shifted to the new automated plant; opex expected to be broadly unchanged.

Competition: management said no meaningful change from JSW's acquisition of AkzoNobel or the Birla Opus entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Indigo not grown faster versus the market leader, and was the IPL advertising pause a missed opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said steep, frequent price hikes benefit the market leader most. The IPL pause was due to raw material uncertainty after the Iran war, not competitor ad intensity or Dhoni's playing status; it intends to put the money back in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is July and August demand holding after Q1 upstocking, and is there a destocking risk for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel overstocking was not seen at Indigo. July was a very good month with momentum maintained or slightly better than Q1; August was too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a price cut in H2, and what are the Q2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No further price hikes are planned for now. A price cut is possible, most likely after Diwali. No Q2 margin guidance was given; management suggested looking at the six-month period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jodhpur plant opex impact, and what is the competitive intensity after JSW-AkzoNobel?
qa_highlights.answer: The new plant replaces the legacy water-based plant with little opex change. Competitive intensity is unchanged, as JSW and AkzoNobel still operate separately.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new plant be ready for the festive season, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production is about 10 days away and should stabilise in about a month. The legacy plant is a backup. Management said gross margin may drop a couple of points, and EBITDA margin may move about 1 point either way.

543259|2026-03.headline: Home First Q4 FY26: record Q4 disbursement of INR1,572 crore (+23.5% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR540 crore (+41.4% YoY); FY27 AUM growth guided ~25%.
543259|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 saw record quarterly disbursement, PAT of INR149 crore (+42.7% YoY, +6.6% QoQ), and AUM of INR15,878 crore (+24.9% YoY, +6.4% QoQ).
