Execution slipped in March owing to a delayed appointed date on one project and geopolitical-driven fuel and bitumen price volatility, with oil and gas revenue of ~INR400-450 crore against an internal expectation of ~INR600 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of ~15% and new order wins of INR20,000-22,000 crore, while order book stands at ~INR26,470 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 20% in FY27 and 25-30% in FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Will margin improve beyond the 10.5-11% range?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 execution miss, particularly oil and gas?

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing for the Agra-Gwalior BOT and the two HAM appointed dates?

qa_highlights.question: Why is execution rate falling versus order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed land aggregation: piecemeal land raises cost and slows work, and provisional appointed dates led to mobilisation before land was ready. Execution rate to be assumed at current level.

543317|2026-06.headline: G R Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 32.71% YoY to ~INR2,423 crores, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 11.02% from 12.65%.

543318|2026-03.headline: Clean Science Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR193 crore with 46% EBITDA margin; FY26 standalone revenue fell 12% to about INR796 crore.
543318|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to about INR193 crore on volume recovery, with EBITDA of INR88 crore (46% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (40%), but revenue fell 19% YoY. For FY26, standalone revenue declined 12% from INR900 crore to INR796 crore, attributed to loss of an FMCG key account (4-MAP), lower offtake and pricing pressure. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 14% to about INR246 crore, led by HALS (Clean Fino-Chem), with EBITDA of INR96 crore (33%) and PAT of INR58 crore. Management said Clean Fino-Chem reached its first positive EBITDA (INR7 crore) and that the Hydroquinone/Catechol plant is still stabilising at about 10-15% utilisation.

segments.name: Performance chemicals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 72% of FY26 standalone revenue. Management cited a rebound in flagship product volumes and a gross margin (RMC 33%) about 2 points better than prior quarters.

segments.name: Pharma-Agro (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed 19% of FY26 standalone revenue. The pharma intermediate plant was refurbished for HALS intermediates, and the older pharma intermediate was dropped.

segments.name: FMCG (standalone)
segments.commentary: Contributed the balance 9% of FY26 standalone revenue. A key FMCG account (4-MAP) was lost during the year.

segments.name: HALS (Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4 FY26, at over 1,000 tonnes per quarter versus about 350-360 tonnes eight quarters earlier. Blended realisation was about INR460/kg versus INR420-430/kg in Q3; exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%. Subsidiary EBITDA margin was about 15% in Q4 versus about 1% in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Performance Chemical 2 (water treatment-related capex) expected to commercialise by September 2026; validation in Q3, initial commercial production in Q4, and a pickup in FY28.
Hydroquinone/Catechol plant expected to reach optimal operations in 1-2 quarters; captive HQ/catechol now replaces imports for TBHQ and Veratrole.
Capex budget for FY27 of about INR80-100 crore; Clean Fino-Chem projects under an INR200 crore enabling Board resolution, with investment likely in the second half of FY27.
Management aspires to a HALS blended realisation of USD7-7.5/kg but did not give FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance, calling FY27 a 'very tricky' year dependent on macro and crude oil.
Management said it is not pencilling in any price hikes; it expects to benefit in an inflationary environment, as it did in FY23.
capex_capacity: Clean Fino-Chem Hydroquinone/Catechol plant commissioned in December 2025; still in initial stabilisation, with utilisation about 10-15% and March 2026 HALS exit utilisation about 40%.
Performance Chemical 2 commercialisation timeline moved due to scarce manpower linked to labour movement from higher gas prices; now targeted by September 2026.
Plans to debottleneck HALS lines and add a dedicated HALS 2020 line (in-house technology, validated with European customers) and to backward-integrate further key intermediates with minimal capex.
Pharma plant refurbished in the next couple of months to produce HALS intermediates, replacing Chinese sourcing.
Subsidiary capital infusion of about INR200 crore in FY26 takes total investment in subsidiary to INR750 crore.
demand_pricing: MEHQ: management is maintaining market share by calibrating prices against Chinese hydroquinone producers, who are less affected by raw material costs. Phenol and acetone prices rose sharply, and long-term contracts (half-yearly or yearly) could not pass on increases; these will be renegotiated on expiry.

HALS demand: export share rose to about 50% in select products (Europe, Middle East, US), with Southeast Asia and LatAm being explored. Distribution partners are adding safety stock, and inbound customer interest is rising.
Anisole: management said it is the largest producer and consumer globally and India; competition from China does not affect its sales, as anisole is mainly used captively.
Base chemical prices reportedly rose about 2x in some commodities, but management said these are not transactional benchmarks. Management said China has a pricing advantage over other geographies.
Management declined to share product-wise revenue, geographic split, or product-level volumes, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HALS revenue jump sharply, and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer validation and trials delayed the response by several quarters. Exports rose to about 50% of sales in select products from about 20%, with over 1,000 tonnes sold in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company passing on higher raw material costs (phenol, acetone, ammonia)?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were passed on partly, not fully; long-term contracts could not be repriced, and these are to be renegotiated as they expire. Q4 subsidiary EBITDA was INR8 crore despite March price spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Performance Chemical 1 (HQ/catechol) utilisation and breakeven outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 10-15%. Management expects two more quarters to optimise norms and yields before ramping utilisation further.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a volume or gross margin explanation for MEHQ, given the share-defence pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sequential growth of 7-8% was volume-led, led by flagship products. Standalone gross margin improved on product mix, with no one-off gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and the performance bonus reversal amount?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex could be INR80-100 crore, with Clean Fino-Chem investments likely in the second half. The bonus reversal was about INR11 crore.

risks_watch: Raw material and commodity volatility (phenol, acetone, ammonia, crude) and the lag in passing on costs under long-term contracts.
Pricing competition in MEHQ from Chinese hydroquinone producers and possible new capacity from Vinati Organics and Gem Aromatics in anisole, MEHQ and BHA.
HQ/catechol plant ramp-up and yield norms; utilisation at about 10-15% still needs to improve.
Performance Chemical 2 commissioning slipping further due to manpower constraints.
Standalone revenue down 12% in FY26 after loss of a key FMCG account; sustained volume recovery needs to be confirmed in Q1 FY27.

Standalone revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR203 crore on realisation gains, while standalone sales fell 6% YoY on volume loss from raw-material and shipping disruptions, including about two weeks of production stoppage. qa_highlights.question: What drove HALS volume and pricing, and is the INR250-300 crore annual run-rate comfortable?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43-45% HALS gross margin sustainable, or helped by cheap acetone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no real benefit from cheap raw material; margins came from higher grades and operational efficiencies, and should be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Geneus Chem transaction and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech transfer for NOR HALS with no transfer fee or royalty (capex only); joint, co-branded marketing with geographic split. Management guided INR300-350 crore additional revenue cumulatively over 3-4 years, separate from direct sales outside the partner.

qa_highlights.question: What was the cause of the YoY decline in legacy volumes, and will volumes recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Propylene shortage at a primary Indian supplier forced about two weeks of shutdown. Management said volumes are not an issue now; raw material pricing and shipping availability remain challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Kemin 5-year contract add volume and need capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kemin is an existing 10-year customer; offtake expected to rise 20-40% starting in 2-3 months. Additional capacity is needed and the process has started; the benefit is supply security rather than pricing concessions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kemin and Geneus deals preempt new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no other Indian or global entrant is likely to enter this alliance given supply security, and that the contract covers BHA, BHT, TBHQ and AP.

qa_highlights.question: Is PC2 on track for September start and what is the ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said labour issues cause a delay; commercialisation expected around November, with stabilisation November-March and revenue from Q1 FY28.

Postpaid disbursal ramp is described as faster than the earlier launch, though no figures were given and management declined to comment on guidance. Net payment margin was about 9 bps, with management pointing to pricing discipline and credit instruments on UPI as drivers. Management said it will spend more on cashback and customer acquisition but within existing guidance, and that new investment will go only into AI, with no material capex plan yet. The company is not pursuing an NBFC licence and says the wallet licence remains a commitment without a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is left and what peak revenue can it support?

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken and what is the outlook for gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes are marginal and mostly domestic; international pricing close to zero. Management could not call the margin bottom given volatile raw material costs and said erosion is external rather than operational.

qa_highlights.question: What will it take to grow beyond 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees 20-22% as doable with new products, cell culture and export support; 15% is the base case including white labelling and contract manufacturing for export.

543412|2026-06.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.
543412|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed a fourth successive quarter of improving core underwriting profitability, with underwriting result at Rs 111 crore versus Rs 16 crore a year earlier. Reported PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore, while normalised PAT (8% investment yield basis) rose 44% to Rs 386 crore, giving annualised ROE of 15.6% versus 12.2%. Fresh retail GWP grew 37% YoY to Rs 730 crore on a 1/N basis, but retail market share slipped to 29% from 31%, which management attributed to long-term policy accounting and deliberate avoidance of riskier pools. Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

segments.commentary: Group share of GWP is now roughly 2.5%, down from about 5% a year earlier; management said group contributed part of the loss ratio improvement but retail also improved.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY, with 98% of customers new to insurance; D2C is 74% of digital fresh business.

Expense ratio expected to improve 30-40 bps consistently each year from technology and productivity investments.

Reinsurance cost expected to fall: the voluntary quota share treaty (2023-24 and 2024-25, three-year) is fading out, and obligatory treaty renegotiation with GICRE may bring benefits; FY28 net reinsurance benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%.
Q2 is seasonally higher for loss ratio; management expects the same trend this year. No loss ratio guidance given.

Fresh-business growth expected to moderate in H2 FY27 and into H1 FY28 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds; management agreed this framing.

Non-metro fresh business growth is 3.5x metro growth.
Customer app has about 16 million downloads and 1.5 million+ monthly active users.
97% of new applications are digitally sourced; generative AI being layered on existing AI/ML claims analytics.
Long-term policies are about 40% of retail fresh business; fresh-to-renewal share about 20:80 in insurance revenue.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is partly driven by the GST waiver; majority of fresh business comes from first-time buyers. Management expects moderation of optical growth rates.

Pricing is annual and product-by-product on a calendar; most pricing actions have been taken in Q4 over the last couple of years, with earned impact flowing through subsequent quarters. Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.
Retail claim settlement ratio 91%; over 9.5 lakh claims settled in the quarter, over 80% cashless.
Senior citizens are under 5% of the book; focus remains on younger cohorts.
Management is watching dengue, malaria and fever outbreaks; telemedicine and home healthcare used to manage these cases.

qa_highlights.question: How will GWP growth of 19% convert into insurance revenue growth, and when will they converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance revenue grew 13.4%; management expects 15-16% through the year as long-term policy earnings build, and higher growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers for loss ratio improvement and how many claims are settled via telemedicine?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combined approach: repricing, portfolio selection, claims fraud control, network management, wellness and teleconsultation. No telemedicine claim count was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the expense ratio improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects 30-40 bps annual expense ratio improvement from tech, digitisation and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of acquisition cost is employee expense and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is split three ways: claims-related in claims, sales-related in acquisition cost, and support costs in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinsurance impact on the expense ratio and what is the full-year benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance cost is falling as the quota share treaty fades; FY28 benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%, though management said this was hard to pin down.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow in H2 as the GST-driven base builds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that H2 FY27 and early FY28 growth could be lower on the high base, and said it will not chase growth for its own sake.

risks_watch: Seasonal Q2 loss ratio pressure from vector-borne and infectious diseases.
Regulatory changes to commissions and claims reforms; management declined to comment until rules are final.

Other expenses rose about 23% YoY to Rs 283 crore, driven by loss of GST input credit and annual rate hikes.
Accounting questions open: finance income under PAA on long-term contracts (Rs 38.8 crore) and DAC balance were not fully explained.

543412|2026-09.headline: Star Health Q2 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 99 crore from a Rs 40 crore loss, with PAT up over threefold to Rs 265 crore.
543412|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the fifth successive quarter of improving loss ratios and underwriting results, with CISR improving 2.9 points to 98%. Gross written premium on a reported 1/n basis grew 19% YoY to Rs 5,275 crore in Q2 and Rs 9,562 crore in H1, while fresh retail health GWP grew 35% in the quarter. Normalized PAT (at an 8% investment yield) rose 70% YoY to Rs 390 crore in Q2. Management flagged that headline growth will moderate in H2 as last year's GST-led surge enters the base, and that regulatory proposals on distribution commissions and expense of management (EoM) are the next key uncertainty.

segments.name: Retail health (fresh)
segments.commentary: Fresh retail GWP grew 35% YoY in Q2 and 36% in H1 on reported 1/n basis; new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% from 89%, with new-to-insurance policies up over 10% and average sum insured up 13%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Network reached 8.7 lakh agents after adding 39,000 in H1; agency productivity up 19% YoY; agency contributes about 70-75% of fresh business and grew about 25% in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C grew 137% YoY in H1 and its share of business rose from 8% to 13%; management says D2C has superior combined ratios. Proprietary channels (agency plus D2C) account for over 90% of retail business.

segments.name: Renewal book
segments.commentary: Management says the standalone renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio; vintage book is about 80% of portfolio. Group business is now a very small share of premium.

guidance_outlook: Company aspires to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently over a long period and hopes to maintain that for FY27, though optical growth moderation is expected in Q3 and Q4 due to GST-led base.
ROE ambition to move from mid-teens to higher-teens over time, with combined ratio as the key lever.
Retail market share and like-for-like comparability under 1/n reporting expected to be restored only by FY28.
Management believes it has a credible path to the proposed EoM limits through operating leverage, productivity and digitization, but will give more detail once regulation is final.
Company will not disclose point-to-point guidance on individual loss ratio metrics.
capex_capacity: Equity allocation about 14% (slightly less than 14%), with internal strategy to cap at around 15%; management may go beyond 15% if markets are very attractive.

Portfolio duration increased toward a target of about 4 years after G-Sec yields rose; management said it has taken some long-duration G-Sec calls and may extend duration further if yields keep rising.
REITs and InvITs: fully invested against the 3% regulatory limit with a small margin of safety; AIF allocation about 2.1-2.2% of funds and growing slowly.
Digital SBU created last year; Salesforce CRM upgraded; AI bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volume at under 20% of human cost.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is driven by a mix of price, volume and higher average sum insured; management did not split the contribution.
Around 80% of the book was repriced in the last cycle; the remaining portion is being repriced this year, with further correction as needed based on loss ratios.
Packages account for about 80% of claims; hospital negotiations described as business as usual, with the Supreme Court drug-pricing order not yet notified.
Management estimates a fresh-to-insurance market share near 40% (not a reported figure) and notes the reported fresh figure includes portability.
Commission ratio moderated YoY because the senior citizen commission cut (15% to 10%) and other efficiencies now show a full 12-month impact.

qa_highlights.question: How is fresh growth tracking in October and by channel, now that the GST-led base is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects optical moderation in Q3 and Q4 but aims for 20%+ fresh growth; it tracks policies sold, agent activations and digital activations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the loss ratio improvement driven by fresh business or by the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Improvement is driven by the vintage book (about 80% of portfolio), since the fresh book at about 20% of the portfolio could not drive it alone; renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio. Fresh and renewal loss ratios are not disclosed separately.

qa_highlights.question: Loss ratio decomposition in Q2 (frequency, severity, pricing) and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss cost held at mid-single-digit growth while earned premium grew close to double digits; management did not give point-to-point metric guidance and will focus on combined ratio going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Equity and duration positioning, and whether there is an equity cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity about 14%, no incremental purchases this quarter; the 15% level is an internal strategy, not a formal cap. Duration lengthened toward about 4 years via G-Sec calls.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company responding to the Rs 59 crore investment-related loss and its FVTPL classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity, ETFs, REITs and InvITs are classified as FVTPL; debt is held to maturity. No breakdown of the Rs 59 crore between realized and unrealized was provided in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the insurance finance income and expense restatement, and will it stay nil?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance finance income and expense (significant financing component on long-term policies) was discontinued as an optional treatment; it is now nil and has no PAT impact because the offsetting income sits in restated insurance revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How are multi-year policies commissioned, and what is the impact of the proposed distribution rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Multi-year policies are around 50% of the fresh book; good agents are paid upfront under Indian GAAP and the amount is deferred under IFRS; clarification is awaited on whether years two and three count as fresh or renewal under the new rules.

543415|2026-06.overview: Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the other income of INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.

543514|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 132 crore (up 52% YoY) and FY26 EBITDA of about INR 204 crore (up 135%). FY26 PAT of INR 130 crore compares with a loss of about INR 252 crore in FY25, and this was the fifth consecutive PAT-positive quarter. Management said FY26 guidance was broadly achieved, with non-commerce well ahead and commerce broadly in line. The J.K. Shah Commerce Education demerger is awaiting final NCLT approval, with listing targeted for end-July or mid-August 2026. FY27 guidance is revenue of about INR 670 crore and PAT above INR 144 crore.

segments.name: Non-commerce (government test prep and academic/K-12)
segments.commentary: Significantly outperformed estimates on government test prep traction and operational improvements. Government test prep posted a Q4 loss of about INR 3 crore after a one-time INR 5 crore impairment; the segment otherwise earned INR 2 crore EBITDA for the year.

segments.commentary: Divested into a joint structure with SNVA; Veranda accounts for 50% of SNVA's consolidated profit as an associate, not line-by-line. A North American entity remains in continuing operations (about INR 51 crore segment revenue) and is planned for eventual sale subject to RBI approvals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 670 crore, about 40% growth YoY.
FY27 PAT projected at over INR 144 crore (CEO said over INR 140 crore in closing).
Commerce FY27 EBITDA expected at INR 180-185 crore; management flagged a minor EBITDA margin dip in commerce from opening about 15 new colleges.

Commerce to reach INR 1,000 crore-plus revenue by FY30.

capex_capacity: Plan to add about 15 new B.Com/commerce colleges (managed portfolio) in FY27 across North and West India, versus 15-17 colleges currently.
Government test prep expansion into Karnataka in FY27, aiming to be the number one player in South India including Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
Academic segment: evaluating managed pre-KG schools and expanding managed K-12 schools.

qa_highlights.question: When will the J.K. Shah demerger list, and how will the listing unlock value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the NCLT hearing is on June 3, 2026, with the final order about 30 days later, then ROC filings and listing approvals; listing is expected by end-July or mid-August 2026. Management said the standalone commerce business is sharply focused and expected to carry a higher valuation multiple.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a vocational-division revenue of INR 51 crore still appear in consolidated results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one North American entity was not hived off with the divestment and remains with the non-commerce business; it is planned for eventual sale subject to RBI approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a Q4 loss in government test prep, and are there further impairments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a one-time INR 5 crore impairment was taken in Q4 following audit testing; the segment otherwise earned INR 2 crore EBITDA for the year. Management said goodwill and intangibles were tested and no further impairment was taken in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will the warrants issued for the BB Virtuals and Navkar acquisitions be treated on demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the warrants are yet to be subscribed, with the deadline in August 2026. If demerger happens before then, warrants will be split proportionately between the two entities on the same asset ratio, per the scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why will FY27 commerce EBITDA margin dip about 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to front-loaded opex for about 15 new colleges. Lease deposits and soft capex are capitalised in year one, while faculty and marketing are expensed; the first year is expected to be marginally breakeven, with benefits from year two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinvestment plan for surplus cash after debt repayment and demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash will fund commerce geographic expansion across all districts and new products including 11th-12th education, and non-commerce expansion in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, plus managed pre-KG and K-12 schools.

risks_watch: Demerger timing: NCLT final order and SEBI/exchange listing approvals; any slippage beyond July-August 2026.
Warrant overhang: about 75% of warrants remain to be subscribed before the August 2026 deadline.
Commerce margin dip in FY27 from the college expansion; watch whether the new colleges breakeven in year one as guided.
Operating risks flagged by management: lower CA pass rates, changes in exam frequency, site selection and faculty availability.
Asset allocation of about 35:65 between the entities is provisional and depends on the appointment date.
Possible further one-time charges; management said no further impairment was taken in FY26.
543514|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 targets, with clear timelines on the demerger. Evasive on the valuation split and the exact allocation of the commerce and non-commerce entities, saying figures will be set on the appointment date.
key_quotes: Importantly, we remain committed to the guidance shared with investors at the beginning of the year and successfully delivered largely in line with our stated expectations.

So the first year is an investment, which obviously we are taking charge on our P&L.
The future benefits of this is what is driving us to deliver potentially a INR 1,000 crores plus revenue for FY '30.

543514|2026-06.headline: Veranda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR150 crore and PAT to INR34 crore, with commerce demerger listing guided for September 2026.
543514|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to about INR150 crore and enrollments rose 35% to about 1.03 lakh students. EBITDA was about INR54 crore with a margin near 36% as stated, but management acknowledged the reported EBITDA growth of 10% was flattered by a INR17 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26; excluding it, EBITDA grew about 30%. PAT rose to INR34 crore from INR5.9 crore, helped by a INR7.35 crore tax reversal tied to an intra-group merger. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT, and said the Commerce demerger NCLT order is expected shortly with listing before end-September 2026.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven last quarter. Target of INR95-100 crore EBITDA over four to five years; Karnataka expansion planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable quarterly finance cost?

qa_highlights.question: Why did tax swing to a credit of about INR3 crore from about INR8 crore a quarter?

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline QoQ and how will FY27 38.8% margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubled college expansion spend, pre-demerger advertising for the commerce brand, and initial work on 15 new colleges, all expensed in Q1; expects benefit in next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of the NCLT approval and listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were reserved at the 20 July hearing; affidavit filed on the appointed date query; next hearing 17 August. Management expects order within about a week, then ROC filing in 3-4 days, a record date one week later, and listing before end-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-commerce be valued lower because it carries all the debt?

543517|2026-03.headline: Hariom Pipe FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR1,667 crore and EBITDA 19% to INR209 crore at a 12.56% margin, with FY27 volume guided at 350,000-360,000 tonnes.

Q4 revenue was INR507 crore (+27% YoY), Q4 EBITDA INR64 crore (+31%) and Q4 PAT INR30 crore (+75%). FY26 volume growth fell short of the 30% guided last year, as management prioritised margin and cash over volume. Management said a Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closure linked to a pollution board order had not yet hit volumes, citing stock and asset-light supply, and that reopening was expected within days.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capacity for about 30% growth on about 288,000 tonnes, subject to market conditions and no compromise on margins. Blended EBITDA is about INR7,200 per tonne, and management said it is confident of maintaining that level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu plant open, and what revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant awaits a reopening order within 2-3 working days, and April 2026 turnover matched April 2025 because of stock and asset-light supply. It said no non-compliance was found and that the closure followed election-period actions by the authorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar capex, debt and revenue roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Total project cost is about INR241 crore with INR195 crore bank debt and an equity component of INR25-30 crore; INR9.56 crore is invested so far. Management said the remainder is backed by central capital subsidy and that solar revenue will be quantified at Q1 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA per tonne or margin be the better guidance metric?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins of about 12.5-12.6% are sustainable and it focuses on profitability rather than volume. It said the EBITDA per tonne figure is not price-dependent in a fixed way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B share and the FY27 product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B was about 20% of sales in Q4, up from 15%. Management said the mix is coils across MS and GI, the focus is B2B plus dealers, and dealer addition is continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Metal Mart subsidiary have a start date?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supplier tie-ups are done and GST registrations are pending in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, with operations to start once registrations are received.

543523|2026-03.headline: Campus Activewear Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, EBITDA margin 19.2%, FY26 PAT margin 8.4%.
543523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, led by online (around 19%) and distribution (around 5.5%). EBITDA was INR 88.5 crore at a 19.2% margin (up 50 bps) and PAT was INR 44.1 crore at a 9.6% margin (up 100 bps). For FY26, revenue grew 11.4% to INR 1,774 crore, EBITDA margin rose 145 bps to 17.5%, and PAT margin rose 80 bps to 8.4%. Management said the mid-year raw material and minimum wage inflation was passed on via MRP hikes taken in early April, and that demand held up in April.

segments.name: Online (marketplace)
segments.commentary: Online grew about 19% in Q4 and 9.8% in FY26; management said all online business is pure marketplace except Flipkart, with Amazon, Snapdeal and brand.com growing faster. Online salience rose in Q4, though GT charges dilute gross margin and billing changed from 16 June to net of freight (INR 82 billed against INR 100 earlier).

segments.name: Distribution (general trade and franchise)
segments.commentary: Distribution grew about 5.5% in Q4 and 10.5% in FY26. Management said the annual distribution meet produced strong four-month forward orders, with AOP alignments with partners closed at over 100% of the target till September.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Sneaker portfolio grew about 100% YoY in FY26 and more than 50% in quarterly terms; the Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar units are producing about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27. Management did not disclose sneaker revenue or volume share.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated its EBITDA margin aspiration band of 17% to 19% for FY27 but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
Management said pricing taken in early April covers the inflation impact and that raw material prices have peaked and are starting to ease; no further price hikes expected.
Plan to open 60 to 80 new EBO stores in FY27 (about 40% COCO and 60% FOFO), after closing 9 to 10 and opening 13 to 14 stores in FY26; store count stood at about 300.
Marketing budget for FY27 set to be aggressive, focused on brand building rather than performance marketing.

Capex in FY27 expected to return to normal maintenance, mold, EBO and IT levels; Pant Nagar expansion including assembly lines is planned over the next three years, after first optimising the upper facility.
Full BIS compliance expected by 31 July 2026, with very little BIS stock remaining.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share of shoes priced below INR 1,000 rise versus Q4 FY25, and is the pricing MRP or realised price?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the figures are realised ASP; the shift reflects MRP corrections after GST on footwear was revised from 12% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What size of price hike was taken and will it suffice against inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined to give the percentage, said hikes were taken proportionately across the range and are enough to cover raw material and minimum wage inflation; peak RM seen, prices to ease in about a quarter, with no price reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses (ex-ad spend) rise only about 5% despite online growth of 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited dynamic online commission negotiations and event-based waivers, plus flat store count meaning no new EBO costs; other costs grew in the 5-6% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lease cash outflow rise sharply, nearly 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Pant Nagar land is a 71-year state government lease treated as lease liability payment; normalised FY26 rent excluding INR 65.4 crore is the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise 5-6 days in FY26 and where will they go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FG inventory was at a very minimal level last year and was rebuilt to the right level by March 2026, which will be maintained going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for sneaker growth, and what is the path to 2 lakh pairs a month?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said capacity is not a constraint now; Pant Nagar can reach 6 lakh pairs per month after two phases and HRD2 can reach 2 lakh (already running), targeting 8-9 lakh pairs per month in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins reach the 17-19% band or slip to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; CEO said the company will endeavour to stay within the 17-19% range guided earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBO expansion plan and capex for stores and facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said 60-70 or about 80 new stores are planned after closing 9-10 and opening 13-14 in FY26; CFO said FY27 capex reverts to normal maintenance, mould, EBO and IT levels, with Pant Nagar expansion over three years.

qa_highlights.answer: CEO said order bookings were strong on a four-month forward basis, numbers not shared; COO said AOP alignments with distributors were closed at over 100% till September.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to online billing change from 16 June (INR 82 billed against INR 100) with freight of INR 18 billed directly by portals, which is not in last year's Q4.

Q4 revenue was about INR317 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier. Management is guiding to a 35-40% revenue CAGR over three to five years and is expanding capacity in EMS, AC, refrigeration and compressors, with the new compressor line in commercial production since January 2026.

financial_highlights.change: from INR240 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: described as normal, in line with expectations

segments.name: Air conditioners (AC)
segments.commentary: Share of revenue fell from about 70-75% to about 60% in FY26; ODM share of AC revenue was 40-50%. Company now has 4 AC customers and expects 1-2 new names next season. Average realisation about INR20,000-20,000-odd per unit.

segments.name: EMS and lighting
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue; running at 70-80% utilisation through the year. Capacity to rise from 4 lakh CPH to 8 lakh (phase 1, by about end-August 2026) and 12 lakh (phase 2, by FY-end).

segments.name: Commercial refrigeration / defreezers
segments.commentary: About 10% of revenue; utilisation about 60%. Capacity 1.5 lakh units to 2.5 lakh (phase 1) and 4 lakh (phase 2); glass-top range added alongside hardtop. Target RAC-type growth of 30-40% in FY27.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue and rising; a major contributor to margin protection in the first nine months.

segments.name: Compressors (reciprocating, new subsidiary Virtuoso Compressors)
segments.commentary: Commercial production began January 2026 at about 60% utilisation on 2.8 million capacity, targeting about 80% in 2-3 months; expansion to 6 million by March 2027. Average realisation INR1,400-1,500; FY27 margin guided at 6-7%; value addition 5-10%.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 35-40% over three to five years, applied to the INR825 crore base; management said it is not revising guidance, with exact numbers to be shared during the year.

PAT margin expected to improve by 50-100 bps over the next two years as Ind AS adjustments fade.
Compressor margin 6-7% in FY27, potentially above double digits over 2-4 years as Chinese imports restrict and backward integration rises (11-12% in 4-5 years).
RAC utilisation target of 60-65% and volume growth of about 30-40% in FY27.
Chennai plant expected to contribute about 5-6% of volume in its first year.
Peak-utilisation revenue capacity from the current expansion is good for beyond INR2,500 crore, but management said reaching that from INR800 crore in two years is a big ask and will take more time.
HoldCo net debt addition of about INR50-60 crore in FY27; INR150 crore debt at the compressor subsidiary; INR250 crore equity approval is a blanket enabling approval, not a fundraising commitment.
capex_capacity: Compressors: capacity 2.8 million to 6 million by March 2027 (9-10 month build), INR150 crore phase-1 investment, already tied up; long-term target 8-8.5 million, with 7.5 million or 9.5 million considered if demand and contracts materialise.
AC: capacity about 1 million to 1.8 million by end FY27, with 1.3 million targeted before the next AC season; investment INR40-50 crore, mainly debt-funded, with some debt already tied up.
EMS: new advanced facility; phase 1 by end-August 2026 and phase 2 by FY-end; investment about INR25 crore, tied up.

Compressor separate manufacturing facility planned at Nasik; development work to start shortly. New Nasik tool room operational.
demand_pricing: Raw-material pass-through about 10-15% across the industry from manufacturers to brands and to consumers; management said margin pressure was offset by customer price hikes, new customers, old inventory, subsidies and product diversification.

Government restricts reciprocating compressor imports to 40% of FY24-25 base-year levels, meaning 50-60% of OEM/ODM requirement must be sourced locally; the company says it is the only OEM/ODM player currently doing this.

Two competitors expected to start local compressor manufacturing (one by end-Q3/Q4 FY27, one mid-2027). Management estimates a market gap of 14-15 million units against total planned capacity of 15-18 million.
Demand described as strong for AC; April-June 2026 expected to be an excellent quarter for RAC. Management said AC demand runway is long because the base is small.

Profitability was weak: EBITDA was negative ₹4.2 crore and PAT negative ₹3 crore (including non-cash ESOP costs), and expenses rose 18% to ₹25.4 crore as sales headcount and product investment expanded. Management highlighted deferred revenue at an all-time high of ₹38.8 crore (+6% QoQ), paying accounts up 16% to 2,350, and new vertical/BU playbook launches that it said are lifting win rates. Management said margins should expand non-linearly once growth re-accelerates, but gave no timeline for positive EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Roadmap to positive EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin expansion is predictable once growth re-accelerates, citing an example where ₹20 crore of incremental revenue drove ₹15 crore of incremental EBITDA in one year. No timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been flat since March 2023 and when will the recovery show?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the slowdown to VC deal activity at a 10-year low; the company prioritised IB and other segments, which now grow at 20–30% QoQ, and the blended rate has improved to about 19% QoQ-annualised from 14%.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition evaluated, given Bloomberg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bloomberg serves public-market users and is rarely used by private-market investors; the global competitive set is about three to four players.

qa_highlights.question: What drives IB success and what else is working?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the three-phase playbook (specialised BU, product augmentation, scale-up) lifted IB to about 30% QoQ growth and is being replicated across about five or six verticals in the UK, US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: How big is VC now as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: VC was about one-third of revenue at peak; it is now lower, but management did not disclose the exact percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Americas declining and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is cyclical (VC deal volumes), not structural, and that US/UK specialised teams are now being replicated internationally with QoQ growth turning positive.

qa_highlights.question: Net adds and realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60 net new paying accounts QoQ; ASP of ₹3.6 lakh per account per year has slightly declined on mix but is now stabilising.

543653|2026-03.headline: Bikaji Q4 FY26 revenue grew close to 18% to about INR720 crores, with FY26 revenue of INR2,994 crores and 9.5% volume growth.

Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.

543985|2026-03.headline: Zaggle FY26 standalone revenue rose about 42% to INR1,853 crores, but FY27 standalone growth guidance slows to 25-30% as DICE moves to an asset purchase.

Price hikes, lower schemes and discounts limited the QoQ gross margin decline to 150 bps. Cost pressure is expected to ease over the next three quarters, with an EBITDA margin target of 17-18% for the year. Q1 impact was about 1.5% from input costs, against an earlier 100-200 bps estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Pens grew 9% versus the ~5% CAGR guided last quarter, while Creatives grew 23% against the ~50% signalled. What went wrong in Creatives?

Pens growth was driven by Flair and Hauser brand pull, and the company said it had previously guided to high single digit. Revenue guidance of 15% was reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and inventory outlook, and the impact of the new ERP system?

The ERP is expected to be fully operational within 2-3 months, with inventory benefits to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the INR214 crore net NPA and INR196 crore guarantee cover on Slide 10, and claim timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is CASA growth of 7% QoQ sustainable and what is the FY27 CASA ratio target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 7% QoQ cannot be sustained every quarter; YoY CASA growth is about 31%. The CASA ratio target is about 20%, with CASA growth expected to exceed term deposit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds and cost-to-income outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds to stay in a 7.3-7.4% range as bulk and retail growth and modest rate increases offset each other. Cost-to-income is 66.7-67% now and should move to 63-65% during the year, not below 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of promoter (holding company) liquidity and rating downgrade.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no financial or operational impact, with no cross-default linkage, no common board members and no obligation on the bank to service promoter debt. The holding company holds 16.9%, down from a peak of 44%; CARE did not place the bank on watch.

risks_watch: Deposit franchise: flat QoQ deposits and about 6% bulk runoff against the 23-25% growth guidance, with H1 results expected to show progress.
MFI concentration at about 27% of the book; 79.8% of unsecured is guarantee-backed, and CGMFU claims timing (INR65 crore in Q3) matters.
Micro LAP declined in Q1 and NBFC book is shrinking by design; both need to turn positive to hit the 19-21% loan growth target.
Promoter-level stress: holding company and JCL rating downgraded by India Ratings after an NCD share-sale deadline extension; the bank says there is no direct impact.
Government deposit recovery is uncertain; the timing of flows from the state government is unclear.
Macro factors such as the Iran conflict, El Nino and gold price moves; management says no visible impact so far.
544118|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on asset quality, credit cost and the guarantee cover. Noticeably cautious on deposits and liquidity, with April-May described as difficult and growth recovery deferred to H1 results. Management was evasive on the merger rumour ("no comment on market speculation").

I think the opportunity to drop cost of funds is now over.
I do want to bring cost income back to much lower levels before the year is over.
We're at a good point now where we're doing 99%, plus or minus 0.1% since December.

544118|2026-09.headline: Jana SFB raised FY27 PAT growth guidance to 100% (from 80%) after Q2 posted its highest-ever PBT; H1 PAT of INR 326 crore equals full-year FY26 PAT.
544118|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the bank's highest-ever quarterly PBT, with H1 PAT of INR 326 crore equal to FY26 full-year PAT. NIM rose to 7.54% from 6.5% a year ago and cost of funds fell to 7.4% from 7.9%. Gross NPA improved to 2.17% but net NPA rose to 1.08%, which management expects to fall below 1% once INR 68 crore of CGFMU guarantee claims are realised. Advances grew 22% YoY to INR 38,752 crore, while CASA growth of 13% YoY lagged deposits at 17.5% TD growth and remains a focus area.

qa_highlights.question: Will slippages trend up or down in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower slippages in Q3 and H2. Q2 had one-offs: a secured loan slippage adding about 0.2% and drought-related MFI slippage of about 0.3%. SMA has graduated down in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 insurance income is credit life and what is the IRDAI consultation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: 80-90% is credit life, 10-20% retail products. Initial IRDAI assessment done; full assessment pending. Management will push penetration and AI-led cost efficiency to offset lower commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cost-to-income decline sustainable and can it fall below 60%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost-to-income expected to stay at or below the September level; management is cautious that sub-60% is unlikely this year. Drivers are productivity, RPA/AI processes and more direct sourcing over DSA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASA outlook and cost of funds risk from rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: CASA fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms but grew 13% YoY; management targets about 20% CASA in H2 via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January. Cost of funds targeted to stay near 7.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guarantee scheme cover the full book and what if it does not?
qa_highlights.answer: Claims of INR 68 crore lodged; NGC expected to pay within about 2 months. CGFMU is not open for fresh guarantees yet, but 1% cover cost has been accrued. If the scheme fails, the accrual becomes a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold loan and micro LAP flat, and when will growth pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold flat due to 6-month loans from Jan-Mar 2026 renewing in Q2 and gold price drop; growth expected to resume in Q3 at about 10% a quarter. Micro LAP may reach 7-8% growth but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Any risks to achieving 100% PAT growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no visible constraint on H2 profit matching H1; credit costs, asset growth and liability growth were all cited as on track.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM move in H2 amid rising rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM around current levels, as MFI share is not rising faster and secured share only reaches about 75%; cost of funds should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook by segment and do drought and geopolitical risks affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME 25-30% growth, affordable housing and vehicles continue strongly. Drought declared in 29 Karnataka districts and 34 Maharashtra districts; slippage impact expected to be immaterial. No material impact from the Iran war so far.

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution PAT margin range of 1.5-1.75% is typical absent mix change; Q4 gross margin dip was due to additional provisioning for slow-moving inventory, not a structural decline.

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation of the existing stabilizer capacity and the threshold to sustain margins?

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-40% still maintained, and how much Egypt revenue is included?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-40% growth for FY27 and said the company is already on track, though demand was weak due to the war. Egypt is only partly included: FY27 Egypt estimate is cut to INR 30-35 crore from INR 50-60 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Oleo revenue potential over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Oleo target is INR 65-70 crore and the three-year target is INR 150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Lubrizol and Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity on Platinum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in lead-free and CPVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook versus the roughly 23% margins of FY23-FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to a mix shift from high-margin lead-free to lower-margin CPVC, which started at a 3-7% contribution margin. Guidance is PAT margin of 11-12% and EBITDA margin of 13-15%, reiterated from the previous call.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise capex, timelines and revenue potential for Egypt and Palghar?
qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6,000 tpa stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026 from August due to a delay in one equipment item. Management said it would not materially affect FY27 revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: Egypt versus Palghar capex and why revenue potential differs?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental working capital needed for Egypt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly a three-month working capital cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Expected margins in Oleo chemicals in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to rise after the company builds its own manufacturing facility; for now it is using CDMO for seed marketing.

qa_highlights.question: How defensible is the domain-knowledge moat against LLM commoditization?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the moat is domain expertise plus proprietary data, with multiple frontier models and specialist AI partners orchestrated together. It said LLMs are not reliable enough for regulated operating-grade work over the next 3 to 5 years, so human-in-the-loop remains necessary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk that AI investment keeps margins from recovering?

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth drivers and what would be different?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a strategy for small and mid-size pharma and generics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is expanding rapidly in mid-size and small companies, with launch models for small biotechs. Generics contribute some revenue, but innovator pharma is prioritised because of the $100 million client opportunity.

Tech infrastructure, systems, manufacturing, digital platforms

segments.name: Jettings (acquired subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹19.22 cr (+7%); EBITDA up over 18%. Employee cost down 20% and operating expenses down 11%, while purchases rose 41.5% to about ₹9 cr. Interest cost is the remaining weak point due to working capital intensity.

segments.name: Government tenders and automation projects
segments.commentary: Two government tenders were won last year and more are in the pipeline. Management says project business is multi-month, high-ticket and built around a separate North and South team.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated sustainable double-digit medium-term growth but did not give a near-term number, and said margins take priority over top-line growth.
Management said it expects to hold the current EBITDA margin (about 13-14%) in FY27 and does not plan to chase top-line growth at the expense of margins.

Capex is split broadly as 41% infrastructure capacity, 30% exports and global expansion, 8% tech and ERP, 3% R&D and 5% product development and other initiatives. The absolute amount is still under board consideration.
Management said the full-year effect of recent investments will show up in FY27, and free cash flow is expected to rise with that.
capex_capacity: Capex is planned over the coming period across infrastructure capacity (41%), exports and global expansion (30%), tech and ERP (8%), R&D (3%) and other product development (5%). The absolute rupee amount has not been disclosed.

Management said the capex was deferred because of Middle East conflict visibility, and it was not committing advances until the outlook clears.

qa_highlights.question: Installed base of 8,000+ printers versus 1,550 sold in FY26 does not reconcile with the prior 5,000+ base.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook: why should double-digit growth return after the 9.2% in FY26?

qa_highlights.question: Jettings acquisition: benefits achieved and performance versus plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Jettings' revenue rose 7% to ₹19.22 cr and EBITDA margin rose to 10.2%, with lower employee and operating costs. It said the interest cost is still high because of working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: Government tenders and automation: size and timing of contribution?

qa_highlights.question: Capex amount and funding?

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Iran/Middle East conflict on raw material prices and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory was built only to customers' absorption capacity, and that service-linked AMCs make it easier to pass through costs. It expects the disruption to ease but said post-ceasefire effects can last 3-5 months.

risks_watch: Revenue growth of 9.2% fell short of the earlier double-digit framework, and PAT growth was held back by depreciation, write-offs and tax.
Supply chain: heavy reliance on imported printheads and electronic components; management acknowledged this and cited a Taiwan Strait scenario as a risk.
Equity dilution: management said equity is still under consideration, while an analyst argued against it given the market capitalisation of about ₹123 cr versus reserves of about ₹44 cr.

544177|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on margins and cash generation, but cautious on top-line growth and capex. It repeatedly deferred to later disclosure on capex size, indigenisation progress and the printer count reconciliation, and it answered several questions only partly.
key_quotes: The strategy of Astec is very simple: we would be providing the world-class solutions at the price which is a win-win for both Astec and the customer, and whatever we commit, we deliver.
We won't be focusing on exorbitant increase in top line, we would be focusing more on our margin profiles.
So we are very cautious in managing our cash, we are very cautious in deploying our resources as far as the CAPEX is concerned.

544179|2026-03.headline: Go Digit reports 17.7% post-tax ROE on Indian Accounting Standards basis for FY26 and a 105.7% combined ratio, with GDPI up 16.2%.
544179|2026-03.overview: Management presented FY26 results re-based to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS, effective 1 April 2026), which were audited for the first time, while stressing its internal KPIs remain NEP-based combined ratio plus DAC and IGAAP solvency. Full-year profit before tax on Ind AS plus DAC was INR239 crores in Q4 (vs INR142 crores) and post-tax profit was INR179 crores (vs INR106 crores). Q4 GDPI grew 21.3% and full-year GDPI grew 16.2%, while Q4 GWP growth slowed to about 6.2% because of a health reinsurance non-renewal. Solvency improved to 2.42 and AUM reached about INR23,000 crores (up 16.3%). Management said it sees motor pricing correcting in April and expects a regulatory response on expense of management (EOM) within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Private car 44%, two-wheeler 32%, commercial vehicles 24% of business. OD/TP mix 38/62 vs industry 41/59. Own-damage loss ratio rose YoY; corrective action started, with impact expected from July-September quarter.

segments.name: Health (incl. group)
segments.commentary: Q4 health reinsurance non-renewal cost about INR252 crores (about INR200 crores in Q3). Retail is under 7% of health; employer-employee about 73% and non-employer-employee about 22%. Health market share about 1.3-1.4%.

segments.name: Fire / commercial
segments.commentary: Fire gross loss ratio 51% in FY26 vs 48% in FY25; net loss ratio rose on two large claims (INR55 crores gross in Q4). Cat treaty retention raised from INR36 crores to INR45 crores; earthquake limit raised from INR1,600 crores to INR2,000 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Q4 two-wheeler premium was INR556 crores vs INR365 crores a year earlier, which pushed up EOM by about 3.5% in the quarter. Management estimates about 40% of FY26 two-wheeler business was new business.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management plans to bid directly in government crop tenders this year, having previously written crop mainly through reinsurance acceptance; scheme structure not yet announced.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no numerical guidance; it said ROE and profitability are the focus.
Motor OD loss ratio expected to stabilise in July-September 2026 quarter and then fall; motor overall loss ratio targeted not to rise YoY in FY27.
New specialty commercial lines expected to reach about INR1,000 crores premium over 3-5 years.
Equity allocation at 8.5% of AUM with a 12.5% ceiling considered comfortable; fixed income duration at 4.5 years, with room to extend if rates rise.
Management expects EOM-related regulation within 2-3 months and expects the commission/management-expense split to be fixed.
Next year's effective tax rate expected at 25.2%.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance renewed for FY27: fire and other treaty capacity increased; property and engineering capacity raised with better commission terms.
A new miscellaneous treaty covers new risk types; an 11% quota share on non-motor, non-health premium was added to cap accumulation in Gujarat, Maharashtra and NCR.
Net retention for scooters and school buses was lowered through funds-withheld reinsurance after the Kolkata incident; management said this does not affect AUM.
Leverage rose to 5% (4.65% in June 2024); management expects it to hold around 5% over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Motor: management sees April 2026 price and commission correction in the market, and believes the market cannot sustain current prices. Growth outlook depends on the new-vehicle cycle, which was strong in H2 FY25.
Fire: softer terms seen in fire, but not in engineering, where growth was higher than fire. Fire market share about 3.9% on GWP.
Health: management plans to grow group health only if pricing improves by about 5%, and expects growth of 50-60% if loss ratio also falls by about 2%.
TP pricing: no motor TP hike this year; management said it is not privy to regulator thinking.
Competition: new non-life entrants are coming; management said it is not losing sleep over them and that EOM relief for new insurers should be split between commission and management expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will fire profitability fall given higher cat reinsurance cost, net loss ratio deterioration, and a possibly softer fire market? Also, what is the crop strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with fire profitability, citing better commission in fire and engineering and profit commission on earned premium. Crop: will bid directly in tenders this year, pending government scheme structure.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fairfax keep its stake after the reverse merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not spoken to Fairfax and said there is no news on the amalgamation timeline. Fairfax holds about 58%; going below 51% would trigger an open offer, and management does not expect a sale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the new specialty commercial lines and what is the motor pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lines could reach about INR1,000 crores of premium in 3-5 years. Motor market correction in April 2026 on price and commission; overall motor loss ratio to be held flat or lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did motor OD loss ratio rise and what is the retention and renewal data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management delayed corrective OD pricing to test retention and sold more SAOD in FY25. Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%. Renewal rates rose in private car across channels.

qa_highlights.question: How will EOM compliance be managed at company level and how does Indian acquisition cost compare internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said line-of-business mix explains the EOM gap and expects regulation to ease expense limits within 2-3 months. Management said Indian acquisition costs have risen over 20 years and cited RBI and Economic Survey commentary.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the discounting benefit and will long-run Ind AS investment yield match IGAAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount-rate effect is stable unless rates move sharply; it moved to 7.09% from 6.9%. Management said investment decisions should be judged on ROE, not on mark-to-market, and that risk-based capital may favour companies with high equity allocation.

risks_watch: Own-damage motor loss ratio: corrective action is due to show from July-September 2026; the next two quarters are the test.
Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%; watch renewal rates and whether the market price correction affects volume.
Fire net loss ratio: two large claims lifted net loss ratio; the cat reinsurance cost rise may compress margins.
EOM regulation: timing and form of relief are unclear, and new entrants may bring forbearance on EOM.
Health: non-renewal of a reinsurance treaty cut Q4 GWP growth to 6.2%; health loss ratios remain a question.

Ind AS vs IGAAP comparability: the DAC unwind (about 65% of INR2,470 crores in FY26-27), the 25.2% tax rate, and the non-booking of INR303 crores of unearned premium (INR109 crores acquisition cost provided) will affect reported profit.
Fixed income duration and rates: duration is 4.5 years; an interest rate move could affect unrealised losses (INR99 crores at 31 March 2026).
544179|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and defensive on reported numbers, pushing the Ind AS/DAC-based KPIs and ROE. Management was evasive on Fairfax, motor pricing timing, and specialty-line sizing, and offered no hard guidance.
key_quotes: And I think for all of you, analysts and fund managers, making comparisons would also become a lot more easier.
So on a loss ratio plus commission basis, which is how we always look at any product or any line of business, we should be seeing some improvement anyway.
Am I losing sleep because of new competition? Not really.
And if you feel that our loss ratio would be worse than anyone else in the market, we'll be more than happy to learn and put more pressure on our management team, including Jasleen to improve.

544179|2026-06.headline: Go Digit's Q1 FY27 GDPI fell 8% and loss ratio rose to 73.3%, with management choosing profitability over growth.
544179|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a deliberately soft quarter, with gross written premium down 8% (about -2% excluding inward reinsurance in group health and crop). Motor own damage, mainly private car, drove the loss ratio up from 70.3% to 73.3%, and management said it had made the wrong call on the stand-alone OD renewals. On its internal KPI basis (NEP with DAC, excluding MTM and discounting), PAT was INR190 crore versus INR200 crore a year ago and combined ratio was 107.2%. Under Indian Accounting Standards (IFRS-style prescribed format), PAT rose to INR372 crore from INR325 crore, helped by unrealised gains and discounting.

financial_highlights.change: About -2% excluding inward reinsurance exits in group health and crop
