segments.name: Motor own damage (private car)
segments.commentary: Primary driver of the loss ratio increase; management cut stand-alone OD and non-new car business, with stabilisation expected in Q2 FY27. Motor overall grew 0.4%, with 2-wheeler growing strongly and private car and CV together down about 27%.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: CV share of motor fell to about 23-24% from roughly 65% four to five years ago, as the company deliberately exited the segment.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: GDPI down 37% against an industry decline of about 27-28%. Gross fire loss ratio was 67% in Q1 despite one large claim; retention is about 20%.

segments.name: Third-party motor
segments.commentary: TP loss ratio 66.6%, broadly stable. Market share was cut from April, with a view that a TP rate hike of 90-95% of vehicles is needed.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Loss ratio rose year on year, attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy. Group health and crop inward reinsurance were not renewed on pricing grounds.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not guide and will not assume that market conditions normalise in the current or next quarter.
Management is assuming soft market conditions persist at least until 31 March 2027.
Own damage loss ratio expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.
Management said that, excluding the drop in fire, the fourth quarter could see a base effect on growth.
Dividend: management said IGAAP solvency (about 242%) supports a dividend, to be considered by the Board in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms.
Underwriting and claims-settlement actions on TP were planned for around the third week of August 2026.
capex_capacity: Investment mix: 9.5% of AUM in equity, REITs and InvITs (AT1 bonds shown separately); management said it could take equity to 13-14% if markets fall, or to 15-18% in its stated framework.
Fixed income duration moved from 4.5 to 4.9 in Q1; reinvestment yield rose to 7.8% from 7.5%. Management said it would extend duration to about 5.2 if the 30-year yield moves above about 7.75%.
Reinsurance commission increased across all lines and reinsurance capacity increased, per management.
Management said it is waiting for RBC norms, expected possibly within FY27, to know whether solvency will be measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing across most lines has fallen and is now down across the board. It cited EOM rules, which pushed commissions up, and low-priced crop, group health, and fire business written to meet EOM.
Claims inflation: no third-party motor rate increase for about five years, while minimum wages, parts, paint and labour costs have risen.
Fire rates were said to be down about 40-45%.
Management said Digit has not chased growth; it gave up fire and commercial business it judged underpriced, and said the 2W and bancassurance/digital channels were growing well.

Supreme Court (June 11, 2026) TP ruling: management said it is comfortable with reserves and will not take a bet on judgment interpretation; two High Court rulings (July 2 Allahabad, July 16 Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GDPI slowdown since listing size-driven or structural from industry and competitive change, and does it require investment in other channels or lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman attributed it to EOM rules pushing commissions up and low-priced crop, group health and fire business written to meet EOM; said Q1 is the first quarter Digit lost market share, and that bancassurance, institutional and digital/B2C channels are growing well. Management is assuming soft conditions persist until at least 31 March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 11 June 2026 Supreme Court TP ruling on TP loss ratio and reserving, and is the step-up recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reserving is based on loss ratio plus legal inflation and frequency, with no separate provision; it is comfortable with reserves and takes no bet on judgment interpretation. Two High Court rulings (2 July Allahabad, 16 July Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling; underwriting and claim-settlement actions were planned for around the third week of August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are there one-off or large losses in fire, marine and engineering this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman confirmed one large fire claim in Q1, but said gross fire loss ratio was 67%; he argued loss ratios are assessed on a gross basis because 80% of fire risk is ceded to reinsurers, and the company gives up treaty commission on some business to protect treaty profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI-driven TP hike needed, and what would be the quantum? What is the dividend policy given solvency and IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 90-95% of vehicles need a TP premium hike, with a view that only about 5% of segments could see reductions; it is running the book without assuming a hike. On dividends, IGAAP solvency is about 242% and the Board will consider a dividend in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms (expected possibly this financial year).

qa_highlights.question: Is the TP claim-settlement approach (83% by compromise) adequate given 17% court awards, and will reserve releases be lower after the Supreme Court ruling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 36,000 TP claims settled since inception, 83% by compromise and 17% by court award; it reported reserve release of INR204 crore for FY18-19 falling to INR132 crore over later years, said no MAD concept is used, and declined to guide on future releases. Motor actuarial review of frequency was expected in 3-5 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the OD loss ratio increase, and why was it not anticipated?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said he took the wrong call by holding stand-alone OD renewals and new-car business written in FY24-25; the problem is in private car, not 2W or CV, and the portfolio was cut sharp from March. OD loss ratio is expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did group health loss ratio rise, and what drove NEP retention and EOM trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health rise was attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy, with claims provided for. Retention rose from a mix of higher retention in commercial lines and lower fire mix; EOM rose slightly at motor level due to exits from low-EOM fire and commercial business and non-renewal of group health and crop inward reinsurance.

risks_watch: Motor own damage loss ratio (73.3% group, private car driven) must stabilise in Q2 FY27 as guided; a miss would extend the margin pressure.
TP reserve adequacy post Supreme Court ruling (11 June 2026): watch the August 2026 underwriting and claim-settlement actions, the review petition, and further High Court interpretations.
Growth trajectory: GDPI down 8% (about -2% ex inward reinsurance); management expects a base effect from Q4 but gave no guidance and assumes soft market through 31 March 2027.
Investment-income dependence: equity raised to 9.5% of AUM at book value; unrealised equity gains of INR268 crore could reverse, and PBT was reduced by INR14 crore from the allocation shift.

Regulatory items: RBC norms timing and whether solvency is measured on RBC, IFRS or IGAAP; EOM, commission and distribution reforms; a possible TP premium hike that management says it has not assumed.
Fire: GDPI down 37% with rates down 40-45%; management says it has cut underpriced business, so watch fire retention and the treaty renewal.
key_quotes: We decided to focus on maintaining profitability. So for us, this is a soft quarter and much of it is soft by choice.
I would say in hindsight, I made the wrong call.
We do not chase growth. That does not pay for itself.
We don't take a bet. We basically look at where the market is.
544179|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and combative on strategy, with management openly framing Q1 as a deliberate choice of profitability over growth and admitting a wrong call on stand-alone OD renewals. It was cautious on guidance, declining to give any and avoiding quantification on TP reserve releases, while being evasive on the RBC and dividend timing.

544181|2026-03.headline: Awfis FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR1,493 crore and EBITDA 37% to INR550 crore, with FY27 guided to 25-27% revenue growth.
544181|2026-03.overview: Awfis reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR1,493 crore (up 24% YoY) and operating EBITDA of INR550 crore (up 37%, margin 36.8%), with PAT before exceptionals up 66% to INR71 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR410 crore (up 21%) with EBITDA of INR152 crore (margin 37%). The company deliberately slowed seat additions to focus on Grade A/A+ premium centers, with gross seat additions of about 30,000 and net addition of about 22,000 in FY26. Design and build (Transform) revenue was softer, though its third-party business grew.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR11 crore in Q4 FY25 (+107%)

Net cash through FY26; net debt to equity -0.20; gross debt to equity 0.09

segments.name: Coworking and allied services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,237 crore (+35% YoY); Q4 revenue INR342 crore (+27% YoY, +6% QoQ). Management said it met both revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY26.

segments.commentary: FY26 softer on project timing and fewer managed aggregation deals. Third-party revenue rose from INR95 crore (FY25) to INR152 crore (FY26), with third-party share at 59% (from 47%). Net D&B margin about 7-8%. INR130 crore of mandates won for delivery over the next 6-7 months.

segments.name: Frame by Awfis (furniture)

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross seat additions appear to be 26,000 when the sum of quarterly guidance was lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross additions were about 30,000 seats, with about 8,000 closed, giving a net addition of about 22,000 (157,000 operational seats vs about 135,000 a year earlier). Seat additions were kept low by a focus on quality over quantity.

qa_highlights.question: Will premiumization be a one-time shift, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premiumization is now the default and non-negotiable, not a one-time step. Growth is driven by realization per seat, with FY27 revenue guided at about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of D&B and the revenue-to-rent ratio?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in lease principal payments in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the 30,000 seats added in FY26 and late-FY25 centers coming off rent-free periods, plus renewal escalations. No average escalation percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the approximately 5% seat closure rate in FY26 a normal churn level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was a portfolio rebalancing year. About 3,000 seats were a single-client short-term setup, and the rest were exits at renewal or from older buildings below the Grade A+ bar. Management said 5% is not the churn rate it expects going forward.

544226|2026-03.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.

544232|2026-03.headline: Interarch FY26 revenue rose 31% to Rs 1,898 crore; FY27 guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore, with order book at Rs 1,700 crore.

segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution from new products such as steel mill rollers and VRM rollers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (tungsten, cobalt, nickel) on fixed-price contracts; gross margin pressure in FY27 with a lag in passing through costs.
Standalone profitability: Q4 standalone PAT fell 3.05% YoY despite revenue growth, and standalone growth depends on Unit 4 commissioning on schedule by end of Q1 2027.
Receivable days at 98 in FY26 with heavy-engineering payment cycles of 75-90 days; management's 80-85 target needs to be met.
Quarterly concentration: Q4 is seasonally large, and management expects Q4 to remain the biggest quarter.
Tejorup defence and railway developmental businesses carry lower initial margins and long gestation periods.
Management's stated 20%+ FY27 growth and 80-100 bps margin expansion are to be tracked against Q1 FY27 results.

More cautious and specific on raw material pass-through and receivables, where answers relied on contract structure and time lags. Declined to quantify new product revenue, citing confidentiality.

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
544264|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. EBITDA margin eased to 12.85% from 13.12%, which management attributed to higher raw material and employee costs as a share of sales. Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.name: Heavy Engineering
segments.commentary: Order book of INR159 crores at 30 June 2026. Management says ~70% of heavy engineering is new project build and ~30% spare parts for installed base; capacity being raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons.

segments.name: Wear Plates and Wear Parts
segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Contributes approximately 1.5% to 2% of revenue. Management said it has not yet won competitive bids for subassemblies; Tejorup (10% stake) is developing a VSHORADS prototype.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.
Management expects Q2 FY27 growth at similar levels to Q1, supported by seasonal monsoon-linked maintenance demand.
More than 80% of the INR209 crore order book is executable in FY27; customers are asking to prepone deliveries.
Railway (Vande Bharat, locomotives) revenue expected to convert within 9-12 months after workshop approval; management said new development items are a longer gestation cycle.
No new capex finalised; management wants to start the next expansion once newly installed capacity reaches 70-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore expansion program across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, with new strip slitting capability for backward integration.
Heavy engineering capacity being expanded from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (includes wear parts and flux-cored wires used internally); new Nagpur shop floor coming live in phases since Q1.
New capacity expected to contribute from the next quarter, but management said ramp-up will take 2-3 years; electrode capacity started in Q4 FY26 with similar 2-3 year ramp.
About INR67 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised; management expects full utilisation by year-end, with savings to be redeployed subject to shareholder approval.
Units 1, 2 and 3 have no capacity change; utilisation there was described as 2-3% in one answer, while management said Units 1 and 3 operate at optimal levels.
demand_pricing: Finished steel production grew ~8.3% in April-June 2026 quarter; cement volume growth expected at 7-8% in FY27.

Named Q1 orders: INR9.88 crore VRM/separator parts (cement), INR8.16 crore roller-press rolls, INR10.63 crore roller assemblies, INR7.49 crore flux-cored wire (defence), INR26.31 crore RAPH rotor assembly (power); aggregate ~INR62.47 crore.
Raw material costs: steel up ~20%, some ferro-alloys like tungsten up several hundred percent; management said gross margin compressed by ~1-1.5% and customers have accepted higher prices.
Heavy engineering payment terms: 10-20% advance, 70-80% post-dispatch, balance after warranty documentation.
Top 10 customer concentration not disclosed on call; management said 60-70% expected, to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers across consumables, wear parts, heavy engineering and trading; domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was 30%+ across the three segments, driven by a higher starting order book. Growth was mainly domestic because Q1 FY26 had large export orders that did not repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material volatility and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices remain high but volatility has eased and customers have accepted higher prices. Gross margin contraction was about 1-1.5%, with steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys up several hundred percent.

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% is executable in FY27, and customers have asked to prepone some deliveries scheduled for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical run-rate is INR1-2 crore per quarter, so management expects INR1-2 crore going forward and treats the rest of the Q1 amount as a one-off extra.

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~20% growth in FY27-28 and an aim to double in three years, with EBITDA margin up 100-200 bps over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

Margin recovery depends on new capacity ramp: management says new heavy engineering and electrode capacity will take 2-3 years to ramp, and new capacity contributes little EBITDA in the near term.
